summary: 2026 年 10 月 29 日星期四，领导人在莫斯科举行的俄罗斯-非洲峰会期间合影留念。（Anastasia Barashkova//美联社泳池照片）|图片联盟/Anastasia Barashkova/Pool 路透社来自美联社 |阿纳斯塔西娅·巴拉什科娃 (Anastasia Barashkova) 十月下旬，非洲领导人抵达莫斯科，参加第三次俄罗斯-非洲峰会以及看似无休无止的外交会议。传达的信息很明确：俄罗斯希望恢复与非洲的接触。克里姆林宫试图将俄罗斯描绘成一个重返非洲大陆的全球大国，继承了苏联支持非洲反殖民主义的遗产。
content:
2026 年 10 月 29 日星期四，领导人在莫斯科举行的俄罗斯-非洲峰会期间合影留念。（Anastasia Barashkova//美联社泳池照片）|图片联盟/Anastasia Barashkova/Pool 路透社来自美联社 |阿纳斯塔西娅·巴拉什科娃 (Anastasia Barashkova) 十月下旬，非洲领导人抵达莫斯科，参加第三次俄罗斯-非洲峰会以及看似无休无止的外交会议。传达的信息很明确：俄罗斯希望恢复与非洲的接触。克里姆林宫试图将俄罗斯描绘成一个重返非洲大陆的全球大国，继承了苏联支持非洲反殖民运动的遗产。在 11 月 19 日与习近平和唐纳德·特朗普会面之前，弗拉基米尔·普京还利用这次峰会推进了另一个地缘政治野心：让俄罗斯拥有与苏联曾经享有的相同的全球地位。普京正在寻找一个“新雅尔塔”，在这个新雅尔塔中，他可以以斯大林的角色与另外两个大国就势力范围进行讨价还价。俄罗斯接待非洲领导人，普京在最近的公开露面中看似不经意地提及苏联在国际关系中的作用，以及他的大规模宣传工作，都反映出总统试图将自己描绘成一位有权重新绘制世界政治版图的政治家。然而，尽管莫斯科声称自己具有独特性，但“非洲+1”峰会却是司空见惯的。
欧洲各国政府以及亚洲和中东地区的其他大国经常召开类似的集会来讨好非洲大陆。为了加强其在非洲的地位，欧洲人应该更加直言不讳地表达自己的利益，并为非洲国家提供俄罗斯以外的替代方案。莫斯科扩大其非洲官僚机构 2023 年举行的第二次俄罗斯-非洲峰会因给非洲带来的好处甚少而受到批评。普京的回应是责成众多俄罗斯政府机构和国家支持的行动者与非洲建立更牢固的关系。到 2026 年，这些努力除其他外，已召开了两次部长级会议，旨在加强政府机构之间的联系；在外交部设立新的非洲伙伴关系司；以及统一俄罗斯党的“为了民族自由！”运动和议会倡议将俄罗斯和非洲政党纳入更广泛的反殖民网络。克里姆林宫还举办青年聚会和媒体论坛，以宣传俄罗斯对全球秩序的看法。这些举措与俄罗斯在非洲的军事存在并存，后者仍然是俄罗斯在非洲大陆最重要的影响力来源。然而，乌克兰战争暴露了莫斯科经济和金融资源的局限性。尽管非洲国家正在根据国家发展目标实现伙伴关系多元化，但普京未能实现他在 2019 年设定的五年内与非洲贸易额翻番至 400 亿美元左右的目标。
他现在的目标是到 2030 年达到 500 亿美元。到 2025 年，俄罗斯与非洲的货物贸易总额将达到 270 亿美元，大致相当于其与哈萨克斯坦的贸易额，而欧盟与非洲的货物贸易额则达到 3560 亿欧元。而且，俄罗斯占非洲外国直接投资存量的不到1%，远远落后于中国、美国和欧盟。农业提供了更多有形收益。 2026年上半年，俄罗斯对非洲的农产品出口额达到29亿美元，比2025年同期增长35%。然而，俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争正在扰乱乌克兰的粮食出口。这与寻求可靠供应返回的非洲政府产生了摩擦

【原文 English Original】
Leaders pose for a family photo during the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Anastasia Barashkova//Pool Photo via AP) | picture alliance / Anastasia Barashkova/Pool Reuters via AP | Anastasia Barashkova In late October, African leaders arrived in Moscow for the third Russia-Africa summit and a seemingly endless procession of diplomatic meetings. The message was clear: Russia wants to renew its engagement with Africa. The Kremlin seeks to portray Russia as a global power returning to the African continent, carrying the Soviet legacy of support for Africa’s anti-colonial movements. Vladimir Putin also used the summit to advance another geopolitical ambition ahead of the November 19th meeting with Xi Jinping and Donald Trump: for Russia to have the same global standing once enjoyed by the Soviet Union. Putin is searching for a “new Yalta” in which he, in Stalin’s role, can bargain with two other great powers over spheres of influence. Russia’s hosting of African leaders and Putin’s seemingly offhand references to the Soviet Union’s role in international relations during recent public appearances, as well as his massive publicity efforts , reflect the president’s attempt to portray himself as a statesman with the authority to redraw the world’s political map. For all Moscow’s claims of uniqueness , however, “Africa+1” summits are commonplace. European governments and other powers across Asia and the Middle East often convene similar gatherings to court the continent. To strengthen their standing in Africa, Europeans should be more vocal about their interests and offer African countries an alternative to Russia. Moscow expands its Africa bureaucracy The second Russia-Africa summit in 2023 drew criticism for delivering little benefit to Africa. Putin responded by tasking numerous Russian government agencies and state-backed actors to build stronger ties with Africa. By 2026 these efforts had amounted, among other things, to two ministerial conferences that aimed to strengthen ties between government agencies; the establishment of a new Department for Partnership with Africa in the foreign ministry; and United Russia’s “ For the Freedom of Nations!” movement and parliamentary initiatives to bring Russian and African parties into a wider anti-colonial network. The Kremlin also hosted youth gatherings and media forums to promote Russia’s view of the global order . These initiatives sit alongside Russia’s military presence in Africa, which remains its most consequential source of influence on the continent. However, the war in Ukraine has exposed the limits of Moscow’s economic and financial resources. While African countries are diversifying their partnerships based on national development objectives, Putin missed the target he set in 2019 to double trade with Africa to around $40bn in five years. He is now aiming for $50bn by 2030. Russia’s goods trade with Africa totalled $27bn in 2025, roughly matching its trade with Kazakhstan , while EU-Africa goods trade reached €356bn . Moreover, Russia accounts for less than 1% of Africa’s inward foreign direct investment stock, far behind China, the US and the EU . Agriculture offers more tangible gains. Russian agricultural exports to Africa reached $2.9bn in the first half of 2026, up 35% in value on the same period in 2025. However, Russia’s war in Ukraine is disrupting Ukrainian grain exports. This creates friction with African governments seeking the return of reliable supplies via the Black Sea. From trade to sovereignty Moscow has limited prospects of competing economically on the African continent. It is therefore increasingly framing partnerships with African countries ideologically while simultaneously pursuing more pragmatic cooperation in selected sectors, such as technology and agriculture. Putin’s speeches, final declarations and business programmes at the 2019, 2023 and 2026 Russia-Africa summits demonstrate this attempt. Putin’s references to military security and terrorism fell even more sharply in his speeches and almost halved in the final declarations. By 2026, references to sovereignty had gained prominence in both programmes and declarations, highlighting the core of Russia’s Africa strategy and tapping into existing anti- French and European sentiment , especially in West Africa. Putin is also placing greater emphasis on colonialism and multipolarity, grounding Russia’s claim to relevance in its vision of a multipolar world , of which the Kremlin is a champion. Russia is also drawing institutions such as universities and media organisations into its Africa policy, tasking them with facilitating cultural cooperation between Russia and Africa. Such organisations can form part of Russia’s wider disinformation campaigns. Between 2019 and 2026, Putin’s speeches nearly doubled their references to education and the Russian language, while the business programmes used them almost twice as often. The use of information-related terms, such as “media” and “informational agenda”, also more than doubled, largely through new media-forum sessions bringing together Russian and African journalists and media executives as a separate part of the third summit. Russia’s more selective and pragmatic agenda also includes energy, which regained prominence in the programmes and declarations between 2023 and 2026, drawing on Russia’s expertise in nuclear power . And, as part of Russia’s drive for pragmatic cooperation, the country also pursues seemingly uncontroversial themes such as its 2026 declaration on civilian AI . However, this offers African partners little immediate help. Many have more pressing industrial and economic needs. Pendulum partnership African governments choose partners pragmatically, based on their ability to deliver socio-economic growth, industrialisation and job creation Moscow’s bureaucratic expansion and stronger ideological approach are struggling to resonate with its potential partners in Africa. African governments choose partners pragmatically, based on their ability to deliver socio-economic growth, industrialisation and job creation. Even so, most of Moscow’s core partnerships in Africa continue to rest on security cooperation. For example, Russia has deployed forces in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger, and in the Central African Republic (CAR), Libya and Equatorial Guinea. It has also formalised defence cooperation with Togo and continues to pursue a military base in Sudan. The share of African speakers from these eight states at the three Russia-Africa summits rose from 5% in 2019 to 23% in 2026. Speakers from Russia’s BRICS+ partners, Egypt and Ethiopia, brought this up to 30% in 2026. Elsewhere, some African countries’ ties with Moscow fluctuate depending on changes of government and their renewed attempts to diversify partnerships. Ghana’s president John Mahama led his country’s 2026 summit delegation, which saw six Ghanaian speakers in the business programme. Russia and Ghana also reached an agreement on bauxite mining and alumina refining, and Russia has committed to help develop Ghana’s first nuclear power plant. Yet, despite Mahama’s ties to Russia (he studied in the Soviet Union), the speech data show that Ghana retains a pragmatic approach. Mahama’s renewed engagement with Russia perhaps reflects a search for partnerships that best serve Ghana’s national interests. Putin used ideological vocabulary more than twice as often in 2026 as in 2019, while his use of economic terms remained largely static. Among Moscow’s security partners, ideological language held roughly steady between 2023 and 2026, while references to trade, energy and investment doubled. Egypt’s emphasis changed little. President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi used ideological terms as often as Putin in 2019, but by 2026 Putin used them 75% more often than Sisi. African leaders outside the core group of eight security partners plus Egypt and Ethiopia used ideological terms 25% less frequently between 2023 and 2026, while the use of pragmatic vocabulary rose by more than a third. Some countries are scaling back their cooperation with Russia amid limited economic returns and tensions over the war in Ukraine. For example, in 2026, South Africa sent its foreign ministry’s director-general and Nigeria a junior foreign minister , replacing the presidents who attended in 2019. Their business programme speaker counts fell from 14 to five and from seven to three, respectively. An opening for Europe Insights from confidential conversations between ECFR’s Africa programme and African policymakers suggest that the continent’s governments and leaders appreciate a more pragmatic approach from European partners. This involves Europeans acknowledging the legacy of European colonialism in Africa, but also realising that in a fragmented global order Africa has options to choose from. Europe would benefit from identifying where Russian political actors are working at cross-purposes and leveraging this fragmentation in diplomatic negotiations with African partners. For example, the former Wagner chief Yevgeny Prigozhin welcomed the Niger coup in 2023, while Russia’s foreign ministry backed ECOWAS in restoring constitutional order. In the CAR, his son Pavel Prigozhin has held on to Wagner’s operations despite the Russian defence ministry’s efforts to absorb them. As Moscow gives its bureaucratic players a bigger role in Africa, such tensions are likely to grow. The Russia-Africa Action Plan for 2027-2029 contains 236 measures, including joint drone, fertiliser and vaccine production, and cooperation between the African Union and the Russia-led Collective Security Treaty Organisation. But these priorities, and Russia’s bilateral agreements with African countries, can undermine one another: Rosatom requires deep cooperation with Accra to develop the planned nuclear power plant in Ghana, for example, but Russia’s coercive recruitment of Ghanaians for its war against Ukraine risks eroding bilateral trust. Even Mahama, who praised Moscow’s support for Africa’s anti-colonial struggles, has challenged Putin over the practice . Where Moscow’s competing interests undermine its summit promises, Europe can build trust by backing projects that African partners themselves prioritise. An example is the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), for which the EU provided technical and financial support. Despite facing some difficulties, the AfCFTA highlights where European and African strategic interests align—and where Europeans can help Africans reach their objectives, without setting the terms. Europeans also need to understand that, for African partners, pursuing a narrative in which Europe “counters” other actors such as Russia may not land well. Although Africa has considerable growth and market potential, the continent does not want to be approached as an international bargaining field. European governments should instead sharpen their own offer and advance investments in areas such as education and training, technology and engineering. Forums such as the AU-EU Senior Officials Meeting in Addis Ababa are essential for Europe to stay aligned with African priorities, while the participation of high-level European leaders, such as German president Frank-Walter Steinmeier at the upcoming German-African Business Summit in Ghana, signals how seriously they take cooperation. * African partners are not going to wait for European countries to take more responsibility in their approach to economic and trade negotiations. Europeans must ground any partnerships with African countries in reliability—a quality that Russian cooperation has yet to achieve. Both Europe and Africa share a strong belief in multilateralism, political dialogue and collective action. This dialogue, if transformed into a pragmatic, well-coordinated approach , would set Europeans apart from the transactional and extractive approaches of other global players. Source

title: Anatomy of a Chinese loanbook
zh_title: 中国贷款簿剖析
source: 国际调查记者联盟 - ICIJ
summary: ICIJ 的中国资本调查揭露了全球最大银行中国工商银行 (ICBC) 的伦敦分行如何例行公事地为企业提供资金以推动北京的地缘政治议程，有时甚至在此过程中藐视自己的合规规则。 ICIJ 与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，获得了工银伦敦泄露的 480 万份内部文件，包括贷款申请表、尽职调查报告、了解你的客户文件和内部电子邮件往来。为了更好地了解工行伦敦业务，ICIJ 数据团队剖析了 200 多个贷款机构
content:
ICIJ 的中国资本调查揭露了全球最大银行中国工商银行 (ICBC) 的伦敦分行如何例行公事地为企业提供资金以推动北京的地缘政治议程，有时甚至在此过程中藐视自己的合规规则。 ICIJ 与 23 家媒体合作伙伴合作，获得了工银伦敦泄露的 480 万份内部文件，包括贷款申请表、尽职调查报告、了解你的客户文件和内部电子邮件往来。为了更好地了解工行伦敦业务，ICIJ数据团队剖析了2010年至2024年期间的200多份贷款协议和修正案。ICIJ发现，在审查的协议和修正案中，工银伦敦至少与另一家中国国有商业银行合作。在中国的银行中，中国银行脱颖而出，成为工银伦敦分行的主要中方合作伙伴：双方签署了 102 项协议。 ICIJ 的分析显示，这家中国银行业巨头的伦敦分行通常与其他中国和国际银行合作，达成价值数亿美元甚至更多的贷款协议。 ICIJ 发现了 36 项贷款协议和修正案，其中一半或以上的资金是由中国贷方提供的。其中 16 个案例的财务承诺完全来自中资银行。
ICIJ 的一项审查发现，作为对该行客户尽职调查过程的一部分，中国工商银行准备的文件显示，该行有时会淡化合规问题，或以其他方式证明继续与其被归类为高风险的客户开展业务是合理的。 在赞比亚，中国工商银行在加剧该国债务负担、造成对中国贷款的依赖以及给赞比亚人造成多年困难方面发挥了作用。在英国，中国工商银行的银行管理人员无视其一位中国客户在美国法院面临的法律风险，以便该银行能够为该公司收购英国竞争对手并巩固其市场份额提供资金。下面的案例研究揭示了一家银行在中国党国议程的推进与其自身的全球商业野心之间取得平衡的内部运作方式。无视红灯 01 2024年5月，工商银行的高风险客户名单包括全球燃料贸易商和分销商Puma Energy的融资部门以及大股东Trafigura Pte.有限公司是一家注册并总部位于新加坡的贸易巨头，主要贸易业务位于瑞士，以及另外两家托克实体。尽管中国工商银行对 Puma 和 Trafigura 的担忧至少可以追溯到 2015 年，但 ICIJ 发现 2015 年至 2024 年间涉及 Puma 和 Trafigura 的 19 项银团信贷安排协议，总价值达 387 亿美元。 ICBC 的伦敦实体在这些贷款中总共承诺提供 14 亿美元。
2015年，工商银行加大了对Puma旗下融资工具Puma International Financing的尽职调查力度；在其2015年5月的强化尽职调查（EDD）报告中，将该公司的贿赂风险评为“高”。 当时，Puma的股东包括安哥拉国有石油公司Sonangol和Cochan Holdings LLC（一家由安哥拉总统顾问Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento创立并担任主席的投资公司）。该报告承认，媒体广泛报道了涉及安哥拉高级官员的贿赂和腐败行为，其中包括当时的总统若泽·爱德华多·多斯桑托斯及其子女，以及Sonangol、Cochan和Nascimento。尽管如此，工行仍对大部分逆回购进行了描述

【原文 English Original】
ICIJ’s China Capital investigation revealed how the London units of the world’s largest bank, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), routinely financed companies to push Beijing’s geopolitical agenda, sometimes flouting their own compliance rules in the process. ICIJ, in collaboration with 23 media partners, obtained 4.8 million internal documents leaked from ICBC London, including loan application forms, due diligence reports, know-your-client documents and internal email exchanges. To better understand ICBC’s London operations, the ICIJ data team dissected more than 200 loan agreements and amendments dated from 2010 to 2024. ICIJ found that ICBC London partnered with at least one other Chinese state-owned commercial bank in more than half of the agreements and amendments reviewed. Among the Chinese lenders, Bank of China stands out as the main Chinese partner of ICBC London: They joined forces in 102 agreements. ICIJ’s analysis shows that the London units of the Chinese banking giant usually partnered with other Chinese and international banks on loan agreements often worth hundreds of millions of dollars—or more. ICIJ identified 36 loan agreements and amendments for which half or more of the money was provided by Chinese lenders. In 16 of those cases, the financial commitments were entirely from Chinese banks. ICBC documents prepared as part of the due diligence process on the bank’s clients show how the bank at times downplayed compliance problems or otherwise justified continued business with clients it had classified as high risk, an ICIJ review found. In Zambia, ICBC played a role in exacerbating the country’s debt burden, creating dependency on Chinese loans and contributing to years-long difficulties for Zambians. In the U.K., ICBC bank officers disregarded legal risks faced in a U.S. court by one of their Chinese clients so the bank could finance the company’s acquisition of a British competitor and consolidate its market share. The case studies below reveal the inner workings of a bank balancing the advancement of the agenda of the Chinese party-state with its own global commercial ambitions. Ignoring Red Lights 01 In May 2024, ICBC’s high-risk client list included the financing arm of global fuel trader and distributor Puma Energy, along with a major shareholder Trafigura Pte. Ltd., a trading giant registered and headquartered in Singapore with major trading operations in Switzerland, and two other Trafigura entities. Despite ICBC's concerns about Puma and Trafigura dating back to at least 2015, ICIJ identified 19 syndicated credit facility agreements involving Puma and Trafigura, between 2015 and 2024, with a combined value of $38.7 billion. ICBC's London entities committed a total of $1.4 billion across those facilities. In 2015, ICBC escalated its due diligence of Puma’s financing vehicle, Puma International Financing; in its May 2015 Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) report, it rated the company’s bribery risk as high. At the time, Puma's shareholders included Angola's state-owned oil company Sonangol and Cochan Holdings LLC, an investment company founded and chaired by Angolan presidential adviser Leopoldino Fragoso do Nascimento. The report acknowledged extensive adverse media coverage alleging bribery and corruption involving senior Angolan officials, including then-President José Eduardo dos Santos and his children, as well as Sonangol, Cochan and Nascimento. Still, ICBC characterized much of the adverse reporting as “rumour based and unfounded” and continued the relationship, subject to enhanced monitoring. In February 2020, ICBC’s EDD report again identified allegations centered on Nascimento’s close ties to former President dos Santos and speculation in media reports and elsewhere that he had used political connections to acquire a stake in Puma Energy while serving as a public official. The report also noted that Nascimento had faced investigations into alleged corruption, conflicts of interest and money laundering in several countries. Yet ICBC cited reasons for discounting the risks, noting that Nascimento did “not appear to have been convicted” of wrongdoing. In December 2021, the U.S. Treasury sanctioned Nascimento and Cochan, saying Nascimento and another Angolan official had embezzled billions from the Angolan government. In 2025, an Angolan court convicted Nascimento of fraud, document forgery, money laundering and influence peddling. Likewise, ICBC's October 2019 Enhanced Due Diligence report came after a highly public Brazilian corruption investigation into allegations that commodity traders, including Trafigura, had bribed employees of Petrobras, Brazil’s state-owned and state-controlled oil company. A month earlier, Reuters reported allegations that senior Trafigura executives Mike Wainwright and José Larocca knew about the bribes. But ICBC's EDD report referred only to "two high-ranking executives” at Trafigura, without identifying them, despite separately listing both men as key controllers of Trafigura. Wainwright's adverse-media assessment was marked "No." ICBC continued the relationship, citing Trafigura's status as a longstanding "strategic client," the participation of major international banks in syndicated loans, its compliance controls and the absence of suspicious activity detected by ICBC. In 2024, Trafigura Beheer B.V., the Dutch-registered former parent company of the Trafigura Group, pleaded guilty in the U.S. to conspiring to violate U.S. anti-bribery laws in a scheme that ran from approximately 2003 to 2014. The companies also reached a settlement agreement with Brazilian authorities. Read responses Responses Trafigura: In response to ICIJ's questions, a Trafigura spokesperson said lender due diligence was a normal part of doing business and that the company cooperated with lenders' reviews, supported by its public financial and sustainability disclosures. Regarding the Petrobras bribery case, the spokesperson referred to Trafigura's 2024 statement announcing the resolution of the U.S. investigation, in which the company said the misconduct involved former employees or agents and was inconsistent with its principles and code of conduct. The statement said U.S. authorities had recognized improvements to Trafigura's anti-corruption compliance procedures. Puma: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Nascimento: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Angolan government: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Cochan: ICIJ could not successfully contact Cochan for comment. Sonangol: Didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. A legal representative for Mike Wainwright didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. José Larocca: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: Didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Puma International Financing S.A., Trafigura Group Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Pte. Ltd., Trafigura Trading LLC Amount $1.4 billionTotal loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2024 From the China Capital files PUMA In their own words: There is a wealth of adverse news in the public domain citing the Angolan Government's bribery and corruption and monopolisation of various industries in Angola.Risk From the China Capital files TRAFIGURA In their own words: The risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened [...] and thus this poses an increased reputational risk to the Bank.Risk Trafigura is an existing and strategic client of the Bank.Mitigating factors Financing Kleptocrats 02 ICBC started lending to Socar, Azerbaijan’s state oil and gas concern, in 2015 when ICBC London took part in a revolving credit facility to one of the company’s subsidiaries, Socar Trading SA. Even though the bank decided to exit this facility in 2019 because of the company's “underperformance and ongoing restructuring," a review of ICBC documents shows that under the head office’s encouragement, ICBC’s London and Turkey offices maintained close connection with Socar. Bank officers in an internal memo noted “Azerbaijan's geopolitical importance in the area's political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors,” adding “SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China's 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy." ICBC London committed to at least three additional loans, each between $25 million and $89 million, even as the bank continued to list Socar among high-risk clients, with one document stating: “the risks of money laundering, sanctions and bribery and corruption are heightened." Corporate bank officers underlined the risks presented by the nature of Socar’s business and its jurisdiction, Azerbaijan; the fact that all the members of its board of directors were, at the time, identified as politically exposed persons, including the president and 12 vice presidents; Socar’s lack of transparency and accountability; and that the company had recently featured in major international corruption scandals. Yet the same year that ICBC listed these risks, 2021, the bank agreed to lend Socar $89 million. ICBC and Socar had deepened their ties in 2018, when the bank’s London branch listed $1.58 billion worth of green bonds on the London Stock Exchange, and Azerbaijan's State Oil Fund, SOFAZ, decided to invest $150 million. Socar, which sells oil and gas on the state’s behalf, contributed about 90% of SOFAZ’s 2017 revenue. The Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project later reported that leaked documents from inside British Petroleum exposed that two Socar subsidiaries were set to siphon off more than $1.7 billion from the Shah Deniz 2 gas project through padded contracts and fake charges. Socar denied the allegations. Read response Response Socar: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. SOFAZ: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrower Socar and its subsidiaries Amount $217 million (4 loans)Total loan commitments Start dates of loans 2015-2021 From the China Capital files In their own words: Given Azerbaijan’s geopolitical importance in the area’s political and economic landscape, and its longstanding partnership with super oil majors, SOCAR is a strategically important client for ICBC in view of supporting China’s 2013 One-Belt One-Road policy aimed at creating infrastructure and establishing links among the Eurasian countries.Risk Consolidating Market Share 03 ICBC records show bank risk management officials looking past the potentially illegal actions of a Chinese customer seeking a loan to buy out one of its competitors. In 2017 ICBC London Branch agreed to back China’s Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.’s acquisition of Sepura PLC, a British telecommunications competitor in the mobile radio communications sector. Hytera designs and manufactures professional mobile communications devices commonly used by law enforcement agencies worldwide — including two-way radios, a market that at the time was expected to be worth $7.3 billion by 2025. The agreement with ICBC London, which was the only lender involved, allowed Hytera to borrow up to $57.1 million over three years. Sepura shareholders had approved the $92.7 million acquisition in January 2017 but antitrust authorities in the UK and Germany, where governments relied on Sepura’s technology, stalled the acquisition. Spanish antitrust authorities also assessed the transaction, which was eventually approved in May of that year. While conducting their due diligence work to approve the loan in early 2017, ICBC London employees discovered that Motorola Solutions Inc., another competitor in the mobile telecommunications market, had filed a lawsuit pending against Hytera in a U.S. federal court for alleged patent infringement and industrial espionage. The bank’s compliance officers allowed the loan to go forward anyway, adding a handwritten note on a printout of an article about the suit that the case wasn’t related to any major financial crime. The article mentioned, however, that Motorola accused Hytera of hiring ex-Motorola employees after they had allegedly stolen thousands of pages of confidential documents. By early 2020, while Hytera was repaying the loan ICBC employees flagged a problem — Hytera had lost its U.S. case. In a briefing note to the bank’s credit committee at the end of April, they wrote that the verdict “confirms that Hytera engaged in illegal trade secret theft and copyright infringement, validating Motorola's global litigation against Hytera.” Following the U.S. court verdict ICBC London received an injunction from a British court ordering the bank to freeze Hytera assets, potentially stopping the repayment of the loan. Seven Hytera employees were later indicted for their alleged roles in the thefts from Motorola; one pleaded guilty in 2022 to charges of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and is awaiting sentencing. Hytera pleaded guilty in 2025 to “conspiracy to steal trade secrets” and was fined $50 million. Hytera was also ordered to pay Motorola more than $400 million in a separate lawsuit. In 2021, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission published a list of Chinese manufacturers, including Hytera, which “pose an unacceptable risk to the national security of the United States.” The same year, the British government passed the National Security and Investment Act which gave heightened power to the government to proactively review acquisitions in 17 sensitive sectors, including communications. Hytera sold its entire shareholding in Sepura in July 2022. Read responses Responses Hytera: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In an email to ICIJ, Sepura said that "neither Sepura PLC nor its shareholders or management at the time were involved in Hytera’s choice of funding for its acquisition of Sepura” and that the company “had no customer relationship with ICBC and held no accounts with the bank” following the acquisition. It also said that it was not “a party to the litigation brought by Motorola against Hytera concerning Motorola’s intellectual property” and that “the technology at issue was distinct from that developed and used by Sepura in its own products”. “Sepura's proprietary technology and IPR were ring-fenced by statutory undertakings, as mandated and defined by the UK government and accepted by Hytera.” Sepura said it “has had no further interaction with Hytera since the sale” in 2022. ICBC:didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Borrower Project Shortway Ltd. (ultimately owned by Hytera Communications Corp. Ltd.) Amount up to $57.1 millionTotal loan commitments Start date of loans May 2017 From the China Capital files In their own words Handwritten note on an article: Not major financial crime issues relatedRisk Buying your backyard 04 ICBC participated in syndicated loans — financing provided by a group of lenders who share the risk — for a Chinese commercial real estate venture that went bust and defaulted on its loans, according to internal loan agreements and property assessments reviewed by ICIJ. In 2017, Chinese real estate tycoon Chen Hongtian and his wife bought two office towers in London’s trendy Canary Wharf commercial district, hoping to convert their $900 million investment into a profitable venture. ICBC London described the area as “one of the world’s premier commercial districts,” with “24 office buildings with around 200 shops, bars, and restaurants” according to a 2022 assessment of 5 Churchill Place’s value by the real estate company managing the asset. The real estate firm’s assessment came as the bank and other creditors looked to liquidate the assets of the embattled tycoon who had found himself short on cash and unable to make payments. By then, ICBC London Branch had committed $205 million out of roughly half a billion in loans made with other banks to Chen’s companies in the British Virgin Islands, through which he and his family owned the London properties. One of those properties, at 20 Canada Square, was mainly occupied by two Western firms, according to a 2022 ICBC internal credit report. But the properties couldn’t compete with more modern and energy-efficient real estate, and their value plummeted. By April 2023 ICBC London had reclassified the loan to Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., a BVI company through which Chen owned some units of the Canada Square property, as “non performing” and added the borrower to its watchlist. Around the same time that ICBC was reviewing the properties, the UK government passed the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act which required overseas entities that hold property in England and Wales to file beneficial ownership information with the company registry. A report published in 2017 by the U.S. Government Accountability Office warned that leasing space in foreign-owned buildings "could present security risks such as espionage and unauthorized cyber and physical access.” The UK’s National Security and Investment Act took effect in January 2022, but real estate was not among the sensitive sectors subject to its mandatory screening requirements for acquisitions. Read responses Responses Chen Hongtian/Cheung Kei group: The Cheung Kei group didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. In statement posted on its website in 2023 the group said that “like all heavy asset holders”, it was “experiencing a phase of cash problems” and that its “overall asset scale and asset quality” were “very high, with a low debt ratio among peers.” At the time the group was “selling some equity in some assets and actively negotiating repayment arrangements with relevant financial institutions” and said it “believed that subsequent financial institution issues will be properly resolved.” ICBC London: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrowers Jovial Link Holdings Ltd. for 5 Churchill Place; Cheung Pang Holdings Ltd., Cheung Kwan Holdings Ltd. for 20 Canada Square (London properties) Start dates of loans 2022 Amount $61.7M / $143.5MTotal loan commitments From the China Capital files In their own words: About 5 Churchill Place, from a credit loan application: The deal as outlined herein offers ICBC London an ideal opportunity to assist an incoming Chinese client in the purchase of a major “trophy” asset that is both well let to tenants of significant covenant strengths and well located within the popular Canary Wharf developmentRisk Trapping In Debt 05 ICBC records on Zambia show a lender watching a borrower facing growing financial risks, while quietly putting protections in place for its own loans. ICBC financed a range of major projects in the country, providing loans for government-owned housing, a hospital, an airport and power projects running to hundreds of millions of dollars. Among them was a $285 million loan approved in 2010 to ZESCO, Zambia's state-owned power company, for two power transmission projects. Between 2015 and 2018, ICBC provided or participated in at least six more loans to ZESCO, totaling $1.2 billion according to AidData estimates, even as the bank was aware of mounting financial pressures on both Zambia and ZESCO. By 2017, a sovereign risk assessment in the bank's files described Zambia as facing limited financing options, rising interest costs, and substantial debt—and specifically pointed to financial pressures on ZESCO. Government net debt had climbed from 23% of GDP in 2013 to an estimated 57% in 2017, while debt costs consumed nearly a quarter of government revenue. ICBC had classified ZESCO as a high-risk client since 2018, citing Zambia's country risk, politically exposed persons and historical adverse media coverage including bribery and corruption allegations, according to a 2023 internal report. Despite these concerns, the bank continued its lending relationship with ZESCO, requiring annual reviews. ICBC built protections into its lending. ZESCO maintained a debt-service reserve account at ICBC London for repayments on the $285 million loan. Money deposited into the account could only be withdrawn by ICBC's head office, which was also the lender, agent and security trustee. ZESCO’s financial precarity triggered a cascade of credit problems. By March 2020, its failure to pay Maamba Collieries Ltd., a Zambian power supplier, had left Maamba unable to meet its own loan obligations to ICBC and other lenders. ICBC records show that lenders sent letters to Zambia's Ministry of Finance seeking government support, contacted Chinese state-owned insurer Sinosure and discussed restructuring the loan. ICBC officials warned that Maamba's loan would be classified as non-performing if payments remained overdue for more than 90 days. The documents offer a window into how the bank continued banking a financially strained borrower while using safeguards to limit its own losses. Read responses Responses ZESCO: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Zambian MOF: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. ICBC: didn’t respond to ICIJ’s request for comment. Main borrower ZESCO Amount $285 millionTotal loan commitments Start date of loans May 2011 From the China Capital files In their own words: The lenders have jointly sent two letters to Ministry of Finance (MOF), emphasizing the continuing non-payment by the ZESCO which may lead to Borrower’s default on the repayment of principal and interest, to seek support from MOF to solve this issue…Risk Contributors: Micael Pereira (Expresso); Scilla Alecci, Miguel Fiandor-Gutiérrez, Micah Reddy, Dean Starkman, Antonio Cucho Gamboa (ICIJ)

title: Compact and Covert
zh_title: 紧凑、隐蔽
summary: 法国土伦——法国海军的潜艇码头位于巴黎最大海军基地的有顶干船坞内和厚厚的混凝土墙后面。这个戒备森严的设施是核攻击潜艇中队最强大、最现代化的攻击艇的所在地，不被窥探。上个月，USNI News 参观了法国海军的一艘 Suffren 级核攻击潜艇 FS Duguay-Trouin (S636)，当时该潜艇正在进行维护。这艘核攻击潜艇于 2023 年服役，是法国海军 Suffren 级的第二艘，将成为法国海军的支柱。
content:
法国土伦——法国海军的潜艇码头位于巴黎最大海军基地的有顶干船坞内和厚厚的混凝土墙后面。这个戒备森严的设施是核攻击潜艇中队最强大、最现代化的攻击艇的所在地，不被窥探。上个月，USNI News 参观了法国海军的一艘 Suffren 级核攻击潜艇 FS Duguay-Trouin (S636)，当时该潜艇正在进行维护。这艘核攻击潜艇于 2023 年服役，是法国海军 Suffren 级的第二艘核潜艇，将成为未来几十年法国水下战争的支柱。 “对我们来说，冷战从未真正结束，”一位退役的法国海军潜艇指挥官在参观期间谈到他从 20 世纪 90 年代到 2010 年代的服役时光时说道。法国与北大西洋公约组织伙伴英国、德国和美国一起，一直在与俄罗斯海军进行水下对峙。从北大西洋的GIUK海峡到地中海沿岸，法国潜艇在日益恶化的安全局势中坚守岗位。随着俄罗斯对欧洲的威胁重新抬头，以及对法国在印度太平洋地区领土的新担忧，巴黎的攻击艇比以往任何时候都更加重要。这艘重 4,765 吨的潜艇停泊在有顶棚的干船坞内，让人们得以一睹法国海军旨在解决的能力和任务。
与现代中国、俄罗斯和美国的核攻击艇相比，紧凑型“苏弗伦”号的船员数量约为一半，排水量也显着减轻。紧凑型船员总数为 70 人，其中包括 15 名军官和 55 名士官，他们可以在鱼雷室后面的食堂享用面包店的新鲜法棍面包和配给的葡萄酒。 Duguay-Trouin 号的高度自动化特性可以从其武器舱中看出，攻击艇的执行官声称武器舱可由两名男子操作。与上一代红宝石级潜艇相比，萨弗伦级潜艇现在可以发射远程巡航导弹打击，承载专门的特种部队行动，并支持欧洲战区以外的扩展部署。从捍卫威慑到新的常规任务 2026 年 10 月 7 日，一艘拥有 38 年船龄的 FS Améthyste (S605) 核攻击艇在倾盆大雨中驶入土伦海军基地。USNI 新闻照片 灰色的阴天被土伦湾的倾盆大雨所取代。雨中出现了一艘潜艇的轮廓，指挥塔上挤满了模糊的人影。小船护送缓慢移动的 FS Améthyste (S605) 进入海湾。这艘冷战时期的攻击艇是法国红宝石级的最后一艘，也是法国海军服役的苏弗伦级之前的第一艘核攻击潜艇。与 Duguay-Trouin 相比，Améthyste 的排水量仅为 2,400 吨，并且是为不同时代而设计的。
与当时的西方和东方同类潜艇相比，红宝石级潜艇在武器装备和排水量上都明显较轻。这种设计理念反映了法国海军最初涉足核攻击艇及其在北大西洋和地中海的作战重点区域。冷战期间，法国海军的前线潜艇部队依赖于十几艘达芙妮级和阿戈斯塔级柴电推进攻击艇。 2026 年 10 月 6 日，SNLE Le Vigilant 首次发射 51.3 导弹。DGA 照片 核心任务之一

【原文 English Original】
TOULON, France — The French Navy’s submarine quay resides within covered dry docks and behind thick concrete walls at Paris’ largest naval base. Concealed from prying eyes, this closely guarded facility is home to the Squadron of Nuclear Attack Submarines’ most capable and modern attack boats. Last month, USNI News visited one of the French Navy’s Suffren-class nuclear attack submarines, FS Duguay-Trouin (S636), while the boat was undergoing maintenance. Commissioned in 2023, the nuclear attack submarine is the second of the sea service’s Suffren class and will form the backbone of French undersea warfare in the coming decades. “For us, the Cold War never really ended,” a retired French Navy submarine commander remarked during the tour about his time serving from the 1990s to 2010s. France, alongside North Atlantic Treaty Organization partners Britain, Germany and the U.S., has been engaged in a constant underwater standoff against the Russian Navy. From the North Atlantic waters of GIUK gap to the littorals of the Mediterranean, French submarines have stood guard amid an increasingly deteriorating security situation. With the resurgence of Russian threats to Europe and new concerns regarding French possessions in the Indo-Pacific, Paris’ attack boats are more relevant than ever. Resting within a covered dry dock, the 4,765-ton submarine provided a glimpse at the capabilities and missions that the French Navy aims to address. Compared to modern Chinese, Russian and American nuclear attack boats, the compact Suffren’s have roughly half the crew and displace considerably less weight. The compact crew complement of 70 personnel, divided between 15 officers and 55 petty officers, can enjoy their fresh baguettes from the bakery and wine ration at the mess behind the torpedo room. Duguay-Trouin’s highly automated nature can be seen within its weapons bay, which the attack boat’s executive officer claimed can be operated by two men. Compared to the previous generation of Rubis-class boats, the Suffren class can now launch long-range cruise missile strikes, host dedicated special forces operations and support extended-deployments beyond the European theater. From Defending the Deterrent to New Conventional Missions The 38-year-old FS Améthyste (S605) nuclear attack boat pulls into Toulon Naval Base under a torrential downpour on Oct. 7, 2026. USNI News photo A gray overcast sky gave way to a torrential downpour across Toulon Bay. A submarine silhouette emerged from the rain with hazy figures crowding the conning tower. Small boats escorted the slow moving FS Améthyste (S605) into the bay. The Cold War-era attack boat is the last of France’s Rubis-class, which was also the first class of nuclear attack submarines in French Navy service before the Suffren class. In contrast to Duguay-Trouin , Améthyste displaced only 2,400-tons and was created for a different era. Compared to its Western and Eastern counterparts at the time, Rubis-class submarines were notably lighter in both armament and displacement. This design philosophy reflected the French Navy’s initial foray into nuclear attack boats and its operational focus areas in the North Atlantic and Mediterranean. During the Cold War, the French Navy’s frontline submarine force relied on more than a dozen diesel-electric propelled attack boats from the Daphné and Agosta classes. The first firing of a 51.3 missile from the SNLE Le Vigilant on Oct. 6, 2026. DGA photo One of the core missions for the Rubis, and now Suffren class, was the escort of the French sea-based nuclear deterrent. Today, the French Navy operates four Triomphant-class submarines, each equipped with 16 M51 submarine-launched ballistic missiles. Alongside air-launched supersonic missiles carried by French Air Force and Navy Rafale fighters, the submarines form the pillars of Paris’ nuclear deterrent. France previously operated a full nuclear triad, but decommissioned its ground-based silos in the 1990s. On the morning of USNI News’ tour of Duguay-Trouin , France held its first at-sea test of a SLBM from FS Le Vigilant (S618) in the Atlantic Ocean. A M51.3 missile soared over the Atlantic in an event presided over by President Emmanuel Macron on a nearby frigate. French defense, military and industry leadership repeatedly highlighted this capability as Europe’s “only sovereign deterrent.” Aside from defending the country’s SSBNs, the Suffren-class brings new capabilities for French undersea warfare. At the front of the attack boat within its highly automated weapons room, the Suffren-class can deploy France’s first-ever submarine-launched cruise missiles. The domestic Naval Cruise Missile program’s roots can be traced to Paris’ failed attempt to procure Tomahawk cruise missiles from the U.S. in the early 2000s. Since 2017, the domestic long-range cruise missiles have enabled French frigates and submarines to strike targets out to 1,000 to 1,400 kilometers. Duguay-Trouin launches the cruise missiles from its four 533mm torpedo tubes. While French Navy frigates debuted the Naval Cruise Missile in combat during a joint operation with the U.S. and U.K. in 2018 against Syrian chemical weapon facilities, a Suffren-class sub first fired the cruise missile in a 2020 test. The FREMM Aquitaine and an SSN simultaneously fired an MdCN missile, shared in April of 2024. French Navy photo The initial production run of the Naval Cruise Missile only assembled 200 munitions, of which only 50 could be fired from the Suffren-class boats. However, the French military announced a new order for the latest variant of the cruise missile earlier this month at Euronaval 2026. This procurement comes amid a new focus by the French military in long-range precision fires influenced by lessons in the Ukraine conflict. Beyond conventional deep strike potential, the submarines also bring a new deployment method for French Navy special forces and the service’s growing hybrid fleet concept. A complement of Commando Marines can deploy from the submarine while submerged via a dry deck shelter module that can be attached for certain missions. The Suffren-class boats can also support swimmer delivery vehicles for these clandestine operations. Within the command center, 10 multi-functional display consoles flank an elevated captain’s seat and central tactical planning table. Each of these displays can be configured for different roles, a capability that can be useful depending on the mission tasked to Duguay-Trouin . French government-controlled shipbuilder Naval Group hopes to use submarines from the Suffren class and their command and control capabilities to support drone mesh networks in a hybrid fleet concept. At a demonstration at a nearby Naval Group facility, the shipbuilder showcased the potential benefits of operating extra-large unmanned underwater vehicles and aerial drones from the same consoles seen aboard Duguay-Trouin . The French Navy has already experimented with the deployment of UUVs, including a Spring 2026 test that saw the launch and recovery of a U.S. Navy Razorback UUV. In contrast to the highly autonomous vision of unmanned systems integration by fleets aboard, France is taking a more conservative force enabler approach in its hybrid fleet concept. French defense and industry officials want their drones to extend the surveillance reach of their manned assets. During the demonstration, the concept helped a French submarine detect targets in the Red Sea to enable an enhanced picture for a commander.

title: Alice Huang’s Shady Shanghai Ties to Business and Government
zh_title: 艾丽丝·黄与上海商界和政府的不正当关系
summary: 内容摘要：黄仁勋间谍丑闻核心人物、Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 通过上海金融界建立了自己的商业网络。她与因财务不当行为而受到制裁的所谓丈夫康伟和后来涉嫌欺诈和贿赂的谷国平等人物有联系。报道称，美国情报部门认为她是中华人民共和国情报部门的合作伙伴。根据开源研究，目前尚不清楚 Alice Huang 在国家安全部 (MSS) 中的确切角色是什么
content:
内容摘要：黄仁勋间谍丑闻核心人物、Megaspeed 前高管 Alice Huang 通过上海金融界建立了自己的商业网络。她与因财务不当行为而受到制裁的所谓丈夫康伟和后来涉嫌欺诈和贿赂的谷国平等人物有联系。报道称，美国情报部门认为她是中华人民共和国情报部门的合作伙伴。根据开源研究，目前尚不清楚 Alice Huang 在国家安全部 (MSS) 中的确切角色是什么；然而，当她结识黄仁勋时，她的兴趣和事工的兴趣很可能是一致的。黄和康利用他们的游戏业务扩展到半导体和数据中心，并在此过程中成为 Nvidia 的客户。随后，黄仁勋接管了香港游戏公司第七大道在新加坡的国际子公司第七大道国际，并通过马来西亚子公司购买了英伟达芯片。美国当局怀疑这些芯片随后被转运到中国。皇康网络与中国地方政府建立了联系。持有顾国平旗下斐讯公司股份的上海松江区投资机构，在顾国平的犯罪活动导致斐讯公司倒闭后，将股份出售给其网络中的一家公司。
科技巨头英伟达 (Nvidia) 联合创始人兼首席执行官 (CEO) 黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 垮台的核心人物是一位名叫黄乐 (Huang Le) 的女性，又名 Alice Huang。媒体报道称，黄女士是英伟达在东南亚最大的客户之一、新加坡计算公司 Megaspeed 的前高管，她与黄仁勋有染。 Megaspeed 涉嫌将受美国出口管制限制的 Nvidia 芯片走私到中华人民共和国（PRC）。报道还称，美国情报部门认为黄女士已被中华人民共和国国家安全部 (MSS) 拉拢（《纽约时报》[NYT]，10 月 29 日；《华盛顿邮报》，11 月 15 日）。 [1] 北京很快否认了这些指控，但一些亲美人士认为中国的知识分子则更加持怀疑态度。他们认为当前的丑闻是特朗普政府内部以及特朗普与“深层政府”之间的内讧的结果（腾讯新闻；X/@Wuuesanren；X/@WoodenHarp，11月10日）。一位上海商人在接受采访时也表达了类似的观点，称黄女士的网络采用了复杂的、多层的公司结构来掩盖最终控制者是谁，并称这种策略是“上海滩从同治皇帝时候就玩的东西了”，指的是19世纪下半叶的早期现代化时期（作者访谈，11月10日）。他相信女士。
黄女士的目的只是将芯片走私到中国。黄出身于上海金融界，她与随后被判犯有金融犯罪的人物的关系表明，她的个人资料应该引起更多的危险信号。她的网络以一家投资公司上海和熙投资管理为中心，该公司是由她所谓的恋人、商人康伟创立的（英国《金融时报》，11 月 10 日）。该网络中的其他主要人物包括黄瑜，英国《金融时报》将其描述为黄女士的妹妹；顾国平

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Alice Huang, the former Megaspeed executive at the heart of the Jensen Huang spy scandal, built her business network through the world of Shanghai finance. She is linked to figures such as Kang Wei, her alleged husband who has been sanctioned for financial misconduct, and Gu Guoping, who was later implicated in fraud and bribery. Reporting indicates that U.S. intelligence considers her a cooptee of People’s Republic of China (PRC) intelligence services. It remains unclear what Alice Huang’s exact role was for the Ministry of State Security (MSS) based on open-source research; however, it is likely that her interests and that of the ministry converged around the time when she became acquainted with Jensen Huang. Huang and Kang used their gaming business to expand into semiconductors and data centers, becoming an Nvidia customer in the process. Huang then took over Hong Kong-based gaming company 7Road’s international subsidiary based in Singapore, 7Road International, and purchased Nvidia chips through a Malaysian affiliate. U.S. authorities suspect the chips were then transshipped to the PRC. The Huang-Kang network cultivated ties with local governments in the PRC. The investment arm of Shanghai’s Songjiang District, which owned a stake in Gu Guoping’s Phicomm, sold the stake to a company in their network after Phicomm failed in the wake of Gu’s criminal activity. At the center of the downfall of Jensen Huang, the co-founder and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of technology giant Nvidia, is a woman identified as Huang Le (黄乐), also known as Alice Huang. Media reporting alleges that Ms. Huang, a former executive of one of Nvidia’s largest customers in Southeast Asia, the Singapore-based computing company Megaspeed, had an affair with Jensen Huang. Megaspeed has been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips covered by U.S. export control restrictions into the People’s Republic of China (PRC). Reports have also said that U.S. intelligence considered Ms. Huang to have been coopted by the PRC’s Ministry of State Security (MSS) ( New York Times [NYT] , October 29; Washington Post , November 15).  [1] Beijing has been quick to deny these allegations, but some pro-U.S. Chinese intellectuals are more skeptical. They view the current scandal as a consequence of infighting within the Trump administration and between Trump and the “deep state” ( Tencent News ; X/@Wuyuesanren ; X/@WoodenHarp , November 10). In an interview, a Shanghai businessman expressed a similar view, saying that Ms. Huang’s network used an elaborate, multilayered corporate structure to conceal who ultimately controlled it, calling this tactic “the sort of thing Shanghai has been doing since the time of the Tongzhi Emperor” (上海滩从同治皇帝时候就玩的东西了), referring to the period of early modernization in the second half of the 19th century (Author interview, November 10). He believed Ms. Huang’s purpose was simply to smuggle chips into the PRC. Ms. Huang emerged from the world of Shanghai finance, where her connections to figures who have subsequently been found guilty of financial crime suggest that her profile should have raised more red flags. Her network centered on an investment firm, Hexi Investment Management (上海和熙投资管理), which was founded by one her alleged romantic partners, the businessman Kang Wei (康伟) ( Financial Times , November 10). Other major figures in this network include Huang Yu (黄瑜), whom the Financial Times describes as Ms. Huang’s sister; and Gu Guoping (顾国平), the founder of communications company Phicomm (斐讯技术) ( Financial Times , November 10; Caixin , November 10).  [2] Ms. Huang co-founded Shanghai Yunxi (上海韵禧) in 2016, and Huang Yu took over the following year ( The Time Weekly , November 9). (Source: Author’s research) Gaming Served as Gateway to Data Centers For Ms. Huang, as for Nvidia, the gaming industry provided a route into the compute business. PRC game publishers often set up foreign entities to serve overseas markets, providing a legitimate reason to import graphics processors and expand data center capacity. Huang became involved with 7Road Holdings (第七大道), a Hong Kong-listed game developer, after it had acquired a portfolio of gaming businesses held by an entity wholly owned by her and registered in the British Virgin Islands ( Caizhongshe , November 11). A circular announcing the acquisition identified a company owned by Kang Wei, Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), as a “party acting in concert” (一致行动人) with Ms. Huang. It also listed among the portfolio’s operating entities in the PRC a company previously owned by a subsidiary of Century Huatong (世紀華通), another firm with ties to Kang and Huang ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 25, 2019).  [3] With Ms. Huang now behind the scenes, Yunxi expanded her business network into the semiconductor and data center industries through cooperation with 7Road starting in 2022. A 7Road subsidiary committed renminbi (RMB) 330 million ($49 million) to a limited partnership managed by Yunxi whose sole asset was a 5.29 percent stake in a Shanghai-based semiconductor wafer manufacturer ( Hong Kong Exchange , May 24, 2022). 7Road also expanded into the data center and cloud computing businesses in 2019, offering cloud services for gaming and the possibility of third-party data center services in a cooperation framework ( Hong Kong Exchange , December 30, 2019; Hong Kong Exchange , May 9, 2021). A 7Road subsidiary involved in Huang’s gaming portfolio later became a vehicle for 7Road’s cloud computing business, buying graphics processors and servers ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 25, 2019).  [4] In 2022, it raised RMB 150 million ($24 million at the time) through a sale-and-lease-back of equipment that included 9,800 graphics processors ( Hong Kong Exchange , March 15, 2022). They can help make introductions, serve as a go-between for the MSS and a source, provide excuses for sources to travel to the PRC, or otherwise assist the MSS in its operations. The MSS may also approach these people because of the access, business, or other ability that they have to support operations ( National Interest , June 11, 2017). [2] In November 2014, CITIC Securities (中信证券) bought a 3.8 percent stake in a technology firm under a stock return swap with Hexi, helping Gu gain control of the listed company ( CSRC , May 12, 2017). Ms. Huang worked in securities financing at CITIC at the time. The deal may have brought her into contact with Kang a year before she joined Hexi ( Hexi Investment , March 17, 2017). [3] In 2014, Hexi subscribed for shares in Century Huatong connected to its acquisitions of Tianyou Software (天游软件) and Wuxi SevenCool (无锡七酷网络). In 2017, Wuxi SevenCool sold the gaming company Hangzhou Shengfeng (杭州盛锋) to Ningbo Jingxuan (宁波镜瑄), whose ultimate controller is Kang (CNINF, March 9, 2014 , March 7, 2017 ). [4] The name of this firm, Shanghai Lingsu (上海凌素), closely resembles another firm within Ms. Huang’s business network, Shanghai Lingsuda (上海领素达), which invests primarily in smart mobility and ride-hailing platforms (see the Interactive Map) ( CAIC , August 16, 2023; Hong Kong Exchange , December 23, 2024). Yunxi also entered the ownership chain of a data center holding company, also based in Shanghai, and in 2025 changed its own registered name to Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing Data Group (上海珑腾智算数据集团) ( Hong Kong Exchange , September 13, 2023; Times Weekly , November 9). In Shanghai business circles, it is common to register a series of companies with names that share the same Chinese characters or use different characters with the same pronunciation. Other businesspeople can then easily tell who actually controls a company from its name alone. [5] Kang had previously used companies he controlled, including Hexi, to take over three major Phicomm shareholding vehicles ( Sina Finance , August 10, 2018). [6] Such data centers under Kang’s control, with refurbishment nearing completion, would very likely use Nvidia chips smuggled into the PRC through Huang’s Megaspeed. [7] The business tactic of offering one’s spouse to another man reaches even much further back. During the Warring States period, Zichu (子楚), a prince of Qin (秦), took an interest in Zhao Ji (赵姬), the consort of the merchant Lu Buwei (吕不韦). Lu, considering how much he had already bet on Zichu to be the next King of Qin, offered Zhao Ji, who was already pregnant, to him. After Zichu became king of Qin, Lu was appointed chancellor and wielded power over the Qin court ( Records of the Grand Historian , accessed November 11). A historical conspiracy theory even held that Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇), first emperor of ancient China, was Lu and Zhao Ji’s son. In the early 2010s, PRC financial media and business books often portrayed Lu Buwei as a merchant who knew how to bet on real power (through whatever means), fueling an interest in him among businessmen of the era (see Fortune China , March 23, 2011). That was precisely when Kang rose to prominence in business. The post Alice Huang’s Shady Shanghai Ties to Business and Government appeared first on Jamestown .

三边会谈 + 气候呼吁 + 间谍事件 Linda_Heyer Thu, 11/19/2026 - 14:46 picture league / Win McNamee/Pool Getty Images AsiaPac via AP Download (pdf - 720.16 KB) MERICS Briefs MERICS China Essentials Nov 19, 2026 11 分钟阅读 三边会谈 + 气候呼吁 + 间谍事件 头条新闻 普京习近平按自己的方式主持峰会，特朗普成为众人瞩目的焦点 美中俄深圳峰会对俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京来说是一次外交胜利，但习近平成为了更大的赢家，他成功主持了一场可能让中国在深圳举办的亚太经合组织峰会黯然失色的会议。对于因俄罗斯近五年的侵略乌克兰战争而被西方孤立的普京来说，这次会议提供了一个轻松的机会来展现一位在国际外交最高层仍然受欢迎的领导人的形象。对习近平来说，中国对两位不可预测的客人的精心舞台管理得到了回报，峰会既没有像莫斯科所希望的那样就乌克兰问题达成“雅尔塔式”协议，也没有像美国总统唐纳德·特朗普所建议的那样让北京参与削减核武器谈判。
根据俄罗斯政府会后发布的联合声明，三位领导人确实同意“就减少核风险和防止核扩散进行对话”，但这不应损害北京的既定立场，即美国和俄罗斯必须在中国加入任何谈判之前大幅削减其更庞大的核武库。习近平、普京和特朗普还承诺改革联合国，并同意增加石油产量。也许对维护基于规则的国际秩序的西方国家来说最痛苦的是，该声明还表示，国家官员的豁免权是“根本性的”，国际刑事法院不得滥用其权力，该法院于 2023 年对普京发出了逮捕令。后一点将加剧欧洲的担忧，即美国总统在几个问题上与北京和莫斯科更加一致。但乌克兰的未来并未出现在官方结论中，这一事实使欧洲免于陷入更糟糕的境地。在莫斯科本身提高了对三边会议的期望后，普京似乎急于挽回乌克兰问题上缺乏进展的面子，并强调他已与习近平和特朗普分别讨论了这场战争。深圳的情况也没有暗示新的平等国家“G3”。在他们第 50 次面对面会面时，习近平再次称普京为“老朋友”，但没有像接待特朗普那样到机场接待他。
周四，习近平与特朗普的双边会晤和午餐会持续了很长时间，以至于普京不得不等待三边会议开始。“最重要的事情可能是三边会议最终举行了。习近平让普京得到了他所寻求的关注，同时为特朗普保留了红地毯待遇。通过这样做，他成功地举办了一场可能有风险的会议。”  伊娃·塞沃特 (Eva Seiwert)，MERICS 高级分析师 更多相关主题：为什么习近平可能有自己的理由避免美俄中峰会 – MERICS 伊娃·塞沃特 (Eva Seiwert) 的评论 媒体报道和来源：中国外交部（CN）：习近平会见俄罗斯总统普京 BBC：普京称俄罗斯、美国和中国对全球和平负有“共同责任” 路透社：直播：特朗普、习近平和普京举行了前所未有的三边会谈，重点关注乌克兰和核武器METRIX 1,042,590,000,000 这是中国2026年前10个月的贸易顺差，以美元计算。顺差突破1万亿美元三月

【原文 English Original】
Trilateral talks + Climate call-out + Espionage affair Linda_Heyer Thu, 11/19/2026 - 14:46 picture alliance / Win McNamee/Pool Getty Images AsiaPac via AP Download (pdf - 720.16 KB) MERICS Briefs MERICS China Essentials Nov 19, 2026 11 min read Trilateral talks + Climate call-out + Espionage affair Top story Putin gets the spotlight and Trump the red carpet as Xi runs the summit on his terms The US-China-Russia summit in Shenzhen was a diplomatic win for Russian President Vladimir Putin, but Xi Jinping emerged as the bigger winner, successfully managing a meeting that risked overshadowing the APEC summit China was hosting in the same city. For Putin, isolated by the West over Russia’s near five-year war of aggression against Ukraine, the meeting offered an easy opportunity to project the image of a leader still welcome at the highest level of international diplomacy. For Xi, China’s careful stage management of two unpredictable guests paid off, with the summit neither producing a “Yalta-style” agreement on Ukraine, as Moscow had favored, nor binding Beijing into nuclear-arms reduction talks, as US President Donald Trump had suggested.  The three leaders did agree to “engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation,” according to a joint statement released by the Russian government after the meeting, but this should not undermine Beijing’s established position that the US and Russia must make substantial reductions to their much larger arsenals before China joins any talks. Xi, Putin and Trump also committed to reforming the UN and agreed to increase oil production. Perhaps most painfully for Western countries that uphold the rules-based international order, the statement also said immunity for state officials was “fundamental” and that the International Criminal Court, which issued an arrest warrant for Putin in 2023, must not abuse its authority.  This latter point will reinforce European concerns that the US president is more aligned with Beijing and Moscow on several issues. But the fact that the future of Ukraine did not feature in the official conclusions spared Europe from worse. After Moscow itself had raised expectations for the trilateral, Putin appeared keen to save face over this lack of progress on Ukraine, stressing that he had discussed the war separately with Xi and Trump. The optics in Shenzhen also did not suggest a new “G3” of equal countries.  Xi once again called Putin his “old friend” at what was their 50th in-person meeting, but did not receive him at the airport as he did Trump. Xi’s bilateral meeting and lunch with Trump on Thursday ran so long that Putin was left waiting for the trilateral to begin.  "The most significant thing may have been that the trilateral took place at all. Xi gave Putin the spotlight he sought, while reserving the red-carpet treatment for Trump. In doing so, he successfully managed a potentially risky meeting.”  Eva Seiwert , Senior Analyst, MERICS More on the topic: Why Xi may have his own reasons to avert a US-Russia-China summit – MERICS Comment by Eva Seiwert Media coverage and sources: Chinese MFA (CN): 习近平会见俄罗斯总统普京   BBC: Putin says Russia, US, and China share 'joint responsibility' for global peace Reuters: Live: Trump, Xi and Putin hold unprecedented trilateral talks, with Ukraine and nuclear arms in focus METRIX 1,042,590,000,000 This is China’s trade surplus in the first ten months of 2026, in US dollars. The surplus broke the USD 1 trillion mark in October, one month earlier than in 2025, putting it on track to exceed last year’s record annual surplus of USD 1.2 trillion. A surge in foreign demand for electric vehicles, technology and AI-related products has seen exports outpace imports, even though the latter are themselves growing rapidly. Exports of computer parts were up 235 percent, those of semiconductors up 110.8 percent, and those of vehicles up 52.2 percent. (Source: General Administration of Customs )  GRAPHIC OF THE WEEK China exported 41 billion USD more goods to Germany between January and October 2026 than it imported from Europe’s largest economy – almost twice the trade surplus recorded in the same period last year. As the latest issue of the SOAPBOX newsletter on China reported, citing Chinese customs data, this increase accounted for nearly one third of the 69 billion USD increase in China’s trade surplus with the EU as a whole.  China’s surplus with Germany grew almost five times as fast as the 22 percent rise in its surplus with the rest of the EU, which reached USD 270 billion. This highlights Germany’s deep economic ties with China – and its resulting exposure to Chinese competition. As China sells more higher-value products abroad and increasingly sources components domestically, Germany faces a big double squeeze: rising imports and falling exports.  SOAPBOX is a weekly newsletter on EU-China trade relations compiled by Rafael Buendia Jimenez and Ilaria Perla. You can subscribe to the newsletter for free here . TOPICS China uses COP31 to showcase Europe’s dilemma on climate and trade China’s clear position at November’s UN climate change conference in Türkiye stood in stark contrast to Europe’s growing dilemma between its climate ambitions, defensive trade policy toward China and growing reluctance to commit more financing for developing countries dealing with global warming.  Before COP 31, Beijing had emphasized the need to discuss “old issues” of insufficient climate financing and “new challenges” of unilateralism and protectionism, which were harming “collective efforts to address climate change.” But in the end, it was the African Group that proposed putting climate-related trade and climate finance on the agenda. Their contention that Europe’s additional levy on carbon-intensive imports is unfair to Africa reinforced China's argument that European protectionism is undermining global climate cooperation. The EU objected to these proposals, which included the tripling of finance pledges, but did not block the Climate Finance Work Programme – a process to work out how developed countries meet their climate finance obligations to developing nations – as a separate agenda item.  The bloc is under pressure to fill a US-sized financing gap after US President Donald Trump’s withdrawal from the Paris agreement. Domestic opposition to a larger pledge is growing, as the EU is already one of the largest donors worldwide. Europe’s reluctance to step up, together with a lack of high-level European leaders at the conference stands in a stark contrast to China’s dominant cleantech offer to the world.  "The EU faces a dilemma: decarbonization is needed to fight climate change, but Chinese cleantech dominance and exports to the EU are a geoeconomics challenge. As the EU grapples with this, China’s proposed solution – more Chinese cleantech and more climate funding from developed countries – is gaining momentum.” Johanna Krebs , Analyst, MERICS Media coverage and sources : Xinhua (CN): 以“双碳”为牵引加快全面绿色转型——生态环境部介绍我国应对气候变化工作成效 Down to Earth: COP31 Adopts Climate Finance Work Programme Amid Tensions Over Adaptation Funding and Trade Carbon Brief: COP31: Agenda adopted! - Conversations / Policy   Carbon Brief: Interactive: Who wants what at the COP31 climate change summit Euronews: ‘More than just a photo opportunity’: Why are key EU leaders skipping the COP31 Leaders’ Summit? Nvidia’s espionage drama could backfire on Chinese AI ambitions Revelations that the chief executive of US chipmaker Nvidia, Jensen Huang, had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy could deal another blow to China’s AI industry, which is already grappling with an economic slowdown and Beijing’s push for labs to switch to less powerful domestic hardware such as chips designed by Huawei. The US government is openly split between advocates of continued commercial engagement and national-security hawks who want to cut off Chinese access to US AI technology. But pressure from lawmakers in Washington for tighter controls is mounting – and Congress could ultimately override any presidential veto of legislation covering foreign trade. China’s AI stocks, already caught in China’s broader market correction, have slumped again. Huang has not just been Nvidia’s guiding light since co-founding the company in 1993, but he also successfully lobbied US officials, including President Donald Trump, over the last two years to relax chip export controls. US lawmakers now want to crack down on smuggling networks that supply China with the most advanced US-designed AI chips and on schemes that give Chinese companies remote cloud access to powerful chips via data centers located in third countries. The Commerce Department will also soon require companies to obtain licenses for advanced semiconductor exports, re-exports and transfers to data centers in Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil. Data centers anywhere in the world will need permission to service Chinese companies.  "China's AI future is deeply tied to policy decisions made in Washington, which the networks and choices of a few tech CEOs can shape in fundamental ways. Huang was one of the most influential advocates of maintaining the flow of US AI chips to China. But the espionage allegations will make that position much harder to defend – and leave China’s AI industry with even fewer options.” Rebecca Arcesati , Head of Program (Co-Lead) Science, Technology and Innovation, MERICS Media coverage and sources: The New York Times: The Fall of Jensen Huang Reuters: US to curb China's access to AI chips as Trump heads to Asia Bloomberg: Nvidia Stops Selling AI chips to China Despite US Approval Xi tightens his grip on local party committees – in good time for a fourth term Xi Jinping’s third term as General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) ends in the second half of 2027, but it looks like he is not going anywhere. The CCP’s Central Committee on November 7, 2026, issued revised regulations on the work of local party committees for the first time since 2015. The new rules are meant to improve decision-making by cadres in provinces, cities and counties to make sure central directives are implemented. Maintaining a strong chain of command from the center down to the local level is of paramount importance to the CCP’s ability to meet its goals – and to securing Xi’s position at the apex of the party, making a fourth term increasingly likely. Xi and the other then 22 members of the Politburo had announced the review of the regulation in March. They require officials to shoulder “political responsibility” for ensuring that the Central Committee’s policies are effectively implemented. Contradicting the leadership’s directives, engaging in local protectionism, pursuing prestige projects designed to demonstrate political achievements and improperly increasing local government hidden debt are expressly forbidden. Local party committee members are subject to “lifelong accountability” for rule violations and decision-making errors. Although permanent responsibility already applies to environmental and certain major administrative decisions, this is a significant extension of the mechanism. "The ideologies of Marx, Lenin and Mao have been removed from the regulations, while Xi’s status as ‘core leader’ has been codified. His latest instructions and speeches are now the first item on the agenda at local party meetings. Xi wants to put cadres’ feet to the fire and make sure they get the job done the way he wants it. He looks like a leader who expects to keep a close eye on them for a while yet.”  Alexander Davey , Analyst, MERICS Media coverage and sources: SCMP: Communist Party lays down the internal discipline law for local leader s Xinhua (CN): 《 中国共产党地方委员会工作条例 》 (Regulations on the Work of Local Committees of the Chinese Communist Party) Communist Party Member Network (CN): 《 中国共产党地方委员会工作条例 (2015) 》 (Archived version of the previous 2015 regulations) Lianhe Zaobao Singapore (CN): Revised work regulations of local party committees bans "vanity" projects and "prestige" projects China successfully targets rich to boost income-tax revenue China appears to be having considerable success in taxing its richer residents more. Revenues from personal income tax surged 90 percent in October 2026 from a year earlier, after tax authorities in July introduced rules requiring Chinese residents to pay tax on assets transferred into offshore trusts and on income generated by them. Taxpayers – mostly the country’s ultra-rich – had until late October to comply, effectively closing a loophole used to protect assets from the Chinese state. Tax revenue linked to offshore trusts reached CNY 160 billion in the first ten months of 2026, which suggests personal income-tax revenue from January to October 2026 is likely to have already exceeded the 2025 full-year total of CNY 1.62 trillion (about EUR 221 billion).  China’s overall tax revenue has been rising over the past year, spurred in particular by securities trading. But with China’s AI bubble deflating and share prices falling, the additional personal income tax revenue from offshore trusts is a welcome boost to state finances. Personal income tax accounts for only a portion of total tax revenue. At 9 percent, it carries less weight than value-added tax, which accounts for 39 percent of revenues, or corporate income tax, which accounts for 23 percent. But the increased flow of revenues from taxing offshore trust assets and income will provide additional fiscal room by offsetting declines in land-tax and consumption-tax revenue.  “The surge in personal income tax takings is the latest sign of China’s push to expand its tax base and strengthen public revenues. The recent focus on taxing offshore trusts, most of which are owned by high-net-worth individuals, also opens up other opportunities. It allows authorities to exercise greater oversight over capital outflows and potentially redistribute wealth more evenly.” Sophia Pradels , Analyst, MERICS Media coverage and sources: Xinhua (CN): 离岸信托收益征税平稳有序推进 (Offshore Trust Income Taxation Is Progressing Smoothly and Orderly) Yicai: China’s Personal Income Tax Haul Nearly Doubles in October on Offshore Trust Windfall Financial Times: China warns of ‘severe’ punishment for offshore trust tax evaders MERICS CHINA DIGEST China's economy falters as factory output, retail sales undershoot expectations (Reuters) Chinese retail sales grew just 0.4% year-on-year in October, down from 1.1% in September, while industrial production growth slowed to 4.8%.  (26/11/16) China's Singles Day sales rise 4.8% to USD 1.78 trillion; AI takes larger role (Reuters) China's Singles Day shopping generated CNY 1.78 trillion in revenues, but annual sales growth slowed to 4.8% from 14.2% in 2025 despite weeks of promotions.
