title: The military lacks an ‘overarching plan’ to improve munition stockpiles—partly because it’s no one’s job
zh_title: 军方缺乏改善弹药库存的“总体计划”——部分原因是这不是任何人的工作
summary: 根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军队可以购买的东西和实际需要的东西之间的差异。
content:
根据政府问责办公室周四发布的一份研究报告，国防部没有确定、实现或衡量其在实现长期弹药生产目标方面取得的进展的“总体计划”，该研究称军方对全球事件过于敏感，并且没有准备好预测自己的需求。美国政府问责局指出，除其他问题外，武器库存缺乏集中权力，武器库存已因伊朗战争而耗尽，对美国与中国发生潜在冲突的计划至关重要。问题的核心在于军方可以购买的东西与实际需要的东西之间存在差异，政府问责局表示，这甚至可能导致弹药投资超出五角大楼的要求。该报告的作者写道：“虽然国防部正在采取措施关注弹药短缺问题，但它无法解决这些差距。” “国防部没有总体计划，也没有指定和授权的领导层来改善弹药库存并满足其弹药需求。由于没有确定长期目标、实现这些目标的战略以及衡量进展的指标，国防部无法确定其行动是否能够解决弹药短缺问题。”包括国防部长皮特·赫格塞斯在内的高级政府官员否认美国存在弹药短缺，尽管有报告和独立分析显示，伊朗冲突已经严重耗尽了弹药。关键武器，特别是备受追捧的爱国者拦截机，其制造时间可能超过两年。
但在对政府问责局研究的回应中，五角大楼官员同意军方需要制定一项长期计划来提高弹药生产的建议。五角大楼负责采购的代理副手大卫·卡德曼写道：“我们同意需要一个总体框架，更好地整合弹药需求、库存水平、生产、资源和长期目标。”他补充说，国防部“已经执行了政府问责局建议中的许多内容”。美国政府问责局的研究并未探讨特定弹药的库存，而是研究了五角大楼跟踪、预测和总体处理一系列武器（从炮弹到战斧导弹）的过程。 “重要的是，[这项研究]与当前的短缺无关，”战略与国际研究中心的高级顾问马克·坎西恩（Mark Cancian）撰写了大量有关弹药政策的文章。 “这关系到未来并决定长期库存、生产和弹药组合。”  国防官员强调需要“高低”弹药组合，即高科技、难以制造的武器和廉价武器之间的平衡。伊朗战争说明了美军对昂贵拦截机的依赖，这些拦截机投入了大量资金来击落廉价的沙赫德无人机，这些无人机的成本只有数万美元。
彭博资讯国防分析师韦恩·桑德斯表示：“当你拥有先进的能力，并且开始消耗先进的能力来击落快速补充的非先进能力时，这是一场我们赢不了的经济游戏。”“这开始转变为军事领域的一场革命，表明我们必须改变我们的学说，同时改变我们在美国的生产能力。”   美国政府问责局国防能力主管戴安娜·摩尔达夫斯基 (Diana Moldafsky) 在周五发给《防务一号》的一封电子邮件中指出，五角大楼已经发现了不足之处

【原文 English Original】
The Defense Department has no “overarching plan” to identify, achieve, or measure its progress toward long-term munition production goals, according to a Government Accountability Office study released on Thursday, which said the military was too reactive to global events and unprepared to forecast its own needs. The GAO cited—among other issues—a lack of centralized authority over weapons inventories, which have been depleted by the Iran war and are vital to U.S. plans for a potential conflict with China. At the center of the problem lies a discrepancy between what the military can buy and what it actually needs, which the GAO said could even result in munition investments that exceed the Pentagon’s requirements.  “While DOD is taking steps to focus on munitions shortages, it is not positioned to address these gaps,” the report’s authors wrote. “DOD does not have an overarching plan or designated and empowered leadership to improve munition inventories and meet its munitions requirements. By not identifying long-term goals, strategies to achieve them, and metrics to gauge progress, DOD cannot be sure that its actions will address its munition shortfalls. ” Top administration officials, including Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, have denied that the U.S. has a shortage in munitions, despite reports and independent analyses showing the Iran conflict has alarmingly drained key weapons, especially for highly-sought Patriot interceptors that can take more than two years to make. But in its response to the GAO study, Pentagon officials concurred with the recommendation that the military needed to develop a long-term plan to improve its munition production.  “We agree with the need for an overarching framework that better integrates munition requirements, inventory levels, production, resources, and long-term objectives,” wrote David Cadman, the Pentagon’s acting deputy for acquisitions, who added that the department “already executes many elements” of the GAO’s recommendation. The GAO study did not explore the inventories of specific munitions, but examined the processes by which an expansive list of weapons — from artillery shells to Tomahawk missiles — are tracked, forecast and generally addressed by the Pentagon. “The important thing is that [the study] is not about current shortages,” Mark Cancian, a senior adviser with the Center for Strategic and International Studies who has written extensively on munitions policy. “It's about the future and deciding long-term inventories, production, and munitions mixes.”  Defense officials have emphasized the need for a “high-low” mix of munitions—that is, a balance between high-tech, hard-to-make weapons and cheaper ones. The Iran war illustrated the U.S. military’s reliance on expensive interceptors, which were heavily expended to shoot down cheap Shahed drones that only cost tens of thousands of dollars.  “When you have an exquisite capacity, and you are starting to expend an exquisite capacity to knock down non-exquisite capabilities that are rapidly replenished, it is an economical game that we're not going to win,” said Wayne Sanders, a defense analyst with Bloomberg Intelligence. “This is starting to turn into one of those revolutions in military affairs to say we have to change our doctrine as well as we change our production capacity in the U.S.”   In an email to Defense One on Friday, the GAO’s director for defense capabilities, Diana Moldafsky, noted that the Pentagon had identified shortfalls before the conflict with Iran, but said that the war “made addressing those shortages more urgent.” “Our key point is that meeting DOD's munitions requirements will be challenging,” Moldafsky said. “A department-wide plan would help the department direct its resources towards its most critical munitions needs.”  Cancian said that Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and the consequent transfer of Patriots and other weapons to Kyiv, introduced concerns about the defense industrial base and its ability to respond to munition needs around the world. Meanwhile, the Pentagon has inked billions of dollars in multi-year “framework agreements” with top defense companies over the last year to help increase high-tech munition production, which require funding from Congress to come to fruition. The Trump administration also invoked the Defense Production Act earlier this year in an attempt to bolster munition supply chains. A Pentagon spokesperson declined to address the GAO study directly, or even to be quoted by name. But they said the military is “fully equipped to strike at the time and place of the President’s choosing…while preserving a deep, ready stockpile to defend our people and interests.” Part of the problem is that no one authority is really in charge of keeping arsenals topped off and ready, the report found.  The GAO identified several Pentagon offices and working groups, including individual service entities, responsible for managing munition inventories, but no one dedicated authority “that empowers the leadership to make decisions that improve munitions inventories department-wide and hold them accountable for the outcomes achieved, such as improving munitions inventory levels.” The study also said that the services maintain separate tools to track munition inventories, which then feed into a Pentagon system known as the Munitions Readiness Initiative. But researchers said the DOD has limited oversight over that tracking platform and hasn’t regularly reconciled it with service-level numbers. Citing an unnamed Pentagon official in its acquisitions and sustainment office, the GAO said “the office was reluctant to impose additional responsibilities on the services for maintaining data to meet MRI’s needs because they recognize that the services already face numerous responsibilities in managing their own munitions inventory data.” The Pentagon concurred with most of the GAO’s recommendations, but only partially agreed with one: that the data management plan be run out of the DOD’s digital and AI office. Cadman’s response said that the Pentagon’s acquisition and sustainment arm was best suited to develop it. ]]>

title: In Pictures: Time-honoured Hong Kong saucemaker to close, ceding land to Northern Metropolis megaproject
zh_title: 图片：香港历史悠久的酱料制造商将关闭，将土地割让给北都大型项目
summary: 在被称为“鹅颈桥”的铜锣湾立交桥一侧，在“坏人打人”的节奏喧嚣声中，顾客们涌入当地一家调味品制造商的商店，该商店位于北部乡村的工厂被清理干净，其所在的土地现已割让给一个庞大的开发项目。 2026 年 10 月 28 日，桂利酱和果脯的铜锣湾店面。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。购物车里装满了老抽、黑醋和甜豆瓣酱，所有这些都自豪地被吹捧为本地制造，而工人们则将啤酒厂剩余的库存从后面运进来。
content:
在被称为“鹅颈桥”的铜锣湾立交桥一侧，在“坏人打人”的节奏喧嚣声中，顾客们涌入当地一家调味品制造商的商店，该商店位于北部乡村的工厂被清理干净，其所在的土地现已割让给一个庞大的开发项目。 2026 年 10 月 28 日，桂利酱和果脯的铜锣湾店面。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。购物车里装满了老抽、黑醋和甜酱油，所有这些都被自豪地标榜为本地制造，而工人们则从后面将啤酒厂剩余的库存推入车内，顾客与白发苍苍的店主亲切地交谈着。继位于香港新界北部的桂利酱和果脯厂址被驱逐和清理后，这家拥有 90 年历史的酱料制造商正在倒计时，直到出售剩余库存并永远关闭铜锣湾店面。 2026 年 10 月 28 日，桂利酱和果脯的铜锣湾店面。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。该公司现已关闭的工厂位于古洞，这是新界的一个农村地区，是北方都市大型项目下开发的地区，该项目旨在实现香港乡村边疆的现代化，并加深与中国大陆的融合。 1936 年开业的工厂关闭，结束了这家酱料制造商的“香港制造”传统。
乔安妮·陈 (Joanne Chan) 是一位忠实顾客，她在商店关门前来到这家商店储备酱汁，对她来说，啤酒厂的倒闭象征着开发项目的损失，从村民的流离失所到对新科技中心需求的怀疑。2026 年 10 月 28 日，桂利酱和果脯的铜锣湾店面。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 “这些传统品牌已经经营了几十年，但政府没有计划让他们继续经营。相反，他们被迫关闭，”她说。该工厂在上个月的驱逐行动后现已被封锁，位于古洞北新发展区，占地 447 公顷，将为公共和私人住宅开发、商业设施和新地铁站让路。 2026 年 10 月 28 日，桂利酱和果脯的铜锣湾店面。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。这家酱料制造商的工厂距离香港和邻近的中国城市深圳之间最近的边境管制站仅 15 分钟车程。整个北都城项目旨在拉近香港与内地的距离，将约 300 平方公里（约占该市土地的三分之一）转变为创新科技中心。 2026 年 10 月 28 日，桂利酱和果脯的铜锣湾店面。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
陈氏家族九十年的经营经历跨越了三代人，他们于 1940 年代在九龙城开设了第一家酿酒厂，当时是当地酿酒商的中心。 1960 年代的城市重建迫使李氏和其他调味品制造商进入新界，该酿酒厂一直留在新界，直到上个月被驱逐。 2026 年 10 月 28 日，桂利酱和果脯的铜锣湾店面。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。事实证明，农村环境对调味品制造商来说是一个福音，因为大片土地使他们能够继续使用传统的露天方法在阳光下发酵和氧化大豆。但大部分酱厂从香港市中心迁往北部腹地

【原文 English Original】
Off to the side of the Causeway Bay flyover known as Goose Neck Bridge, over the polyrhythmic din of “villain hitting,” customers crowded into a local condiment maker’s shop after its factory in the rural north was cleared, the land it stood on now ceded to a gargantuan development project. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Shopping trolleys were filled with dark soy sauce, black vinegar, and sweet soybean paste, all proudly touted as locally made, while workers carted in what remained of the brewer’s stock through the back and customers exchanged friendly words with grey-haired shopkeepers. Following the eviction and clearance of Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s factory site in Hong Kong’s northern New Territories, the 90-year-old saucemaker is counting down the days until it sells off its remaining inventory and closes its Causeway Bay storefront for good. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Its now-shuttered factory was in Kwu Tung, a rural area in the New Territories tapped for development under the Northern Metropolis megaproject, which aims to modernise Hong Kong’s rustic frontier and deepen its integration with mainland China. The closure of the factory, opened in 1936, brings the saucemaker’s “Made in Hong Kong” legacy to an end. For Joanne Chan, a loyal customer who came by the shop to stock up on sauces ahead of its closure, the brewer’s end is emblematic of the development project’s toll, from the displacement of villagers to doubts over the demand for a new tech hub. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “These traditional brands have operated for decades, but the government has no plan to let them keep going. Instead, they’re being forced to close,” she said. The factory, now sealed off after an eviction operation last month, falls within the Kwu Tung North New Development Area, which spans 447 hectares and will make way for both public and private residential developments, as well as commercial facilities and a new MTR station. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The saucemaker’s factory was just a 15-minute drive from the closest border control point between Hong Kong and the neighbouring Chinese city of Shenzhen. The entire Northern Metropolis project is meant to draw Hong Kong closer to the mainland, transforming about 300 square kilometres — roughly a third of the city’s land — into an innovation and technology hub. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Kui Lee’s nine decades in business have spanned three generations of the Chan family, who opened their first brewing yard in the 1940s in Kowloon City, then a hub for local brewers. Urban redevelopment in the 1960s forced Kui Lee, along with other condiment makers, into the New Territories, where the brewer remained until last month’s eviction. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The rural surroundings proved to be a boon for condiment makers, as the large swathes of land allowed them to keep using traditional open-air methods to ferment and oxidise soybeans under sunlight. But most of the sauce factories that moved from Hong Kong’s urban core to its northern hinterland in the mid-20th century are now facing eviction for the Northern Metropolis. One saucemaker, Koon Chun, is fortunate enough to continue operating after the megaproject clears out its current site. Moving to its new facility, however, will take about a decade. Yuet Wo Soy Sauce, Kui Lee’s neighbour in Kwu Tung, is looking for a new site in a Tsuen Wan industrial building to stay in business. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Rural villages, sawmills, and carp farms are also on their way out — with some already evicted — as deadlines loom for the Northern Metropolis project. With the October clearance operation, the family also moved out of their homes on the Kwu Tung site, according to a South China Morning Post report, which noted that power was cut off and water pipes were severed two days ahead of the clearance deadline. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Joanne Chan spoke of her own experience of being evicted from a village house in Tuen Mun some two decades ago to make way for a railway line. “I understand the pain that land resumption and eviction causes; I’m strongly opposed to it,” she said. “You could grow your own fruit trees in your own yard, but after the eviction, all you get is a few hundred square feet,” she said, referring to government resettlement policies. “Those university towns and tech parks aren’t what we need as ordinary citizens.” Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Go ahead, ask her,” she said, pointing to another middle-aged customer browsing the store’s wares. “Do you think she wants [artificial intelligence]?” Other customers also lamented the store’s impending closure, including a new mother buying ingredients for pork knuckle and ginger stew, a traditional postpartum dish made with sweetened black vinegar. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “I don’t know where I’m going to find soy sauce when they close, especially dark soy sauce,” said another customer, Tsang, who works nearby. The condiment – darker and less salty than its counterparts and mainly used to give dishes a deeper colour – is among Kui Lee’s most well-known products. Kui Lee Sauce and Preserved Fruit’s Causeway Bay storefront, on October 28, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Shops like these are getting harder to come by these days. Once one of them closes, there won’t be another to take its place. Of course, it’s a pity, but in this day and age, there’s nothing that can be done,” she said.

title: China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow
zh_title: 中国海军发展成为珠海航展的焦点
summary: 中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际防务、航空领域最重要的赛事之一
content:
中国人民解放军海军表示，正在准备在即将于珠海举行的第十六届中国国际航空航天博览会上进行重要亮相，军舰、舰载机、先进武器系统和无人平台将成为重点展示。扩大后的海军部分将包括在海湾另一边的高栏港设立一个新的海事装备展区，这标志着解放军海军首次在此次活动中设立这样的专门展示区。珠海已成为国际国防和航空航天史上最重要的活动之一，成为中国快速发展的航空和军事工业的主要公开展示地。两年一度的中国国际航空航天展览会（俗称中国航展）于 1996 年首次举办，为展示中国一些最先进的军事硬件提供了难得的机会，其中包括在其他地方很少如此详细展示的飞机和系统。虽然该活动也是中国航空航天工业向潜在国际客户推广其产品的主要平台，但它日益成为展示新军事能力和提供难以评估的项目的重要场所。
第十五届中国国际航空航天展览会（又称 2024 年中国航展）于 2024 年 11 月 15 日在中国广东省珠海市中国国际航空航天展览中心举行。摄影：VCG/VCG via Getty Images 前几届已经取得了一些特别重大的进展。 2016 年的展会上，J-20 隐形战斗机首次公开飞行亮相，而 2018 年的展会则以不同寻常的方式展示了这架飞机，包括展示其装载空对空导弹的内部武器舱。 2022年的展会上，歼20首次在珠海进行静态展示，同时还有运20重型运输机、直20直升机以及在展会上进行首次飞行演示的运20空中加油机。最近，2024 年的展会特别引人注目的是 J-35A 隐形战斗机的公开亮相和具有弹射能力的 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机的出现。一架 J-15T 舰​​载战斗机在 2024 年中国航展上进行飞行表演。CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images 今年的展览定于 12 月 7 日至 13 日举行，除其他外，将展示中国海军的广泛能力，特别强调其舰载航空能力的快速发展，这一点我们过去已经详细讨论过。
预计将亮相的最引人注目的飞机包括 J-15T 舰载战斗机、作战型 J-35 隐形战斗机、KJ-600 舰载机载预警和控制 (AEW&C) 飞机、Z-20 直升机的几种海军型号，也许最重要的是新型 JL-15 舰载教练机，它是陆基 JL-10 的发展型。JL-15 舰载教练机的照片突出显示了制动钩和弹射器发射杆。虽然我们之前在珠海见过 J-15T，但如果它配备国产 WS-10H2 发动机，将会引起特别的兴趣。这样的配置将让人们更仔细地了解中国舰载侧卫衍生产品的最新演变

【原文 English Original】
China’s People’s Liberation Army Navy (PLAN) says it’s preparing a major presence at the upcoming 16th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition in Zhuhai, with warships , carrier-based aircraft , advanced weapons systems, and uncrewed platforms set to feature prominently. The expanded naval component will include a new maritime equipment exhibition area at Gaolan Port, located just on the other side of the bay, marking the first time the PLAN has established such a dedicated display at the event. Zhuhai has become one of the most important events on the international defence and aerospace calendar, serving as China’s principal public showcase for its rapidly developing aviation and military industries. First held in 1996, the biennial China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China, provides an unusual opportunity to see some of the country’s most advanced military hardware, including aircraft and systems that are rarely shown in such detail elsewhere. While the event also serves as a major platform for China’s aerospace industry to promote its products to potential international customers , it has increasingly become an important venue for revealing new military capabilities and offering glimpses of programs that are otherwise difficult to assess. A general view of the 15th China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, or Airshow China 2024, at the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition Center on November 15, 2024, in Zhuhai, Guangdong Province of China. Photo by VCG/VCG via Getty Images Previous editions have produced some particularly significant developments. The 2016 show saw the J-20 stealth fighter make its first public flying appearance , while the 2018 edition provided an unusually revealing look at the aircraft, including a demonstration of its internal weapons bays, loaded with air-to-air missiles . The 2022 exhibition featured the J-20 on static display for the first time at Zhuhai, alongside the Y-20 heavy transport aircraft, Z-20 helicopter, and YY-20 aerial refueling tanker, which made its first flying demonstration at the event. More recently, the 2024 exhibition was particularly notable for the public debut of the J-35A stealth fighter and the appearance of the catapult-capable J-15T carrier-based fighter. A J-15T carrier-based fighter conducts a flight demonstration at Airshow China 2024. CFOTO/Future Publishing via Getty Images This year’s exhibition, scheduled to take place from December 7 to 13, will showcase, among others, a broad range of the PLAN’s capabilities, with a particularly notable emphasis on the rapid evolution of its carrier aviation capabilities, something we have addressed in detail in the past . Among the most noteworthy aircraft expected to feature are the J-15T carrier-based fighter, the operational J-35 stealth fighter, the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft, several naval variants of the Z-20 helicopter, and, perhaps most significantly, the new JL-15 carrier-capable trainer, a development of the land-based JL-10 . A photo of the JL-15 carrier-capable trainer with the arrestor hook and catapult launch bar highlighted. Chinese internet via X While we have seen the J-15T at Zhuhai before, the aircraft will be of particular interest if it is shown with the indigenous WS-10H2 engine. Such a configuration would offer a closer look at the latest evolution of China’s carrier-based Flanker derivative and its ongoing transition toward a more domestically supported carrier aviation ecosystem. The appearance of the J-35 would be another major highlight. The aircraft represents a significant step in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ambitions, bringing a fifth-generation stealth fighter capability into the carrier air wing. Its presence would provide another opportunity to examine the progress of China’s next-generation naval fighter program. Back in 2014, Zhuhai saw the public debut of the FC-31 fighter demonstrator. At the time, it was still a land-based concept, and export was the main talking point, although there was already speculation about a naval variant, today’s J-35. A People’s Liberation Army Navy J-35 fighter during trials from the carrier Fujian last year. Chinese internet via X Meanwhile, the KJ-600 is arguably one of the most important developments in the PLAN’s carrier aviation ecosystem. The twin-engine turboprop aircraft is designed to provide airborne early warning and battle management capabilities, something that would transform the situational awareness and coordination available to China’s carrier strike groups. One of the first high-definition photos of the KJ-600 carrier-based airborne early warning and control (AEW&C) aircraft. Chinese internet via X Several variants of the Z-20 family are also expected to feature, reflecting the growing importance of helicopters in carrier operations, including airborne anti-submarine warfare, utility, and other maritime support missions. You can read more about the Z-20 family and other Chinese rotary-wing developments in this previous TWZ deep-dive on the topic . A Z-20F, the anti-submarine warfare variant of the naval Z-20 family. Three more naval Z-20s are seen in the hangar behind, including a Z-20J shipborne transport and assault variant. Chinese internet via X Perhaps the most intriguing aircraft on the list, however, is the JL-15. The JL-15 is derived from the Hongdu JL-10, also exported as the L-15 Falcon, a twin-engine advanced jet trainer and lead-in fighter trainer. The navalized development was initially reported to be designated JL-10J, but is now confirmed as being the JL-15. A tailhook-equipped mockup was spotted alongside the aircraft carrier Fujian in 2024. However, its operational status remains unclear, and China is known to have encountered difficulties with its earlier JL-9G naval trainer, whose tailhook was reportedly deleted following structural problems. Regarding the rumoured JL-10J carrier-capable jet trainer, another hint was spotted next to the carrier Fujian: It appears to be an unfinished JL-10J mockup stored on the dockside . So question is: Two tails as shown in the latest CG or just one like the regular JL-10? pic.twitter.com/BM8W8MRGWK — @Rupprecht_A (@RupprechtDeino) March 19, 2024 Its appearance would provide a particularly interesting indication of how China is thinking about training its next generation of carrier-based pilots. A carrier-capable development of the JL-10 would be an important addition to the emerging carrier aviation ecosystem, bridging the gap between conventional jet training and the demanding requirements of operating from an aircraft carrier. The JL-15 also makes an interesting comparison with the U.S. Navy’s somewhat stuttering efforts to introduce a new training jet for its carrier pilots. The U.S. Navy’s Undergraduate Jet Training System (UJTS) program is intended to replace its aging fleet of T-45 Goshawk trainers, but the acquisition effort has encountered considerable difficulties. Earlier this month, we described how Sierra Nevada Corporation (SNC) withdrew its proposed clean-sheet Freedom Jet from the competition, citing concerns over the Navy’s insistence on firm-fixed-price production commitments before the aircraft’s design had sufficiently matured. This leaves the Beechcraft M-346N , based on Leonardo’s established M-346 Master , as the only publicly known remaining contender . The program has also experienced schedule slippage, with the initial contract award now expected in the fourth quarter of Fiscal Year 2027. Perhaps more significant is the difference in the two services’ approaches to carrier aviation training. The U.S. Navy has removed the requirement for its next-generation jet trainer to be capable of operating from an actual aircraft carrier, including carrier qualification and simulated carrier touch-and-goes at land-based facilities. Instead, it increasingly relies on advanced simulation, virtualized training, and assisted carrier landing technologies to prepare pilots for the demands of carrier operations. The JL-15, by contrast, is intended to support carrier-based pilot training. A dedicated carrier-capable trainer could offer China a more direct pathway for preparing pilots for operations aboard its increasingly sophisticated — and expanding — carrier fleet. Taken together, the PLAN aircraft being lined up for Zhuhai this year illustrate the increasingly sophisticated and integrated nature of China’s carrier aviation ambitions . As well as the aircraft carriers and their embarked aircraft, these ambitions also require other surface and subsurface vessels to operate effectively. Uncrewed systems will form another important part of the display. The exhibition will include aerial drones, uncrewed underwater vehicles, and other autonomous platforms, reflecting the PLAN’s growing interest in the potential of uncrewed warfare. Chinese media reports suggest that the WZ-2 uncrewed helicopter will receive its public debut at Zhuhai, while the PLAN may well also want to capitalize on its recent announcement that it had successfully launched and recovered a GJ-21 stealthy flying-wing uncrewed combat air vehicle (UCAV) aboard the Type 076 amphibious assault ship Sichuan . GJ-21. Chinese internet via X A chance to see the GJ-21 up close would be a huge deal, but there are many other naval drone options that could be revealed in more detail. There are likely to be more navalized collaborative combat aircraft (CCA) concepts and developments, especially since the adoption of the electromagnetic aircraft launch system (EMALS) catapult opens up a huge range of possibilities for uncrewed aircraft operating as part of a carrier air wing. Potentially, these could include the mysterious MQ-25-like drone that we recently discussed , the role of which remains unclear. On top of that, constant CCA testing at locations such as Malan suggests there could be much more to discuss than just the systems officially highlighted. Many other naval drones will surely be on display as well, including lower-end attritable concepts. Beyond static displays, China’s navy plans to organize flight demonstrations, formation flights, and simulated operational exercises. Its stated aim is to highlight not only the capabilities of individual platforms but also their ability to operate together in complex maritime environments. Photos have emerged showing apparent rehearsals for the display, presenting examples of the J-15, J-35, and KJ-600 to represent Beijing’s broader carrier air wing ecosystem. Two J-15s, two J-35s, and a KJ-600 purportedly taking part in a rehearsal for a formation fly-over at Zhuhai. Chinese internet via X It is not immediately clear which versions of the J-15 are participating in this formation flight: they could be J-15Ts, but another possibility is the electronic warfare version, the J-15DT , that we have profiled in the past. Regardless, they highlight how China’s carrier aviation ambitions are increasingly focused on catapult-assisted takeoff but arrested recovery (CATOBAR) operations, which offer many advantages . The J-15DT electronic warfare version of the Chinese carrier Flanker is outfitted for operations aboard catapult-equipped flattops like the Fujian . Chinese internet via X For the first time, the exhibition will also include a substantial surface fleet component, making use of the docks at the nearby Gaolan Port. Among the vessels expected to be featured are the Type 075 amphibious assault ship, the Type 055 guided-missile destroyer, and the Type 054A guided-missile frigate. Their presence will offer a public-facing showcase of China’s increasingly sophisticated surface fleet and its expanding range of maritime capabilities. It should also be recalled that it was at Gaolan Port where at least one Chinese uncrewed surface vessel , a distinctive trimaran craft, was first spotted. The Type 055 guided-missile destroyer Nanchang sails during the naval exercise Joint Sea-2021 on October 19, 2021, in the Western part of the Pacific Ocean. Photo by Sun Zifa/China News Service via Getty Images The broader messaging surrounding the exhibition is also notable. According to the PLAN, this year’s displays will place greater emphasis on operational readiness and training, with active-duty equipment that regularly participates in exercises and maritime security missions taking precedence over purely exhibition-oriented displays. This should underscore how Beijing has rapidly spun up its naval capabilities, introducing new and more capable equipment that is increasingly capable of more sustained out-of-area operations. The expanded naval presence at Zhuhai looks set to provide a substantial public showcase of China’s ongoing naval modernization. As well as the combination of the J-15T, J-35, KJ-600, and Z-20 variants, the JL-15 points to an increasingly comprehensive carrier aviation enterprise. And, judging by previous editions of the show, there will almost certainly be more novelties on display as well. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post China’s Naval Developments Set For The Spotlight At Zhuhai Airshow appeared first on TWZ .

title: Tai Po fire: Wang Fuk Court residents who sold titles excluded from third owners’ meeting next month
zh_title: 大埔火警：宏福苑卖业居民下月第三次业主大会被排除
summary: 政府指定的遭受火灾的宏福苑管理员已宣布下个月举行第三次业主会议，但已出售业权的居民除外。 2026 年 8 月 20 日，宏福苑周边地区仍被警方封锁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。合安管理公司周一宣布，宏福苑自去年11月致命大火以来的第三次业主大会将于12月6日在大埔社区中心举行。这场大火造成 168 人死亡，数千人流离失所，成为香港数十年来最致命的火灾之一。与过去两次见面不同
content:
政府指定的遭受火灾的宏福苑管理员已宣布下个月举行第三次业主会议，但已出售业权的居民除外。 2026 年 8 月 20 日，宏福苑周边地区仍被警方封锁。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。合安管理公司周一宣布，宏福苑自去年11月致命大火以来的第三次业主大会将于12月6日在大埔社区中心举行。这场大火造成 168 人死亡，数千人流离失所，成为香港数十年来最致命的火灾之一。与过去的两次会议不同的是，下个月的会议将在一个地点举行，这表明合安预计出席人数将会减少。过去两次会议是在四个场地进行转播，以容纳大量前宏福苑居民。消息公布后，一些根据政府回购计划出售公寓的居民被告知，他们将不再有资格参加业主会议。 HKFP看到，在通过在线系统发出的通知中，Hop On表示，未在土地注册处记录中列为公寓注册业主的居民将无法报名参加下个月的会议。政府表示，宏福苑共有1,984户业主，其中99.3%表示愿意根据回购计划出售业权，只有13户拒绝出售。
当局表示，他们计划最早于明年立法收购所有未售出的业权。2026 年 7 月 19 日，宏福苑居民参加在大埔社区中心举行的业主会议。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。居民正在签署正式销售协议，将其产权转让给政府，一些居民已经开始根据换屋安排选择新的政府补贴单位。但据一位吴姓居民表示，一些尚未正式转让产权的居民或许可以参加下个月的会议。吴周一告诉《香港新闻社》，她的家人原计划在本月底签署正式合同，但现在要等到下个月的会议之后。合安表示，会议议程将包括宏福苑财务状况报告、任命2026财年审计师的决定，以及可能出现的任何其他事务。

【原文 English Original】
The government-appointed administrator of fire-hit Wang Fuk Court has announced a third owners’ meeting next month, excluding residents who have sold their titles. The area surrounding Wang Fuk Court remains blocked by police force on August 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Hop On Management announced on Monday that the third Wang Fuk Court owners’ meeting since last November’s deadly blaze will be held on December 6 at the Tai Po Community Centre. The blaze killed 168 people and displaced thousands, making it one of Hong Kong’s deadliest fires in decades. In a departure from the past two meetings — which were broadcast across four venues to accommodate a large turnout of former Wang Fuk Court residents — next month’s meeting will take place at a single venue, signalling that Hop On anticipates lower attendance. Following the announcement, some residents who had sold their flats under a government buyback scheme were told they would no longer be eligible to attend the owners’ meeting. In a notice issued via an online system and seen by HKFP, Hop On said residents not listed as a flat’s registered owner in Land Registry records would be unable to sign up for next month’s meeting. The government has said 99.3 per cent of all 1,984 Wang Fuk Court homeowners have indicated they are willing to sell their titles under the buyback scheme, leaving only 13 households refusing to sell. Authorities have said they plan to introduce legislation as early as next year to acquire any unsold titles. Wang Fuk Court residents attend a flat owners meeting at Tai Po Community Centre on July 19, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Residents are in the process of signing formal sales agreements to transfer their titles to the government, and some have begun selecting new government-subsidised units under a flat-swap arrangement. But some residents who have yet to formalise their title transfer may be able to attend next month’s meeting, according to one resident surnamed Woo. Woo told HKFP on Monday that her family had planned to sign the formal contract at the end of this month, but would now wait until after next month’s meeting. Hop On said the meeting agenda will include a report on Wang Fuk Court’s financial status, a decision on the appointment of an auditor for the 2026 financial year, and any other business that may arise.

title: Hong Kong to impose citywide drone ban, harbour and road curbs for Interpol General Assembly next week
zh_title: 香港下周将在国际刑警组织大会上实施全市无人机禁令、港口和道路限制
summary: 香港将在下周主办国际刑警组织年度峰会时实施空中、海上和陆地限制，限制无人机和小型飞机的行动以及维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通。当局将于 2026 年 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日第 94 届国际刑警组织大会期间在整个香港空域设立临时飞行限制区。图片：截图来自香港警方。国际刑警组织第94届大会将于11月30日至12月3日在香港举行，与会代表
content:
香港将在下周主办国际刑警组织年度峰会时实施空中、海上和陆地限制，限制无人机和小型飞机的行动以及维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通。当局将于 2026 年 11 月 30 日至 12 月 3 日第 94 届国际刑警组织大会期间在整个香港空域设立临时飞行限制区。图片：截图来自香港警方。国际刑警组织第94届大会将于11月30日至12月3日在香港举行，来自196个成员国的代表将出席，探讨全球安全问题。警方行动组总警司黄志荣在周一的新闻发布会上表示，预计将有超过 1000 人参加此次活动，其中包括国际刑警组织成员国的警察局长以及政府高级官员。他表示，峰会期间，香港的整个空域将被指定为临时飞行限制区，禁止无人机、小型飞机和直升机以及滑翔伞、风筝和“大量气球”进行未经授权的操作。黄用粤语说：“但这些限制不会影响民用飞机的运营。”他补充说，民航处将向航空公司和飞行员公布航空限制的范围。
他警告居民，在下周的临时禁令期间，不要在未经许可的情况下操作无人机，并指出，根据《小型无人机令》，违法者最高可被处以10万港元罚款和两年监禁。 海上和陆地交通限制 当局将限制国际刑警组织峰会将在湾仔举行的香港会议展览中心附近的维多利亚港部分地区的海上交通，同时会场周围的道路也将被关闭。 2024 年 4 月 3 日，一名男子俯瞰香港维多利亚港。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港水上的士是一条深受游客欢迎的跨海路线，在峰会期间将跳过湾仔站。行人也将被禁止进入会展中心外的长廊。黄先生呼吁居民留意交通管制，提前计划出行。他还敦促船只和巴士运营商提前计划，避免在国际刑警组织峰会场地附近接送乘客。黄补充说，警方将在活动期间协调港口和会场附近的海上和陆地交通。这是香港首次主办国际刑警组织大会，也是该活动第三次在中国举办。北京分别于1995年和2017年举办过两次。
上周，香港警方在邻近的中国城市深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织峰会期间逮捕了五名非法无人机操作男子，此前当局在香港北部领空的大部分地区实施了为期四天的禁飞区。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong will enforce air, sea and land restrictions when it hosts Interpol’s annual summit next week, limiting drone and small-aircraft operations as well as marine traffic in parts of Victoria Harbour. Authorities will impose a temporary restricted flying zone across the entire Hong Kong airspace for the duration of the 94th Interpol General Assembly from November 30 to December 3, 2026. Photo: Screenshot, via Hong Kong Police. The 94th International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) General Assembly is set to take place in Hong Kong from November 30 to December 3, with representatives from 196 member countries expected to attend to address global security issues. Wong Chi-wing, chief superintendent of the police’s operations wing, told a press conference on Monday that more than 1,000 people are expected to attend the event, including the police chiefs of Interpol’s member countries as well as senior government officials. He said Hong Kong’s entire airspace would be designated a temporary restricted flying zone for the duration of the summit, barring unauthorised operations of drones, small aircraft and helicopters, as well as paragliders, kites and “large numbers of balloons.” “But the restrictions will not affect civil aircraft operations,” Wong said in Cantonese, adding that the Civil Aviation Department would publicise the scope of the air restrictions for airlines and pilots. He warned residents against operating drones without a permit during the temporary ban next week, noting that offenders face a maximum penalty of a HK$100,000 fine and two years’ imprisonment under the Small Unmanned Aircraft Order. Sea and land traffic curbs Authorities will restrict marine traffic in parts of Victoria Harbour off the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai, where the Interpol summit will take place, while roads surrounding the venue will also be closed. A man looks out over Victoria Harbour in Hong Kong, on April 3, 2024. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Hong Kong Water Taxi, a cross-harbour route popular with tourists, will skip its Wan Chai stop for the duration of the summit. Pedestrians will also be barred from entering the promenade outside the convention and exhibition centre. Wong urged residents to take note of the traffic restrictions and plan their journeys in advance. He also urged boat and bus operators to plan ahead and avoid picking up or dropping off passengers near the Interpol summit venue. Police will coordinate sea and land traffic in the harbour and near the venue for the duration of the event, Wong added. This will be the first time Hong Kong hosts the Interpol General Assembly and the third time the event has taken place in China. Beijing hosted it twice, in 1995 and 2017. Last week, Hong Kong police arrested five men over illegal drone operations during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the neighbouring Chinese city of Shenzhen, after authorities imposed a four-day restricted flying zone across much of Hong Kong’s northern airspace.

title: Beijing hails ‘healthy competition’ after small-circle vote for body that selects Hong Kong’s leader
zh_title: 在小圈子投票选出香港领导人后，北京赞扬“良性竞争”
summary: 北京负责香港事务的最高机构对周日小圈选举委员会竞选的投票率创历史新高表示欢迎，一些重量级候选人意外落选。 2026年11月22日，选举管理委员会主席乐大卫（右二）与政制及内地事务局局长谢淑丽（左二）在香港会议展览中心举行的2026年选举委员会界别分组一般选举中央点票站清空投票箱。图片：香港政府一站通。国家港澳事务办公室
content:
北京负责香港事务的最高机构对周日小圈选举委员会竞选的投票率创历史新高表示欢迎，一些重量级候选人意外落选。 2026年11月22日，选举管理委员会主席乐大卫（右二）与政制及内地事务局局长谢淑丽（左二）在香港会议展览中心举行的2026年选举委员会界别分组一般选举中央点票站清空投票箱。图片：香港政府一站通。中国国务院港澳事务办公室周一表示，组建负责选举香港领导人的强大选举委员会的竞争体现了“良性竞争”。只有一小部分香港人口有资格在周日的选举中投票，5,709 名符合资格的选民中有 5,640 人参加了投票，投票率达到创纪录的 98.8%。整个香港约有410万登记选民。周日共有 856 名候选人角逐 31 个界别分组的 723 个议席。另外 259 个席位没有竞争，其中 362 个席位由当然成员填补，156 个席位由指定机构的代表填补。他们将共同组成由 1,500 人组成的选举委员会，该委员会将在明年的行政长官选举中进行提名和投票。它还将在2029年的下一次立法会选举中提名和选举90名立法会议员中的40名。
港澳事务办公室发言人周一在一份中文声明中表示，“这次选举委员会竞选再次体现了新选举制度的广泛代表性、政治包容性、均衡参与性、公平竞争性。”该发言人表示，“这次选举真正实现了‘选贤任能’的目标。”选举管理委员会主席乐大卫（中）于2026年11月22日在选举事务处首席选举主任（策划及研究）赵博恩（右）陪同下参观位于港湾道体育馆的2026年选举委员会界别分组一般选举投票站，了解选举活动的情况。图片：香港政府一站通。自北京于2021年彻底改革香港选举制度以确保只有“爱国者”治理香港以来，周日的选举是强大的选举委员会的第二次选举。 2021年3月，北京通过立法，确保“爱国者”治理香港。此举减少了立法机构中的民主代表性，加强了对选举的控制，并引入了一个亲北京的审查小组来选择候选人。当局表示，此次整顿确保了这座城市的稳定和繁荣。但这些变化也引发了国际社会的谴责，因为许多传统反对派仍然身陷囹圄、自我流放或退出政坛。
解说：北京的选举改革 解说：新的选举规则 但周日的竞选也给一些政治重量级人物带来了意外的损失。令人意外的是，香港律师会会长汤智恩未能在 15 名议员的法律界界别分组中获得席位，而香港总商会首席执行官杨伟雄也在 17 名商业（第一）界别分组的竞标中落败。周日，多名富豪和商界领袖当选，其中包括盈科拓展集团主席李泽楷、香港首富李嘉诚的小儿子和信和集团董事长。

【原文 English Original】
Beijing’s top body overseeing Hong Kong affairs has hailed the record turnout in Sunday’s small-circle Election Committee race, which saw some heavyweight candidates suffer surprise losses. Electoral Affairs Commission (EAC) chair David Lok (second right), and the Secretary for Constitutional and Mainland Affairs, Janice Tse (second left), empty a ballot box at the Central Counting Station of the 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections located at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre on November 22, 2026. Photo: GovHK. The Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council, China’s cabinet, said on Monday that the race to form the powerful Election Committee tasked with choosing the city’s leader embodied “healthy competition.” Only a tiny fraction of Hong Kong’s population was eligible to vote in Sunday’s race, in which 5,640 of 5,709 eligible electors cast ballots — a record-breaking 98.8 per cent turnout. Hong Kong as a whole has about 4.1 million registered voters. A total of 856 candidates were vying for 723 seats across 31 subsectors on Sunday. A further 259 seats were uncontested while 362 were filled by ex-officio members and 156 by representatives of designated bodies. Together they will form the 1,500-strong Election Committee, which will nominate and vote in next year’s chief executive election. It will also nominate and elect 40 of the 90 lawmakers in the next Legislative Council election in 2029. “This Election Committee race once again demonstrates the broad representativeness, political inclusiveness, balanced participation, and fair competition of the new electoral system,” a spokesperson for the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office said in a Chinese-language statement on Monday. “This race truly achieves the goal of ‘selecting the virtuous and capable,'” the spokesperson said. Electoral Affairs Commission chair David Lok (centre), accompanied by the Principal Electoral Officer (Planning and Research) of the Registration and Electoral Office, Brian Chiu (right), visits the polling station of the 2026 Election Committee Subsector Ordinary Elections located at Harbour Road Sports Centre to observe how electoral activities are conducted on November 22, 2026. Photo: GovHK. Sunday’s race was the second for the powerful Election Committee since Beijing overhauled Hong Kong’s electoral system in 2021 to ensure only “patriots” govern the city. In March 2021, Beijing passed legislation to ensure “patriots” govern Hong Kong . The move reduced democratic representation in the legislature, tightened control of elections and introduced a pro-Beijing vetting panel to select candidates. Authorities say the overhaul ensures the city’s stability and prosperity . But the changes also prompted international condemnation , as much of the traditional opposition remains behind bars , in self-exile or has quit politics. Explainer: Beijing’s electoral overhaul Explainer: New electoral rules But Sunday’s race also returned unexpected losses for some political heavyweights. In a surprise upset, Law Society of Hong Kong president Roden Tong failed to secure a seat in the 15-member legal subsector, while Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce CEO Patrick Yeung also fell short in his bid for the 17-strong commercial (first) subsector. Multiple tycoons and business leaders were elected on Sunday, including Pacific Century Group chair Richard Li, the younger son of Hong Kong’s wealthiest person, Li Ka-shing, and Sino Group chair Daryl Ng.

title: Hong Kong police arrest 38-year-old man over fatal Tsim Sha Tsui crash that killed Muslim community leader
zh_title: 香港警方因尖沙咀车祸导致穆斯林社区领袖死亡而逮捕38岁男子
summary: 周日，一辆汽车在尖沙咀驶上人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤，警方拘捕一名涉嫌酒后驾驶及危险驾驶致人死亡的38岁男子。 2026 年 11 月 22 日星期日下午 2:30 左右，一辆汽车冲上普拉特大道 (Prat Avenue) 的人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤。照片：由詹姆斯·奥肯登提供。据警方新闻稿称，事件发生在下午 2:30 左右，发生在 Prat Avenue。当地媒体分享了闭路电视和旁观者的镜头，显示司机和一名女乘客在事发后试图逃离现场。
content:
周日，一辆汽车在尖沙咀驶上人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤，警方拘捕一名涉嫌酒后驾驶及危险驾驶致人死亡的38岁男子。 2026 年 11 月 22 日星期日下午 2:30 左右，一辆汽车冲上普拉特大道 (Prat Avenue) 的人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤。照片：由詹姆斯·奥肯登提供。据警方新闻稿称，事件发生在下午 2:30 左右，发生在 Prat Avenue。当地媒体分享了闭路电视和旁观者的镜头，显示司机和一名女乘客在事故发生后试图逃离现场。总督察刘家恒在周日的警方新闻发布会上表示，有几名公众跟踪司机并向当局报警。 2026 年 11 月 22 日，总督察刘家恒（左）在新闻发布会上。图片：香港警务处截图，来自 Facebook。新闻稿称，一名53岁男性行人在昏迷不醒的情况下被送往伊丽莎白女王医院，并于下午3时23分证实死亡。新闻稿称：“经进一步调查，该名38岁私家车男司机因酒后驾驶及危险驾驶致人死亡被捕，现被拘留调查。” 2026 年 11 月 22 日星期日下午 2:30 左右，一辆汽车冲上普拉特大道 (Prat Avenue) 的人行道，造成一人死亡、三人受伤。照片：由詹姆斯·奥肯登提供。
警方补充，一名62岁非华裔男性行人头部受伤，两名年龄分别为31岁和70岁的女性行人四肢受伤。三人均在神志清醒的情况下被送往伊利沙伯医院。事故发生后，人行道和路边看到一串损坏的自行车、碎片和破损的栏杆。穆斯林领袖被杀 香港穆斯林理事会在社交媒体上发布的帖子称，受害者是当地主要伊斯兰教育组织 Khatme Nubuwwat 伊斯兰理事会有限公司的副主席贾维德·马哈茂德 (Javed Mahmood)。屏幕截图：香港穆斯林理事会，来自 X。酒后驾驶的最高处罚是罚款 25,000 港元和监禁三年。危险驾驶致人死亡罪名成立，可判处十年监禁及罚款港币五万元。没有报告交通意外亦违反《道路交通条例》。然而，警方周一告诉香港新闻社，目前还没有关于被捕男子可能面临的指控的最新消息。致命车祸发生后的第二天，警方的 Instagram 页面上出现了一幅人工智能生成的漫画，上面写着“现实生活不是游戏。喝酒吗？不要开车”，这显然是对新发布的视频游戏《侠盗猎车手 VI》的模仿。西九龙交通部第一特别调查队正调查案件。目击者或任何知情者请致电 3661 9188 与警方联系。

【原文 English Original】
Police have arrested a 38-year-old man on suspicion of drink-driving and dangerous driving causing death after a vehicle mounted a pavement in Tsim Sha Tsui on Sunday, leaving one person dead and three injured. A vehicle mounted a pavement on Prat Avenue at around 2:30pm on Sunday, November 22, 2026, leaving one dead and three injured. Photo: Courtesy of James Ockenden. The incident took place on Prat Avenue at around 2:30pm, according to a police press release. Local media shared CCTV and bystander footage appearing to show the driver and a female passenger attempting to flee the scene after the crash. Speaking at a police press briefing on Sunday, Chief Inspector Lau Ka-hang said several members of the public followed the driver and alerted authorities. Chief Inspector Lau Ka-hang (left) at a press briefing on November 22, 2026. Photo: HKPF screenshot, via Facebook. The press release said a 53-year-old male pedestrian was rushed to Queen Elizabeth Hospital unconscious and was certified dead at 3:23pm. “After further investigations, the 38-year-old private car male driver was arrested for drink driving and dangerous driving causing death and is being detained for enquiries,” the press release said. A vehicle mounted a pavement on Prat Avenue at around 2:30pm on Sunday, November 22, 2026, leaving one dead and three injured. Photo: Courtesy of James Ockenden. Police added that a 62-year-old non-ethnic Chinese male pedestrian sustained head injuries, while two female pedestrians, aged 31 and 70, suffered limb injuries. All three were taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in a conscious state. A trail of damaged bicycles, debris and mangled railings was seen across the pavement and roadside following the crash. Muslim leader killed Social media posts by the Muslim Council of Hong Kong identified the victim as Javed Mahmood, the vice-chair of Khatme Nubuwwat Islamic Council Limited, a major local Islamic education organisation. Screenshot: Muslim Council of Hong Kong, via X. The maximum penalty for drink-driving is a HK$25,000 fine and three years behind bars. Those convicted of causing death by dangerous driving face 10 years’ imprisonment and a HK$50,000 fine. Failing to report a traffic accident is also a breach of the Road Traffic Ordinance. However, police told HKFP on Monday that there was no update yet on the charges the arrested man might face. A day after the fatal crash, an AI-generated cartoon appeared on the police Instagram page stating that “real life is not gaming. Drank? Don’t drive,” in an apparent parody of the newly released video game Grand Theft Auto VI. Special Investigation Team 1 of Traffic Kowloon West is investigating the case. Witnesses or anyone with information are urged to contact officers on 3661 9188.

title: Hong Kong cinema takes spotlight at Taiwan’s Golden Horse film awards
zh_title: 香港电影在台湾金马奖上备受瞩目
summary: 周日，两部受香港民主运动启发的电影在台湾金马奖上获奖，其中一部获奖感言献给了“监狱里的人”。 2026 年 11 月 22 日，在台北举行的第 63 届台湾金马奖颁奖典礼上，香港女演员袁咏仪凭借电影《余韵》获得最佳女主角奖后摆姿势拍照。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/法新社。 《三只小猪》是一部黑色幽默电影，讲述了香港两个青少年偷猪头的故事，在这场被誉为华语电影的盛会上获得了最佳真人短片奖。
content:
周日，两部受香港民主运动启发的电影在台湾金马奖上获奖，其中一部获奖感言献给了“监狱里的人”。 2026 年 11 月 22 日，在台北举行的第 63 届台湾金马奖颁奖典礼上，香港女演员袁咏仪凭借电影《余韵》获得最佳女主角奖后摆姿势拍照。照片：I-Hwa Cheng/法新社。 《三只小猪》是一部黑色幽默电影，讲述了香港两名青少年偷猪头的故事，在这场被誉为华语奥斯卡的盛会上获得了最佳真人短片奖。 《出发的场景》探讨了一位香港电影制片人和他关系疏远的父亲之间的关系，该片赢得了最佳纪录片奖。故事背景是 2019 年该市发生大规模、有时甚至是暴力的民主抗议活动。次年，北京实施了一项国家安全法，批评者称该法压制了异议。香港随后于 2024 年颁布了一项本土法规，用于审判活动人士和抗议领袖。 《三只小猪》的代表罗安迪周日在台上代表导演锺锦尼和其他剧组人员发表获奖感言时表示：“也许我们的作品会在一瞬间被监狱里的人看到，成为他们心中微小而坚定的光芒，成为真正的陪伴。” “我想把这个奖项献给每一位曾经或仍在监狱里的‘小猪’。
我们将来还会见面的。”另一部香港电影《生来就好》（讲述了一名前囚犯在城里遇见了一位苦苦挣扎的年轻演员的故事）获得了最佳影片和最佳原创剧本奖。台湾导演徐震杰凭借《双喜》击败了日本资深导演田中宏之（专业名称为“萨布”），夺得最佳导演奖。自从一名台湾导演在 2018 年的获奖感言中表示支持台湾独立以来，“非常自豪”的中国导演和一线明星基本上回避了金马奖。北京声称自治民主的台湾是其领土的一部分，在两地政治紧张局势加剧之际，2019 年禁止演艺人员参加金马奖。尽管如此，许多香港明星还是出现在今年台北颁奖典礼的红地毯上。另请参阅：香港电影无视警告，在台湾金马奖上强势亮相 凭借《余韵》中的表演获得最佳女主角的袁安琪表示，她“非常自豪”能够成为“众多获奖的香港电影人之一”。台湾刘冠廷凭借《双喜》获得最佳男主角奖。香港演员兼男子组合成员江业生凭借《我们什么都不是》中的角色获得最佳男配角奖。台湾演员、两届金马奖得主舒淇凭借《女孩》获得最佳新人导演奖，这是她受自己童年启发的导演处女作。
首次担任颁奖典礼主持人的香港演员威尔·柯表示：“今年入围的影片来自各地……金马奖真是汇聚了各地的华语电影。”好莱坞明星赞达亚、杰森·莫玛惊喜现身，与《沙丘》搭档、金马主席张震一起通过视频亮相，共同颁奖。

【原文 English Original】
Two films inspired by Hong Kong’s pro-democracy movement won gongs at Taiwan’s Golden Horse Awards on Sunday, with one acceptance speech dedicated to “those in prison”. Hong Kong actress Angela Yuen poses for photos after winning Best Leading Actress for the movie Afterpiece at Taiwan’s 63rd Golden Horse film awards ceremony, in Taipei on November 22, 2026. Photo: I-Hwa Cheng/AFP. “Three Little Pigs”, a dark-humour film about two teenagers in Hong Kong on a mission to steal a pig’s head, picked up the prize for best live action short film at the prestigious event, dubbed the Chinese-language Oscars. “Scenes from Departure”, which explores the relationship between a Hong Kong filmmaker and his estranged father, won best documentary feature. It is set against the backdrop of the city’s huge and sometimes violent pro-democracy protests in 2019. The following year, Beijing imposed a national security law that critics say has quelled dissent. Hong Kong then enacted a homegrown code in 2024, with both used to try activists and protest leaders. Andy Law, a representative for “Three Little Pigs” delivering an acceptance speech on behalf of director Chung Kam-nei and other crew members, said on stage on Sunday: “Maybe in one instant our work will be seen by those in prison, becoming a small yet unwavering light for them, and genuine companionship.” “I want to dedicate this award to every ‘little pig’ who has been or is still in prison. We’ll see each other in the future.” Another Hong Kong film, “We Are Born Good” — about a former prisoner who meets a struggling young actor in the city — won best film and best original screenplay. Taiwanese director Joseph Hsu Chen-chieh bagged the best director award for “Double Happiness”, beating veteran Japanese director Hiroyuki Tanaka, known professionally as Sabu. ‘Very proud’ Chinese directors and A-listers have largely shunned the Golden Horse Awards since a Taiwanese director voiced support for the island’s independence in an acceptance speech in 2018. Beijing, which claims self-ruled democratic Taiwan as part of its territory, banned entertainers from attending the event in 2019 at a time of rising political tensions between the two sides. Still, many Hong Kong stars were spotted on the red carpet for this year’s ceremony in Taipei. See also: Hong Kong films defy warnings with strong presence at Taiwan’s Golden Horse awards Angela Yuen, who won best leading actress for her performance in “Afterpiece”, said she was “very proud” to be among “many Hong Kong filmmakers who won awards”. Taiwan’s Liu Kuan-ting won best leading actor for “Double Happiness”. Hong Kong actor and boy band member Anson Kong Ip-sang picked up the prize for best supporting actor for his role in “We’re Nothing at All”. Taiwanese actor and two-time Golden Horse winner Shu Qi won best new director for “Girl”, her directorial debut inspired by her own childhood. “This year quite a lot of the nominated films come from everywhere… the Golden Horse Awards really bring together Chinese-language films from different places,” said Hong Kong actor Will Or, who made his debut as host of the ceremony. In a surprise appearance, Hollywood stars Zendaya and Jason Momoa joined via video to jointly present an award with their “Dune” co-star and Golden Horse chairman Chang Chen.

title: USNI News Fleet and Marine Tracker: Nov. 23, 2026
zh_title: USNI 新闻舰队和海军陆战队追踪器：2026 年 11 月 23 日

Murtha (LPD-26) 和登船的第 13 海军陆战队远征部队。2026 年 11 月 8 日，在佛罗里达州梅波特，分配给自由型濒海战斗舰圣路易斯号 (LCS-19) 的一级消防员大卫·罗宾逊 (David Robinson) 在该船从大沼泽港出发时收起系泊缆。美国海军照片 濒海战斗舰 USS 明尼阿波利斯-圣保罗号(LCS-21) 和圣路易斯号 (LCS-19) 被分配给美国南方司令部，但目前停泊在佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地的港口。2026 年 11 月 13 日，土耳其海军 SH-70 直升机在地中海“马维·巴利纳”演习的摄影演习中编队飞过阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰布尔克利号 (DDG-84)。在地中海作战的独立部署的导弹驱逐舰包括：美国海军奥斯卡·奥斯汀号（DDG-79），母港为罗塔海军基地。 USS Bulkeley (DDG-84)，母港为罗塔海军基地。 2026 年 11 月 21 日，红海，一名水手在阿利·伯克级导弹驱逐舰“冈萨雷斯”号 (DDG-66) 上夜间使用六分仪观测月亮。美国海军照片 有两艘导弹驱逐舰在红海作业：“杰森·邓纳姆”号 (DDG-109)，母港为佛罗里达州梅波特海军基地。“冈萨雷斯”号 (DDG-66)，母港位于弗吉尼亚州诺福克海军基地。在阿拉伯海，一名水手观察刘易斯和克拉克级干货船美国海军塞萨尔·查韦斯号 (T-AKE-14) 与尼米兹级航空母舰乔治·H·W·布什号并肩航行。

content:
2026 年 11 月 7 日，美国海军陆战队部队侦察连、第 2 侦察营、第 2 海军陆战师在芬兰南部海岸的北约增强警戒活动波罗的海哨兵期间进行船只行动。美国海军陆战队照片 作为芬兰海军演习和北约增强警戒活动 (eVA) 波罗的海哨兵的一部分，四打海军陆战队侦察兵本周将在芬兰执行任务。芬兰海军的窄水域 26-2 演习将于周三在芬兰南部沿海地区和芬兰湾开始。此次演习将持续到12月。 4. 此次演习是芬兰海军秋季的主要演习，芬兰海军舰艇和部队与北约盟国在波罗的海北部及其沿岸进行联合海军作战训练。据芬兰海军新闻稿称，除了芬兰人员、船只和飞机外，爱沙尼亚海军指挥和支援舰EML Wambola (A433)以及约50名美国海军陆战队人员也将参加此次演习。这支海军陆战队共有四​​打成员，来自海军陆战队第二师第二侦察营和驻扎在北卡罗来纳州勒琼海军陆战队基地的第二海军陆战队远征军信息大队。该大队于 10 月初在欧洲海军陆战队轮调部队 (MRF-E) 的指挥下进行前沿部署，当时他们的任务是向芬兰提供先进的远征监视和战术侦察能力，同时与波罗的海哨兵指挥下的终点海岸旅一起作战。
该部队部署的能力包括 Stalker VXE-30 无人机系统 (UAS)。芬兰国防军和边防部队的约 3,500 名人员，包括应征入伍者和预备役军人，正在参加“狭窄水域 26-2”行动。新闻稿中写道：“这次演习是测试 12 月份应征入伍的部队组成技能的机会，也是训练预备役人员执行战时任务的机会。”芬兰陆军和芬兰空军将在南海岸和波罗的海北部利用直升机、战斗机和无人系统进行与演习相关的飞行活动。美国海军陆战队参谋中士。巴尼·南 (Barney South) 是海军陆战队第二师第二侦察营第二部队侦察连的一名海军陆战队队员，在 2026 年 5 月 22 日于芬兰穆斯塔马举行的狭窄水域 26 演习中，在两栖插入期间占据安全位置。 美国海军陆战队照片 芬兰海军还将利用这次演习让芬兰公司测试新技术，包括各种无人系统以及监视和保护设备。海军操作环境。该军种将收集演习的反馈，用它来评估测试系统对海军防御的贡献。演习结束后，美国海军陆战队将恢复参加自10月以来一直在进行的波罗的海哨兵活动。
北约于 2025 年 1 月启动了波罗的海哨兵，以阻止进一步破坏波罗的海关键水下基础设施的企图。根据美国海军陆战队在北约演习中发布的信息，在 10 月份的波罗的海哨兵期间，美国海军陆战队与芬兰部队合作提供远征监视和战术侦察能力，加强海域意识并支持保护重要海底基础设施的努力。 “这一努力展示了海军陆战队远征能力如何补充盟军海上力量、提高信息能力

【原文 English Original】
U.S. Marines with Force Reconnaissance Company, 2d Reconnaissance Battalion, 2d Marine Division, conduct boat operations during NATO Enhanced Vigilance Activity Baltic Sentry off the coast of southern Finland, Nov. 7, 2026. US Marine Corps photo Four dozen Reconnaissance Marines will operate in Finland this week as part of a Finnish naval exercise and NATO’s enhanced Vigilant Activity (eVA) Baltic Sentry. The Finnish Navy’s Narrow Waters 26-2 drill will begin Wednesday in the coastal areas of Southern Finland and in the Gulf of Finland. The exercise will run throughDec. 4. The exercise is the Finnish Navy’s main exercise in autumn and involves Finnish Navy ships and troops and NATO allies training in combined naval operations in the northern Baltic Sea and its coast. In addition to Finnish personnel, ships and aircraft, Estonian Navy command and support ship EML Wambola (A433) and about 50 U.S. Marine Corps personnel will participate in the exercise, according to a Finnish Navy news release . The Marine force –four dozen members – are from 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division and II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group based out of Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, N.C. The group were forward deployed in early October under Marine Rotational Force-Europe (MRF-E) when they were tasked to Finland to provide advanced expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities while operating alongside the Finish Coastal Brigade under Baltic Sentry. The capabilities fielded by the unit include the Stalker VXE-30 Unmanned Aerial System (UAS). Approximately 3,500 personnel, including conscripts and reservists, of the Finnish Defense Forces and Border Guard are participating in Narrow Waters 26-2. “The exercise is an opportunity to test the skills of conscripts mustering out in December in their unit compositions, and train reservists for their wartime tasks,” reads the release. The Finnish Army and Finnish Air Force will conduct exercise-related flight activity with helicopters, fighters and unmanned systems on the south coast and northern Baltic Sea. U.S. Marine Corps Staff Sgt. Barney South, a force reconnaissance Marine with 2nd Force Reconnaissance Company, 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, holds a security position during an amphibious insertion as part of exercise Narrow Waters 26 in Mustamaa, Finland, May 22, 2026. US Marine Corps photo The Finnish Navy will also use the exercise to have Finnish companies test new technology, including various unmanned systems and surveillance and protection equipment, in a naval operating environment. The service will collect feedback from the exercise, using it to assess the contribution of the tested systems to naval defense. Following completion of the exercise, the U.S. Marines will resume their participation in Baltic Sentry activities, which has been ongoing since October. NATO launched Baltic Sentry in January of 2025 to deter further attempts to damage critical underwater infrastructure in the Baltic Sea. During Baltic Sentry in October, U.S. Marines worked alongside Finnish forces to provide expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities, strengthening maritime domain awareness and supporting efforts to protect critical undersea infrastructure, according to a U.S. Marine Corps release on the NATO exercise. “The effort demonstrated how Marine Corps expeditionary capabilities can complement Allied maritime forces, improve information sharing, and contribute to security across the Baltic maritime environment,” reads the release. U.S. Marine Corps Major General Daniel Shipley, Commander, U.S. Marine Corps Forces Europe and Africa, met with Rear Admiral Tuomas Tiilikainen, Commander of the Finnish Navy on Nov. 6 in Finland to discuss NATO interoperability, the U.S.-Finnish defense relationship and the role of combined forces in defending the Alliance’s northern and eastern flanks, according to the release. The engagement highlighted the ongoing partnership between the U.S. Marine Corps and Finnish Navy and the importance of integrating capabilities within a broader Nordic force prepared to defend NATO territory, reads the release. U.S. Marines with 2nd Force Reconnaissance Company, 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, board a U-600 Jurmo LCP Watercat M12 during Finnish weapons and boat familiarization training as part of exercise Narrow Waters 26 in Upinniemi, Finland, May 15, 2026. US Marine Corps photo In Narrow Waters 26.2, Finnish, Estonian and U.S. forces will train together to refine maritime command and control, reconnaissance, fire coordination and Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear (CBRN) defense. The exercise is meant to strengthen participants’ ability to share information, synchronize operations and integrate complementary capabilities in a complex maritime environment, reads the release. “When Allies train together in demanding environments, we build the trust, capability, and combat credibility required to operate as one combined force,” said Shipley in the release. “Our Finnish allies are highly capable. The [U.S] Marines are here to sharpen interoperability with Finnish and Estonian allies, strengthen maritime readiness, and ensure our Alliance remains prepared to meet any challenge.” Finnish, Estonian and U.S. personnel will train at the task group, task unit and unit levels to strengthen coordination and improve their ability to operate together. The Recon Marines will contribute reconnaissance, fires liaison and coordination, command and control, and CBRN defense capabilities. “These contributions will help participating forces strengthen maritime domain awareness, integrate air and missile defense, coordinate strike capabilities, and rehearse responses to CBRN threats,” reads the release. As part of its transition to Force Design 2030, the Marine Corps has not only been carrying out training in distributed and dispersed operations in the Indo-Pacific but also in Northern Europe. Along with participation in Baltic Sentry, the service deployed expeditionary long-range missile systems to Norway in August and September under Operation Atlantic City 26 . The Marine Corps also continues to carry out conventional warfare training in Norway with 3,000 Marines deploying to Norway in March for exercise Cold Response .

Philippine marines assigned to 4th Marine Brigade, and U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, participate in a cumulative training event for maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes Islands, Philippines, June 25, 2026. US Marine Corps photo MANILA, Philippines — The U.S. pledged to grant a $2 billion foreign military financing loan package for Manila’s military modernization efforts and the development of an airport in the Luzon Strait. The targeted defense assistance was one of several deals inked last week during President Donald Trump’s visit to the Philippines for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations’ annual summit. Announced alongside Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., these deals mark a drastic increase in Washington’s commitment to its longtime Indo-Pacific ally. The $2 billion in defense loans will be made available for the Philippines covering the sale of “critical defense and security capabilities from U.S. suppliers,” according to the White House. “The United States will utilize $400 million in [foreign military financing] for the Philippine military to expand its operational reach and deterrence capabilities in the South China Sea, including long-range fires, command and control, critical infrastructure and multi-domain drones, supporting 1,500 American jobs,” reads the White House’s release on the Manila deals. The Philippines has received considerable proposals from Lockheed Martin covering a variety of systems, including M142 High Mobility Rocket Systems and F-16V Viper fighter jets, USNI News understands. Additionally, the defense prime partnered with Gibbs and Cox to arm its International-class frigate design, which has been pitched to the Philippine Navy. Manila previously voiced interest in procuring Lockheed Martin’s Mid-Range Capability, a ground-based Mark 41 vertical launching system that the U.S. Army has had forward deployed in the Philippines since April of 2024. American aid packages contributing to Manila’s nascent Asymmetric Capabilities Program , an unmanned systems mesh network, involve drone firms Maritime Tactical Systems, Inc. and Ocean Aero. U.S. defense officials previously told USNI News that attack drones will be transferred next year. Beyond the loans, defense infrastructure developments at Subic Bay and the Batanes Islands were also announced in the White House release. These include a fuel storage facility worth $40 million at Subic Bay, the site of a former U.S. Navy base that has been increasingly tapped by Washington in its regional deterrence efforts. Since 2022, almost every branch of the U.S. military has staged forces and supplies at Subic Bay. In recent years, the U.S. Army and the U.S. Marine Corps contracted storage facilities for vehicles and supplies around the strategic bay. This summer saw the U.S. Coast Guard stage cutters at a pier across from the Philippine Navy’s primary base. U.S. Marines assigned to 3rd Littoral Combat Team, 3rd Marine Littoral Regiment, 3rd Marine Division, unload a Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction System from a KC-130J Super Hercules assigned to Marine Aerial Refueler Transport Squadron (VMGR) 152, Marine Aircraft Group 12, 1st Marine Aircraft Wing, for maritime key terrain security operations during KAMANDAG 10 at Itbayat, Batanes Islands, Philippines, June 19, 2026. US Marine Corps photos In the middle of the Luzon Strait, the allies plan to increase their “operational access” through the modernization of Basco Airport. Located within 100 miles of Taiwan, the airport is in an area that would become crucial in a potential cross strait conflict. Since 2025, the U.S. Marine Corps has used the airport to insert maritime sensing teams and anti-ship missile-equipped Navy-Marine Expeditionary Ship Interdiction Systems. From the Batanes Islands, Washington and Manila can lock down the strategic first island chain chokepoint. U.S. and Philippine Marines have practiced delivering missile systems and setting up ground-based radar nodes across the archipelago. One of these maritime domain awareness teams emplaced on an island only 88 miles away from Taiwan during an exercise in 2024.

Tad DeHaven 11 月 12 日，特朗普总统表示，英伟达“只有一个人”取代黄仁勋。他指的是苹果前首席执行官蒂姆·库克。 11 天后，英伟达宣布黄仁勋复职，特朗普对 CNBC 表示，“我做了这笔交易。”  为什么总统要达成这样的协议？黄在承认与一名涉嫌与中国情报部门有联系的女性有染后辞职。两位英伟达股东敦促董事会对让他回归持开放态度。一名英伟达员工建立了一个网站，人们可以在上面签署一封呼吁他回归的信。股东和员工完全有权向董事们提出自己的理由，而董事们已于 11 月 17 日告诉投资者，他们无意恢复黄的职位。英伟达董事会也有充分的理由询问联邦官员对可疑情报行动的了解。根据董事会的声明，政府的回答缓解了他们对国家安全的担忧。他们还会见了黄，并表示他们对他能够领导公司感到满意，尽管他们自己的调查仍在进行中。但特朗普向他们施压，要求他们恢复黄的职位，从而越界了。任何仍然认为让黄回来是一个错误的董事都被迫权衡英伟达违抗总统可能付出的代价。这让人有理由怀疑英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的决定是否真的正确。如果董事会的内部调查发现更多涉及黄的令人不安的信息，会发生什么？
特朗普宣称其复职对美国繁荣至关重要，它会不愿意对这位首席执行官采取行动吗？当 CNBC 的萨拉·艾森问特朗普他的底线在哪里时，他回答说：“我是为了国家而这样做。”用特朗普的话说，美国的繁荣取决于黄仁勋掌管英伟达。难怪吉姆·克莱默在同一次电话会议上询问，如果该公司陷入财务困境，华盛顿是否会提供援助。特朗普表示，他认为事情不会发展到这个地步，但他正在回答有关一家上季度盈利 653 亿美元的公司的救助问题。我们已经看到，当华盛顿认定一家公司太重要而不能倒闭时，董事会会发生什么。 2009年，通用汽车依靠联邦救助维持生存，奥巴马政府罢免了首席执行官里克·瓦格纳，并任命了他的继任者弗里茨·亨德森。亨德森后来告诉调查人员，通用汽车的董事认为财政部篡夺了他们选择首席执行官的权力。美国政府已经对英伟达的业务拥有足够的发言权，可以要求削减对中国的某些芯片销售。下次特朗普向黄求助时，他可以提醒黄是谁帮助他重新获得了工作。正如我的同事斯科特·林西科姆 (Scott Lincicome) 今天指出的那样，这种干预的经济成本比周一英伟达股价的上涨更难以看出。以英特尔为例。 2025 年 8 月，特朗普因首席执行官陈立武 (Lip-Bu Tan) 与中国的关系而要求他辞职。
谭匆匆赶到白宫，特朗普说他在那里告诉他，“如果你聪明的话，就把你公司 10% 的股份交给美国。”谭保住了他的工作，联邦政府成为英特尔股东。同月，蒂姆·库克前往白宫寻求苹果的关税豁免。正如斯科特所记录的那样，据报道，特朗普和商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克向库克施压，要求英特尔生产一些苹果芯片。苹果获得了豁免。十个月后，特朗普将他所说的苹果和英特尔之间的交易归功于自己。 “我们是

【原文 English Original】
Tad DeHaven On November 12, President Trump said there was “only one man” to replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia. He meant former Apple CEO Tim Cook. Eleven days later, Nvidia announced Huang’s reinstatement, and Trump told CNBC , “I made the deal.”  Why was that the president’s deal to make? Huang resigned after acknowledging an affair with a woman suspected of ties to Chinese intelligence. Two Nvidia shareholders urged the board to keep an open mind about bringing him back. An Nvidia employee set up a website where people could sign a letter calling for his return. Shareholders and employees had every right to make their case to the directors, who had told investors on November 17 that they had no intention of reinstating Huang. Nvidia’s board also had good reason to ask federal officials what they knew about the suspected intelligence operation. The government’s answer eased their national security concerns, according to the board’s statement . They also met with Huang and said they were satisfied that he could lead the company, though their own investigation remains open.  But Trump crossed the line by pressuring them to reinstate Huang. Any director who still thought it was a mistake to bring back Huang was forced to weigh what it might cost Nvidia to defy the president. That makes it fair to wonder whether Nvidia’s board was truly kosher with reinstating Huang. What happens if the board’s internal investigation turns up more troubling information involving Huang? Will it be reluctant to act against a CEO whose reinstatement Trump declared essential to American prosperity?  When CNBC’s Sara Eisen asked Trump where he drew the line, he replied, “I’m doing it for the country.” In Trump’s telling , American prosperity depends on having Huang at the helm of Nvidia. Little wonder that Jim Cramer asked on the same call whether Washington would come to the company’s aid if it got into financial trouble. Trump said he didn’t think it would come to that, but here he was fielding a bailout question about a company that earned $65.3 billion last quarter. We’ve seen what happens to a board when Washington decides a company is too important to fail. In 2009, while General Motors depended on a federal bailout to stay afloat, the Obama administration ousted CEO Rick Wagoner and appointed his successor, Fritz Henderson. Henderson later told investigators that GM’s directors felt Treasury had usurped their authority to choose the CEO. The administration already has enough say over Nvidia’s business to claim a cut of certain chip sales to China. And the next time Trump asks Huang for a favor, he can remind him who helped get him his job back. As my colleague Scott Lincicome pointed out today , the economic costs of this kind of interference are harder to see than Monday’s jump in Nvidia’s share price.  Take Intel . In August 2025, Trump called on CEO Lip-Bu Tan to resign over Tan’s ties to China. Tan scurried to the White House, where Trump says he told him , “If you’re smart, give the United States of America 10 percent of your company.” Tan kept his job, and the federal government became an Intel shareholder.  That same month, Tim Cook went to the White House seeking a tariff exemption for Apple. As Scott has documented , Trump and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick reportedly pressed Cook to have Intel make some of Apple’s chips. Apple got its exemption. Ten months later, Trump took credit for what he described as a deal between Apple and Intel. “We want capital flowing to companies for commercial reasons,” Scott told the New York Times . Good luck with that when the president is out recruiting customers for a company in the federal portfolio . “Investors have grown accustomed to President Trump influencing the prospects of different companies, whether it’s rare earth metals, energy, and chips,” JoAnne Feeney, a portfolio manager at Advisors Capital Management, told Bloomberg . “It certainly has made investing more complicated because it has to be factored into which stocks you choose to hold. It’s not the way the US capitalistic system is designed.” No, it’s not .  Huang is due to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3 about chip exports. Congress is already asking the administration which officials weighed in with Nvidia’s board and what they said to get Huang reinstated.  But Congress ought to keep Nvidia in mind as it considers the Senate’s defense authorization bill . Section 1051 would let the Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital buy stakes in suppliers of critical minerals and other materials while barring its director from taking a board seat or obtaining other voting representation. Trump didn’t need a seat on Nvidia’s board to get its directors on the phone. Now imagine taking that call when the federal government is also one of your largest shareholders.

The “Antalya pact”, proposed by the joint Turkish-Australian presidency, was rejected in the final hours by the EU, the UK and several climate-vulnerable nations. Meanwhile, many developing countries criticised the lack of progress on climate finance and indecision on a proposed $120bn target for funding climate adaptation. Interactive: Tracking negotiating texts at the COP31 climate summit Interactive: Who wants what at the COP31 climate change summit With stark divisions preventing agreement on the presidency-led pact, UNFCCC chief Simon Stiell expressed “deep disappointment”, speaking of “scope to improve, modernise and reform” the UN climate process. Despite a chaotic endgame that saw the overrunning COP become the longest in history, it did not end in complete failure, with many items adopted in the closing plenary. These included fairly limited or procedural outcomes on a new “ mechanism ” for global “ just transitions ”, plus support for countries struck by climate disasters. There was some progress beyond the negotiations, though, with growing coalitions of nations championing “ roadmaps ” for “transitioning away” from fossil fuels. With the presidency promoting “ electrification ” as a key theme, around 80 nations also signed up to a global target of securing 35% of final energy consumption from electricity by 2035. Here, Carbon Brief provides in-depth analysis of all the key outcomes from Antalya, both inside and outside the COP31 negotiations. (See Carbon Brief’s coverage of COP30 , COP29 , COP28 , COP27 , COP26 , COP25 , COP24 , COP23 , COP22 , COP21 and COP20 .)
