content:
自从泰国政府于2026年9月7日批准选择韩华海洋的4000吨级Ocean-40F护卫舰设计以来，招标过程一直受到抗议和投诉的困扰。最后，11 月 18 日，泰国皇家海军 (RTN) 发言人查宁·斯里雅帕伊 (Chanin Sriyaphai) 少将宣布，在一项关于程序缺陷的上诉得到维持后，总审计长部下属的上诉和投诉委员会已下令取消招标。此次招标于 2026 年 4 月结束，吸引了来自六家国际造船商的激烈竞争：ASFAT、韩华海洋、HD 现代重工、Navantia、ST Engineering 和 TAIS。在韩华海洋被宣布为唯一通过资格要求的竞争者作为优先投标人后，当该项目进入允许此类提交截止到 9 月 18 日的法定期限时，所有其他竞争者都提出了上诉。韩华海洋当时应该被正式宣布为获胜者。然而，由于上诉过程旷日持久，价值 167.3 亿泰铢（5.08 亿美元）的合同从未获得授予。为泰国提议的 Ocean-40F 比例模型。它建立在 DSME 建造的 HTMS Bhumibol Adulyadej 的血统之上。
(戈登·亚瑟) 上诉和投诉委员会认为，四家落败竞争者的论点没有分量，但它确实证实了泰国护卫舰建造财团的第五项投诉，该财团与 Navantia 组建了一家合资企业，并提出完全在泰国建造这艘军舰。该财团的实质性投诉是，当投标人列出他们过去的造船记录以证明他们的能力时，合同的职权范围没有正确规定货币门槛。参与资格。尽管财政部规定投标人必须证明其已达到前项目价值占项目预算 50%（即约 85 亿泰铢）的门槛，但招标并未要求他们提供详细的财务标准。此次取消将迫使 RTN 根据 2017 年《公共采购和供应管理法》第 119 条第 2 款完全重新招标护卫舰计划。代理委员会的所有成员也必须更换。 RTN总司令Nares Wongtrakul海军上将表示，海军将尊重法律程序、保护公共利益并追求泰国国防所需的能力。他重申需要一个公平、透明的程序，让纳税人可以监督。条款重新措辞的新招标流程还需要六个月的时间准备，此外还必须成立新的委员会。
此外，时间限制意味着海军需要在2027年9月底之前签署合同，才能使用本财期分配的预算。查宁承认，“我们承认职权范围不完整，不符合规定，我们尊重这一判断。”他在为海军辩护时指出，“事实上，不存在价值 85 亿泰铢的护卫舰。”他声称这就是海军简化条件以验证实际造船经验的原因。他强调，这与腐败或偏袒一个竞标者无关。这张照片显示 HTMS 普密蓬·阿杜德 (HTMS Bhumibol Adulyadej) 于 2018 年 12 月在前往泰国的交付航程中抵达香港。（图片来源：Gordon Arthur）

【原文 English Original】
Ever since the Thai government endorsed the selection of Hanwha Ocean’s 4,000-tonne Ocean-40F frigate design on 7 September 2026, the tender process has been beset by protests and complaints. Finally, on 18 November, Royal Thai Navy (RTN) spokesman Rear Admiral Chanin Sriyaphai announced that the Appeals and Complaints Committee, under the Comptroller General’s Department, had ordered cancellation of the tender after one appeal was upheld regarding procedural flaws. This tender that closed in April 2026 had attracted stiff competition from six international shipbuilders: ASFAT, Hanwha Ocean, HD Hyundai Heavy Industries, Navantia, ST Engineering and TAIS. After Hanwha Ocean was declared preferred bidder as the only contender to pass qualification requirements, all the other contenders filed appeals when the project entered a statutory period allowing such submissions through till 18 September. Hanwha Ocean was supposed to be formally declared the winner at that point. However, the contract worth THB16.73 billion (US$508 million) was never awarded because of this protracted appeals process. A scale model of the Ocean-40F proposed for Thailand. It builds upon the lineage of the DSME-built HTMS Bhumibol Adulyadej . (Gordon Arthur) Cancellation The Appeals and Complaints Committee decided that arguments from four of the losing contenders did not carry weight, but it did put credence on a fifth complaint from the Thai Frigate Building Consortium, which had formed a joint venture with Navantia and was offering to build the warship entirely in Thailand. The consortium’s material complaint was that the contract’s terms of reference did not properly specify monetary thresholds when bidders listed their past shipbuilding track records to prove their eligibility to participate. The tender did not require them to give detailed financial criteria, despite Ministry of Finance regulations stipulating that bidders must demonstrate they had reached the threshold of a former project worth 50% of the project budget, or around THB8.5 billion. This cancellation will force the RTN to entirely retender the frigate programme as per Article 119 Paragraph 2 of the 2017 Public Procurement and Supplies Administration Act. All members of acting committees would have to be replaced too. Admiral Nares Wongtrakul, the RTN’s Commander-in-Chief, said the navy would respect the legal process, protect the public interest and pursue the capabilities that Thailand needs for its defence. He reiterated the need for a fair, transparent process that taxpayers could scrutinise. A fresh tender process with reworded terms will take another six months to prepare, plus new committees will have to be set up. Furthermore, time constraints mean the Navy needs to sign the contract by the end of September 2027 in order to use its allocated budget for the current fiscal period. Chanin admitted, “We acknowledge that the terms of reference were incomplete and did not comply with the regulations, and we respect the judgment.” In the navy’s defence, he noted that, “In reality, no frigate worth 8.5 billion baht exists.” He claimed that was why the navy simplified conditions to verify practical shipbuilding experience. He stressed this had nothing to do with corruption or favouring one bidder over another. This photo shows HTMS Bhumibol Adulyadej arriving in Hong Kong on its delivery voyage to Thailand in December 2018. (Credit: Gordon Arthur) Fallout Because no deal had been signed under the original tender, the RTN does not expect to be liable for damages. However, in response to cancellation, local media reported that Hanwha Ocean filed a petition with Thailand’s State Audit Office on 18 November. The South Korean company apparently requested an investigation into potentially unlawful actions that have caused it hardship and unfair treatment. Hanwha Ocean is eligible to enter the next tender, but it will hold no favoured status compared to any other contender. However, it is concerned that it is now at a disadvantage because details of its original proposal have already been disclosed. Hanwha Ocean therefore petitioned the ombudsman for the tender process to be suspended until this investigation is concluded. Despite all this kerfuffle, the choice of the Ocean-40F frigate was somewhat logical given that Daewoo Shipbuilding & Marine Engineering – the forerunner to Hanwha Ocean – had delivered a similarly sized frigate to the RTN in 2018, HTMS Bhumibol Adulyadej . The frigate price is likely to rise because of the passage of time, and such contractual rigmaroles leave a bitter taste in the mouths of would-be competitors. Following the RTN’s frustrating saga over the procurement of an S26T submarine from China, this is yet another bad look for Bangkok. The first time around, long before the five appeals were lodged, the navy had stated, “The Royal Thai Navy recognises that the frigate procurement project has attracted considerable public and societal interest, as it concerns national security, the protection of Thailand’s maritime interests and the use of public funds. The RTN therefore places the utmost importance on ensuring that every stage of the process is conducted correctly, cost-effectively, transparently and in a manner that is subject to scrutiny.” The renewed process will now come under even greater scrutiny. Nonetheless, Chanin said with confidence, “Please watch how the new tender process unfolds. In the end, everything will be proven by the results.” Local involvement The tender outlined a minimum level of 20% indigenous content and the transfer of technology. Eight domestic shipbuilders and the Thai Shipbuilding and Repairing Association hadsigned a memorandum of understanding in preparation for this frigate programme in March 2025. They said their agreement “seeks to consolidate private-sector expertise and resources in preparation for complex naval programmes, including the potential construction of frigates for the Royal Thai Navy”. The eight local companies include Asian Marine Services, Marsun, Seacrest Marine, Unithai Shipyard and Engineering, Thai International Dockyard, Mariart (Thailand), Lantacruz and Prakarnkonlakarn Shipyard. Marsun stated, “Their capabilities span ship construction and repair, advanced engineering, systems integration and specialised maritime services. By combining their strengths, the companies aim to build a coordinated national capacity capable of delivering complex, large-scale naval projects within Thailand.” However, no Thai shipbuilder has ever attempted to construct a naval vessel as complex as a frigate before. The most sophisticated naval vessels built in Thailand to date are two 2,000-tonne Krabi -class offshore patrol vessels built in conjunction with BAE Systems. The RTN shared in an 18 September statement that its new warship would be able to conduct surface warfare, anti-submarine warfare and air defence. It also said the frigate would be capable of conducting land attack missions and countering drones. The navy also revealed that Hanwha Ocean’s offer included offshore patrol vessel and unmanned surface vessel designs, as well as technology transfer and development of a tactical data link and combat management system. Programme scope One reason that this competition is being fought so fiercely is that the Thai navy ultimately wants more than just one frigate. Under its 2026-32 budget commitment, the RTN has already sought THB35 billion for the first pair. Beyond that, it needs four new frigates by 2037. Thailand needs these modern warships to help secure both its Andaman Sea and Gulf of Thailand coastlines. The post Royal Thai Navy Forced to Retender Frigate Programme appeared first on Naval News .

title: Hong Kong court orders activist Eddie Tse to pay gov’t legal fees over dropped San Tin Technopole challenge
zh_title: 香港法院命令活动人士谢伟业因新田科技城挑战被撤销而支付政府律师费
summary: 香港一家法院下令环保活动人士谢伟业支付律师费，此前他放弃了对政府在香港与中国大陆边境附近建设大型科技中心的决定的质疑。 2024 年 11 月 11 日，Eddie Tse 在香港高等法院前。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据《证人报》报道，高等法院周二作出判决，责令谢支付环境保护署和土木工程拓展署的法律费用，该署在司法复核被驳回之前已为诉讼程序做好了准备。高的
content:
香港一家法院下令环保活动人士谢伟业支付律师费，此前他放弃了对政府在香港与中国大陆边境附近建设大型科技中心的决定的质疑。 2024 年 11 月 11 日，Eddie Tse 在香港高等法院前。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。据《证人报》报道，高等法院周二作出判决，责令谢支付环境保护署和土木工程拓展署的法律费用，该署在司法复核被驳回之前已为诉讼程序做好了准备。高等法院法官拉塞尔·科尔曼在判决中表示，两个政府部门为此案聘请了六名大律师，称其“明显荒谬”，因此只判谢谢支付两名大律师的费用。社会工作者、环保组织拯救大屿山联盟召集人谢先生于2024年8月对环保部门兴建新田科技城的决定提出法律质疑。同年8月，法院批准司法复核，谢先生申请法律援助。然而，当年11月，法院批评政府拖延处理法律援助申请。去年1月，谢被指控向当局作出虚假陈述以获取老人津贴和公共住房，并因涉嫌欺诈被捕。后来，他因挑战政府而被拒绝提供法律援助。
新田。资料图片：香港政府一站通。去年四月，谢决定退出法律挑战，理由是他和他的家人受到骚扰和恐吓。法院驳回前区议员陈黛比接手司法覆核的申请，质疑因而被驳回。司法复核的受访者申请了法律费用，而谢则以公共利益为由寻求豁免。法官拉塞尔·科尔曼周二表示，由于司法审查在任何法律原则得以澄清之前就已终止，因此不属于公共利益诉讼费用减免的范围。牌照被吊销 去年7月，谢因在福利计划中诈骗政府16,780港元而被判处120小时社区服务。谢现年 69 岁，自 1993 年以来一直是注册社会工作者。在欺诈定罪后，社会工作者注册委员会（SWRB）吊销了他的社会工作者执照三年。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong court has ordered environmental activist Eddie Tse to pay legal fees after he dropped a challenge against the government’s decision to build a huge technology hub near the city’s border with mainland China. Eddie Tse in front of Hong Kong’s High Court on November 11, 2024. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The High Court handed down judgment on Tuesday ordering Tse to pay the legal costs of the Environmental Protection Department and the Civil Engineering and Development Department, which had prepared for the proceedings before the judicial review was dismissed, The Witness reported. High Court judge Russell Coleman said in the judgment that the two government departments had engaged six barristers for the case, calling it “plainly absurd,” and therefore only granted costs for two barristers to be paid by Tse. Tse, a social worker and convenor of the environmental group Save Lantau Alliance, lodged a legal challenge against environmental authorities’ decision to build the San Tin Technopole in August 2024. The court granted leave for judicial review in August that year, and Tse applied for legal aid. However, in November that year, the court criticised the government over its delay in processing the legal aid application. In January last year, Tse was arrested on suspicion of fraud after being accused of making false statements to authorities to obtain an elderly allowance and public housing. He was later denied legal aid for his challenge against the government. San Tin. File photo: GovHK. In April last year, Tse decided to withdraw from the legal challenge, citing harassment and intimidation directed at him and his family. The court denied former district councillor Debby Chan’s application to take over the judicial review, and the challenge was consequently dismissed. The respondents to the judicial review applied for legal costs, while Tse sought a waiver on public interest grounds. Judge Russell Coleman said on Tuesday that because the judicial review was discontinued before any legal principles could be clarified, it fell outside the scope of public interest litigation cost waivers. Licence suspended In July last year, Tse was sentenced to 120 hours of community service for defrauding the government of HK$16,780 in welfare schemes. Tse, 69, had been a registered social worker since 1993. Following the fraud conviction, the Social Workers Registration Board (SWRB) suspended his social worker licence for three years.

title: Hong Kong government rules out official Tai Po fire memorial, announces HK$630 million in new victim grants
zh_title: 香港政府排除设立官方大埔火灾纪念馆，宣布新增6.3亿港元遇难者补助金
summary: 香港政府在大埔火灾一周年之前宣布，不会举办任何官方纪念活动，同时公布了针对悲剧受害者的新补贴计划。 2025年12月10日，一束鲜花被留在大埔宏福苑附近的路边。2025年11月26日，一场致命大火，吞没了该住宅区八个街区中的七个。照片：何凯莉/HKFP。政务司司长陈家伟周二在商业电台表示，当局不会举办任何活动悼念火灾遇难者，因为
content:
香港政府在大埔火灾一周年之前宣布，不会举办任何官方纪念活动，同时公布了针对悲剧受害者的新补贴计划。 2025年12月10日，一束鲜花被留在大埔宏福苑附近的路边。2025年11月26日，一场致命大火，吞没了该住宅区八个街区中的七个。照片：何凯莉/HKFP。政务司司长陈家伟周二在商业电台表示，当局不会举办任何活动哀悼火灾遇难者，因为社区已经开展了各种活动，包括宗教团体组织的活动。陈补充说，政府不会阻碍合法的纪念活动，并且在某些情况下会提供安排交通等协助。不过，陈敦促公众“谨慎”选择纪念活动，并指出网上有些人试图利用纪念活动“制造麻烦”。陈的这番言论是在 11 月 26 日大埔火灾一周年纪念日之前发表的。一些纪念活动的组织者似乎面临着当局的压力，一些教堂收到了警方的询问，活动突然被取消。与此同时，政府宣布为火灾受害者提供两项新的补助金，总额约为6.3亿港元，帮助他们“尽快开始新的生活”。民政及青年事务局局长麦惠文会见传媒。
民政及青年事务局局长麦家丽周二向传媒表示，在“新起点支援津贴”计划下，每间单位的业主将获发30万港元的补助金，而每名死者家属将获发20万港元的补助金。这些补助金将从宏福苑支援基金中拨出，该基金是一项政府主导的基金，已向企业和公众筹集了 45 亿港元。麦说，火灾发生一年后，支持基金“已基本用完”。该基金约28亿港元已指定用于支持政府买断受火灾影响的宏福苑住宅小区的所有物业。 “化悲痛为动力” 去年11月26日，大埔宏福苑住宅小区发生火灾。当该庄园正在进行大规模翻修工程时，它始于一栋建筑，并迅速蔓延到其他六个街区。这是该市几十年来最严重的火灾，夺去了 168 人的生命，其中包括 10 名家庭佣工，并导致数千人无家可归。调查这起致命火灾的独立委员会一个月前向政府提交了一份关于火灾原因和建议的报告。行政长官李家超在10月下旬的新闻发布会上带领高层官员宣布时任房屋署署长何温妮因火灾辞职，并根据委员会的建议采取了一系列改革措施。
布政司陈家祥。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。陈表示，政府将全面落实火灾后成立的独立委员会提出的全部 120 项建议。他补充说，其中近 30 项建议已经推出，其余近 90% 的建议要么已准备好实施，要么已经在实施中，其中绝大多数将于明年完成。 “我也是香港人。这件事太严重了，令人心碎和悲伤……现在已经一年多了。”

【原文 English Original】
The Hong Kong government has announced ahead of the first anniversary of the fatal Tai Po fire that it will not host any official memorial activities, while unveiling new subsidy schemes for victims of the tragedy. A bouquet of flowers is left on a roadside near Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, on December 10, 2025. A deadly blaze broke out on November 26, 2025, and engulfed seven of the eight blocks of the housing estate. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. Chief Secretary for Administration Eric Chan said on Commercial Radio on Tuesday that authorities would not host any events to mourn the fire victims, as various activities, including those organised by religious groups, were already underway in the community. Chan added that the government would not obstruct legal memorial activities and would, in some cases, offer assistance such as arranging transportation. However, Chan urged the public to choose memorial activities “carefully,” noting that some people online were attempting to use memorial events to “make trouble.” Chan’s remarks came ahead of the first anniversary of the Tai Po fire on November 26. Organisers of some memorial activities have appeared to face pressure from authorities, with some churches receiving police enquiries and an event abruptly cancelled . Meanwhile, the government announced two new grants for the fire victims, totalling around HK$630 million, to help them “start a new life as soon as possible.” Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak meets the press. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak told the press on Tuesday that under the “New Beginning Support Grants” scheme, the owner of each flat would be offered HK$300,000, while another grant of HK$200,000 would be provided to the family of each deceased victim. The grants will be disbursed from the Support Fund for Wang Fuk Court, a government-led fund that has raised HK$4.5 billion from corporations and members of the public. Mak said that one year after the fire, the support fund “has been largely used up.” About HK$2.8 billion from the fund has been earmarked to support the government’s buyout of all property titles at the fire-hit Wang Fuk Court residential estate. ‘Channel sorrow into motivation’ On November 26 last year, a blaze broke out at the Wang Fuk Court residential estate in Tai Po. It started in one building and quickly spread to six other blocks while the estate was undergoing a large-scale renovation project. It was the deadliest blaze the city had seen in decades, claiming 168 lives, including 10 domestic workers, and leaving thousands homeless. An independent committee probing the deadly fire submitted a report on its causes and recommendations to the government a month ago. Chief Executive John Lee led top officials at a press conference in late October to announce that then-housing chief Winnie Ho had resigned over the blaze , alongside a series of reform measures based on the committee’s recommendations. Chief Secretary Eric Chan. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Chan said the government would fully implement all 120 recommendations put forward by the independent committee established following the fire. Nearly 30 of the recommendations have already been rolled out, while nearly 90 per cent of the remainder are either ready for implementation or already underway, with the vast majority set to be completed next year, he added. “I am also a Hongkonger. This incident was so severe, heartbreaking and sad… It has now been a year and our hearts are heavy. But from the perspective of the government, we should channel our sorrow into motivation for transformation, and make sure there will not be another such incident in the future,” Chan said in Cantonese.

title: In Taiwan, investors ‘really happy’ at Jensen Huang’s return
zh_title: 在台湾，投资者对黄仁勋的回归“非常高兴”
summary: 周二，台湾投资者欣喜若狂，因为黄仁勋在突然退出导致股价暴跌不到两周后重返英伟达，台湾以科技股为主的股市飙升逾 9%。台北 101 大楼上的一条信息写着：“台湾爱 Jensen。”照片：@VVTing2026，来自 X. 黄出生于台湾，在访问期间像摇滚明星一样受到欢迎，为这个处于全球人工智能热潮中心的岛屿创造了巨额财富。今年岛上的投资者纷纷涌入股市，其中越来越多的人借钱购买繁荣的股票
content:
周二，台湾投资者欣喜若狂，因为黄仁勋在突然退出导致股价暴跌不到两周后重返英伟达，台湾以科技股为主的股市飙升逾 9%。台北 101 大楼上的一条信息写着：“台湾爱 Jensen。”照片：@VVTing2026，来自 X. 黄出生于台湾，在访问期间像摇滚明星一样受到欢迎，为这个处于全球人工智能热潮中心的岛屿创造了巨额财富。今年，随着基准指数创下历史新高，岛上的投资者纷纷涌入股市，越来越多的人借钱购买蓬勃发展的科技行业的股票。尽管许多人对黄与一名美国官员怀疑为中国情报机构工作的女性的恋情持悲观态度，但他们更担心的是丑闻对其投资的影响。 “看到他回来让我真的很高兴，”33 岁的教育行业工作人员安迪·陈 (Andy Chen) 说。 “网上大家都在开玩笑，‘黄爸爸事件’给了很多人抄底的机会。” Nvidia 创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋于 2025 年 5 月 19 日在台湾台北举行的 Computex 2025 上发表主题演讲。照片：Nvidia。台交所上周暴跌 17.5%，促使政府出手干预稳定市场。但周二，在芯片巨头台积电和联发科股价上涨 10% 的推动下，该指数飙升逾 9%。
英伟达在纽约的股价飙升了 31.5%，使该公司的市值增加了超过 9000 亿美元。“前天和前几天，每个人都非常痛苦，因为我们的净资产缩水了，”30 岁的财务经理 Jennifer Lin 告诉法新社。林说，黄回到英伟达“是一个非常好的决定”。 “我的股票回来了，我的股票市值也恢复了……心情真好。”尽管英伟达的回归似乎稳定了这家芯片巨头以及更广泛的股市和人工智能生态系统，但到底发生了什么仍然存在疑问。有人猜测黄的外遇和突然离开公司是一个阴谋的一部分。 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 出席在华盛顿特区安德鲁·W·梅隆礼堂举行的白宫人工智能峰会。 2025 年 7 月 23 日。照片：白宫，来自 Flickr。 36 岁的制药公司员工雪莉·施 (Sherry Shih) 告诉法新社：“一个企业家的私生活会对全球经济产生如此巨大的影响，我感到非常惊讶。” “整个事情发展得如此之快，让你觉得幕后有什么事情吗？”林更加强调：“我认为有人陷害了他。”陈说，英伟达最近的惊人业绩让这家科技巨头的董事会“别无选择，只能要求他回来”。 “当然，他的私人道德行为很糟糕，”陈承认。 “但生意归生意，个人归个人。
他的个人行为并不能抹杀他对公司运营、对世界、对台湾的贡献。”

【原文 English Original】
Taiwanese investors rejoiced on Tuesday as the island’s tech-heavy stock market soared more than nine percent following Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia less than two weeks after his abrupt exit sent shares plummeting. A message on Taipei 101 reads, “Taiwan loves Jensen.” Photo: @VVTing2026, via X. Huang, who was born in Taiwan and feted like a rock star during his visits, has generated huge amounts of wealth for the island at the centre of the global AI boom. Investors on the island have piled into the stock market this year, a growing number of them borrowing money to buy shares in the booming tech sector, as the benchmark index hit record highs. Though many took a dim view of Huang’s affair with a woman US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, their greater concern was the scandal’s impact on their investments. “Seeing him come back makes me really happy,” said Andy Chen, 33, who works in the education industry. “Everyone online is joking that the ‘Papa Huang incident’ gave a lot of people a chance to bottom‑fish and buy in.” Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang gives a keynote speech at Computex 2025 in Taipei, Taiwan, on May 19, 2025. Photo: Nvidia. The Taiex plunged 17.5 percent last week, prompting the government to intervene to stabilise the market. But it soared more than nine percent Tuesday, boosted by gains of 10 percent in chip giants TSMC and MediaTek. Nvidia rocketed an eye-watering 31.5 percent in New York, adding more than US$900 billion to the firm’s market value. “Everyone was really miserable the day before yesterday and the previous few days, because our net worth shrank,” Jennifer Lin, a 30-year-old finance manager, told AFP. Huang’s return to Nvidia “is a very good decision”, Lin said. “My stock has come back, the market value of my shares has recovered too… I’m in a really good mood.” While the return to Nvidia appears to have stabilised the chip giant and the broader stock market and AI ecosystem, there are still questions over what really happened. Some people speculated that Huang’s affair and sudden departure from the company had been part of a conspiracy. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang at the White House AI Summit at Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium in Washington, DC. on July 23, 2025. Photo: The White House, via Flickr. “I feel it’s quite surprising that the private life of a single entrepreneur could have such a huge impact on the global economy,” Sherry Shih, 36, a pharmaceutical company employee told AFP. “The way the whole thing has developed so quickly just makes you think is there something going on behind the scenes?” Lin was more emphatic: “I think someone set him up.” Nvidia’s recent blockbuster results had given the tech giant’s board “no choice but to ask him to come back”, Chen said. “Of course, his private moral conduct is bad,” Chen conceded. “But business is business, personal is personal. His personal behaviour doesn’t erase his contributions to the company’s operations, to the world, and to Taiwan.”

title: Truths, Lies, and Prospects for the New Cross-Strait Security Complex in the Taiwan and Luzon Straits
zh_title: 台湾吕宋海峡新的两岸安全复合体的真相、谎言与前景
source: 华盛顿全球台湾研究中心
summary: 下载整期 PDF 简介 当前霍尔木兹海峡的危机表明了战略性地缘政治瓶颈如何影响全球供应链。吕宋岛和台湾海峡也不例外。曾经被学者和政治家想象为孤立和分裂的这些西太平洋阻塞点，一旦太平洋地区爆发重大冲突，就有可能损害世界经济动脉。在去年的另一篇《全球台湾简报》文章中，作者创造了“新的海峡两岸安全复合体”（NCSSC）一词来表示菲律宾的巩固地位。
content:
下载整期 PDF 简介 当前霍尔木兹海峡的危机表明了战略性地缘政治瓶颈如何影响全球供应链。吕宋岛和台湾海峡也不例外。曾经被学者和政治家想象为孤立和分裂的这些西太平洋阻塞点，一旦太平洋地区爆发重大冲突，就有可能损害世界经济动脉。在去年的另一篇《全球台湾简报》文章中，笔者创造了“新的海峡两岸安全复合体”（NCSSC）一词，以表示菲律宾巩固其群岛和海上防御：将西菲律宾海（WPS）和吕宋海峡作为共同关注点，并将吕宋海峡的未来安全与台湾海峡的安全联系起来。简而言之，NCSSC指的是两岸政治体之间发生和交叉的物质、制度和认知模式。笔者认为，国家社会保障委员会并不是一个空词。它代表了多个参与者遵守的有机行动框架：包括中华人民共和国（PRC）、台湾、菲律宾、美国和日本。该框架的一个值得注意的方面是认知方面如何影响互动的物质和制度模式。
简而言之，虽然一些行为者最近正在恢复过去的真相，即菲律宾伊瓦坦人民和台湾道族人民之间的过去联系，以塑造未来的关系，但还有一些行为者也在利用过去散布谎言。这包括中华人民共和国淡化这种联系，以及对巴丹群岛的主权声索。最终，国家安全安全委员会敦促各国和其他行为者为更广泛的印太地区的未来安全议程制定更明确的政策和灵活的机制。交互框架？众所周知，菲律宾在推行其外交和安全政策方面总是得过且过。文献争论它是否有一个深思熟虑的大战略，但有一件事是肯定的：台湾的未来现在在马尼拉的视野中，因为它看到中华人民共和国不受限制的地区野心。正如菲律宾领导人的言论和官方文件所指出的那样，“被拖入潜在的冲突”是一回事。然而，认识到其在更广泛的印度太平洋地区的地缘政治重要性是另一回事。 NCSSC 是一个合理的框架，可以了解区域参与者在近期和遥远的未来如何互动。最近发生的事件显示了这种互动的规律性。从积极的角度来看，我们可以看到台湾人和菲律宾人在历史和文化上如何通过海洋联系在一起。 2026年6月，来自台湾最南端岛屿兰屿的20名涛人驶入菲律宾最北端岛屿巴丹群岛玛哈涛的一个港口。
这是一段约 111 英里的旅程，乘坐的是名为 Tatala（陶族人所称）或 Tataya（巴丹群岛伊瓦坦人所称）的传统木船。陶人与伊瓦坦人之间如此深厚的联系——尽管由于殖民主义而休眠了 300 年——展示了该地区的当代人民如何通过复制这种 4000 年的移民和航海实践来讲述这些闻所未闻的故事。事实上，这种重燃提醒人们注意它们与南岛语系的联系。尽管缺乏高级政府官员对陶伊-伊瓦坦交流的明确支持声明，菲律宾运输安全办公室战略性地

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Introduction The current crisis in the Strait of Hormuz demonstrates how strategic geopolitical chokepoints can affect the global supply chain. The Luzon and Taiwan Straits are no different. Once imagined by academics and politicians to be isolated and separated, these Western Pacific chokepoints have the potential to harm the world’s economic arteries should a major conflict erupt in the Pacific Region. In a separate Global Taiwan Brief article from last year, this author coined the term, “New Cross-Strait Security Complex” (NCSSC) to denote the Philippines’ consolidation of its archipelagic and maritime defense: interlocking the West Philippine Sea (WPS) and Luzon Strait as a common concern, and linking the Luzon Strait’s future security with that of the Taiwan Strait. Put simply, NCSSC refers to the material, institutional, and cognitive patterns occurring and intersecting between the polities of the two straits. This author argues that the NCSSC is not an empty term. It represents an organic framework of action observed by multiple actors: including the People’s Republic of China (PRC), Taiwan, the Philippines, the United States, and Japan. One notable dimension of this framework comes with how the cognitive aspect affects the material and institutional patterns of interactions. Simply put, while some actors are recently recovering truths of the past—namely, the past connection between the Philippines’ Ivatan people, and Taiwan’s Tao people—to shape the future relations, still others are also using the past to spread lies. This includes the PRC’s downplay of that connection, and claims over the Batanes Islands. Ultimately, the NCSSC impels states and other actors to produce clearer policies with flexible mechanisms for the future security agenda in the broader Indo-Pacific region. A Framework of Interaction? The Philippines is known to muddle through in pursuing its foreign and security policies. The literature debates whether or not it has a deliberate grand strategy , yet one thing is certain: the future of Taiwan is now in Manila’s sights as it sees the PRC’s regional ambitions unrestrained. “To be dragged into a potential conflict”—as noted by Philippine leaders’ rhetoric and official documents —is one thing. However, to appreciate its geopolitical importance in the broader Indo-Pacific is another. The NCSSC serves as a sensible framework to see how regional actors might interact in the immediate and distant future. Recent events show the regularity of such interaction. On a positive note, we can see how Taiwanese and Filipinos are historically and culturally linked by the seas. In June 2026, 20 Tao people from Orchid Island (Lanyu, 蘭嶼 ), Taiwan’s southernmost island, sailed into a port in Mahatao, Batanes, the Philippines’ northernmost island. This was a journey of about 111 miles using a traditional wooden boat known as Tatala (as known by the Tao people) or Tataya (as known by the Ivatans of Batanes). Such deep connections between the Taos and Ivatans—although dormant for 300 years due to colonialism—demonstrates how contemporary peoples of this region are making these unheard stories heard by replicating this 4000-year practice of migration and seafaring. Indeed, such rekindling serves as a reminder of their Austronesian linkage. Though lacking an explicit supportive statement of the Tao-Ivatan exchange by higher government officials, the Philippines’ Office for Transportation Security strategically framed its press release about Manila’s resolve to “ensure that the country’s northern maritime gateways remain protected and efficient” in the case of “welcoming communities.” Image: The Batanes Strait, between Taiwan and the northern Philippines. In 2026, PRC government institutions began to advance the claim that the Batanes Islands (part of the Philippines) were Chinese territory, based on the extension of the continental shelf from Taiwan. (Image source: Google Maps ) Interestingly, two Chinese officials— Ambassador to the Philippines Jing Quan, and Consul and Head of Post Li Xiaoyan of the Chinese Consulate in Laoag, Ilocos Norte— arrived in Batanes on the same day as the Tao people’s arrival for an “official visit” to the province’s officials. On the one hand, this visit serves to remind Philippine officials of Manila’s “One-China Policy.” On the other hand, it also means that Beijing is now playing into the logic of the NCSSC, which serves as a prognosis for broader regional tensions. Some academics from the PRC contest the “ Out of Taiwan” theory of Austronesian linkage between the Tao and Ivatan peoples. Rather, they prefer to propagate Beijing’s narrative of historic rights over Taiwan, contending that these indigenous peoples came instead from mainland southern China. In July 2026, a Global Times article reported that several PRC-based academics at an academic symposium in Jinan University ( 暨南大學 ) asserted that the Batanes Islands “are legally China’s sovereign territory and form a natural geographic extension of China’s Taiwan island,” on the basis of the 1898 Treaty of Paris and the so-called “Japan-Philippines maritime delimitation talks.” In other words, by virtue of PRC’s historic claims on Taiwan and the Tao’s linkage to the Ivatans, Batanes is allegedly an integral part of the PRC. Philippine government officials have rebuked such PRC academic’s claims on Batanes. For instance, Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. noted at the sidelines of the West Philippine Sea summit that such talking points by PRC academics validated his agency’s assessment that Beijing wants to control the Western Pacific. Moreover, given that there is no serious legal basis for such claims, Teodoro noted that “it’s a joke.” Separately, Philippine Foreign Affairs Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro noted that the government would not listen to unofficial channels, while her agency’s spokesperson Analyn Ratonel said that “flights of fancy should not be dignified with a response” since “the Philippines’ sovereignty over Batanes is settled and not up for debate.” Batanes’ lone District House Representative, Ciriaco Gato Jr., similarly rebuked such claims, noting that “any challenge to our status is not merely a geopolitical provocation; it is an affront to our identity that we will not tolerate.” The Philippine’s National Historical Commission (NHC) debunked the Chinese scholarly claims, noting that there is a continuous shelf extending from Northern Luzon through the Babuyan and Batanes Islands and into parts of the Taiwan archipelago based on “current satellite and oceanographic data.” There were also reported circulations among Chinese social media apps last year suggesting that the Philippine province of Palawan—which puts the Municipality of Kalayaan in the WPS under its jurisdiction—is allegedly part of China, by virtue of Ming-era Admiral Zheng He’s explorations. At the macro-level, the Philippine government recognizes that such Chinese talking points are reinforced by foreign influence and malign interference (FIMI) operations —various kinetic activities that aim to alter Filipino solidarity in favor of PRC’s narratives. All Set for the Future? These latest events demonstrate that the framework of interaction demonstrated by the NCSSC does not only involve material and institutional aspects, but also the most basic of human cognitive elements—identity, historical memory, and people-to-people linkage—which are all essential to make the case for brokering the regional commons. They also point to a common denominator: the PRC’s irredentist and unrestrained expansion. However, the NCSSC also opens novel methods for various stakeholders to explore opportunities to assert their agency. The first opportunity refers to cognitive patterns. Whether by constraints or deliberate choice, the Taiwanese government has yet to make any comments on the claim by PRC-based academics regarding Batanes. While ignoring Chinese talking points against the Philippines may sound risk-averse, there is an equal harm inherent in isolating these comments outside the PRC’s broader FIMI operations. Taiwan’s political and security apparatuses would be well advised to invest their attention in curating counter-responses. Moreover, both Manila and Taipei must also leverage linkages between Filipino and Taiwanese cultural communities, academics, think tanks, and civil society organizations, to counter the PRC’s FIMI operational logic. The second opportunity refers to institutional patterns. Since Taiwan is de facto limited in its diplomatic options, the Philippines—with its rapidly expanding strategic partnerships—could serve as a node of a broader security network by framing the Luzon and Taiwan Straits as strategic nerves that cannot be unilaterally occupied by one regional hegemon. Rather, the Straits represent a politically plural area in which to enforce a rules-based international order. This would mean enhancing logistical points of entry and exchange through increased port security, diversifying areas of cooperation between their respective coast guards, fisheries agreements, and anti-piracy and anti-smuggling frameworks, among others. Moreover, while Filipino and American officials argue that Balikatan exercises are solely for Philippine defense, and not intended as a stage for a Taiwan contingency, Filipino and other regional scholars and analysts otherwise note that they are not mutually exclusive. Here, wargaming centers by academics and think tanks can intensify stress-testing assumptions into wider grand strategic considerations, which ripple into Track 1.5/2 dialogues and influence public opinion. The third opportunity refers to material patterns. So far, it is microchip discourse which catches the main attention of the PRC, the US, and other global players on this NCSSC. Minilateral forums serve as cost-efficient avenues in addressing shortcomings of multilateral forums that have been hijacked by PRC’s “Global South Champion” narrative. Moreover, informal talks—like the “Smart Harbor” forum in December 2025 between Taipei and Philippine officials—demonstrate the balance between strategic autonomy and risk-aversion. The Luzon Economic Corridor, which feeds into the US’s Pax Silica initiative to counter the PRC’s World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization (WAICO), are both welcome developments. Taiwan has stated on separate occasions that it is willing to expand economic corridors with the Philippines, either through its proposed “ Silicon Prosperity Initiative ” or as an external node with Pax Silica . So far, Pax Silica has not been well received by most Filipinos, largely due to the lack of an accurate and transparent blueprint, which in turn caused fear among local communities. So far, the Philippines rejection of a diplomatic immunity bargain by the United States in the proposed Pax Silica compound in North Luzon are very well noted points to rebuke PRC narratives of the Philippines “as an American Puppet.” However, the broader goal must be the ability of the Philippines to become a formidable node of the global supply chain through state-led development—not “independent” for its own sake—while addressing local woes. In sum, there is a need for more assertive Philippine counterproposals to serve the country’s industrial interests if it is to become Taiwan’s capable partner. Strategic uncertainty will continue to pervade the 21 st century, and the new geopolitical reality of the NCSSC has now emerged around which all stakeholders must carefully design their approach. They must set clear policy interests while maintaining flexible mechanisms. As for the Philippines and Taiwan, they have an opportunity to set their shared path by modeling such interactions. The main point: The Philippines is becoming more relevant to the future of Taiwan’s security, as the two island states find their security concerns ever-more connected. It is time for all stakeholders to integrate the New Cross-Strait Security Complex as part of the broader regional security architecture. They should and can achieve this through clearer policies, with flexible and responsive mechanisms for future interaction. The post Truths, Lies, and Prospects for the New Cross-Strait Security Complex in the Taiwan and Luzon Straits appeared first on Global Taiwan Institute .

title: Double Dragon: How Taiwan and South Korea Can Collaborate through Chips
zh_title: 双龙：台湾和韩国如何通过芯片进行合作
source: 华盛顿全球台湾研究中心
summary: 下载整期 PDF 台湾和韩国是亚洲四小龙中人口和经济总量最大的两个国家，两国是激烈的竞争对手，尤其是在半导体制造业。但它们对中国市场的共同依赖已成为双方都无法单独解决的弱点。每个人都控制着全球半导体制造的关键节点，它们共同可能构成全球硬件生态系统的瓶颈。台北和首尔应该合作开拓新市场并与大国进行谈判。他们在一起拥有任何一方都无法运用的影响力
content:
下载整期 PDF 台湾和韩国是亚洲四小龙中人口和经济总量最大的两个国家，两国是激烈的竞争对手，尤其是在半导体制造业。但它们对中国市场的共同依赖已成为双方都无法单独解决的弱点。每个人都控制着全球半导体制造的关键节点，它们共同可能构成全球硬件生态系统的瓶颈。台北和首尔应该合作开拓新市场并与大国进行谈判。他们在一起所拥有的影响力是任何一个人都无法单独有效地运用的。台湾和韩国是竞争对手，也是伙伴，长期以来一直是死对头。 1992年首尔从台北转而承认北京这一相对较新的记忆，给许多台湾人留下了挥之不去的背叛感，因为韩国是亚洲最后一个与台湾断绝外交关系的国家。据称，在2000年代和2010年代，韩国三星电子推行“杀台”计划，旨在削弱台湾的芯片制造能力。此外，2010年亚运会跆拳道比赛的有争议的裁判，也被称为“索克门”，严重侵蚀了双边的公众善意。 2012年，富士康创始人郭台铭在讨论与三星的竞争时，使用具有种族主义贬义的“高丽棒子”来指代韩国人，引发强烈批评，进一步助长韩国的反台情绪。
鉴于这段痛苦的历史和所涉及的非常现实的财务利益，韩国和台湾芯片公司的竞争常常被相互对抗的感觉所掩盖。过去，外部试图协调台北和首尔的芯片政策——例如总统乔·拜登的“芯片4联盟”概念——失败了，因为他们没有充分考虑台湾和韩国领先芯片制造商之间激烈竞争的逻辑。然而，不健康的竞争和民族主义不应该让任何一方蒙蔽双眼。如今，两个邻近的东亚民主国家及其制造业冠军之间的协同关系比许多人想象的要强得多。台裔英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋近期分别于5月底和6月初连续访问台湾和韩国，受到两地热烈欢迎。这样的反应说明了两国经济在当今半导体行业中的相互联系和互补程度有多深。黄先生还因其对促进美韩关系的贡献而被授予今年的詹姆斯·范弗利特奖。在经济上，亚洲邻国建立了持久的关系。 2025年，韩国是台湾第三大贸易伙伴，台湾是韩国第四大贸易伙伴。此外，两个经济体之间已经存在部分劳动分工。
台湾公司，尤其是台湾积体电路制造股份有限公司（台积电、台湾积体电路制造股份有限公司）制造先进的逻辑芯片，而韩国的三星和 SK 海力士则在存储器领域占据主导地位。这些公司（以及两国）是当今人工智能革命不可或缺的一部分，无论是在训练人工智能模型还是为数据中心提供服务方面。到2025年，两国经济体的双边芯片贸易额将超过600亿美元，其中台湾的先进逻辑芯片支持韩国人工智能计算基础设施的快速发展，而台湾则封装了许多韩国制造的高带宽内存（HBM）芯片。 2025年台湾进口额约493亿美元

【原文 English Original】
DOWNLOAD FULL ISSUE PDF Taiwan and South Korea, the two largest of the Four Asian Dragons by population and economic output, are fierce rivals, especially in the semiconductor manufacturing industry. But their common reliance on China’s market has become a vulnerability that neither can address alone. Each controls crucial nodes of global semiconductor manufacturing, and together they could constitute a chokepoint in the global hardware ecosystem. Taipei and Seoul should collaborate to open new markets and negotiate with major powers. Together, they have leverage that neither one can wield so effectively alone. Rivals, but Also Partners Taiwan and South Korea have long been bitter rivals. The relatively recent memory of Seoul switching recognition from Taipei to Beijing in 1992 has left a lingering sense of betrayal among many Taiwanese, as South Korea was the last country in Asia to end diplomatic relations with Taiwan. In the 2000s and 2010s, South Korea’s Samsung Electronics allegedly pursued a “kill Taiwan” plan aimed at undermining Taiwan’s chipmaking capabilities. Furthermore, the contested judgment in the taekwondo competition at the 2010 Asian Games, also called “ Sockgate ,” sharply eroded bilateral public goodwill. In 2012, Foxconn founder Terry Gou (郭台銘), while discussing competition with Samsung, used the derogatory racist slur, gaoli bangzi (高麗棒子), to refer to Koreans, prompting strong criticism and further fueling anti-Taiwanese sentiment in South Korea. Given this bitter history and the very real financial stakes involved, the South Korean and Taiwanese chip firm rivalry is often shaded by feelings of mutual antagonism. In the past, outside attempts to align Taipei and Seoul’s chip policies—such as President Joe Biden’s “Chip 4 Alliance” concept —fell short because they did not adequately reckon with the logic of heated competition between leading Taiwanese and South Korean chipmakers. However, unhealthy rivalry and nationalism should not blind either side. The two neighboring East Asian democracies, together with their manufacturing champions, have a far more synergistic relationship today than many assume. Taiwanese American Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s (黃仁勳) recent consecutive visits to Taiwan and South Korea in late May and early June, respectively, garnered warm welcomes in both places. Such a reaction speaks to how deeply interconnected and complementary the two economies have become in today’s semiconductor industry. Huang was also awarded this year’s James A. Van Fleet Award for his contributions to the promotion of US-South Korea relations. Economically, the Asian neighbors have built enduring ties. In 2025, South Korea was Taiwan’s third-largest trading partner, while Taiwan was South Korea’s fourth-largest . Furthermore, a partial division of labor already exists between the two economies. Taiwanese firms, notably Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC, 台灣積體電路製造股份有限公司), manufacture advanced logic chips , while South Korea’s Samsung and SK Hynix dominate memory. These companies (and both countries) are integral to today’s AI revolution, both for training AI models and supplying data centers. The two economies conducted over USD 60 billion in bilateral chip trade in 2025, with Taiwan’s advanced logic chips supporting rapid AI compute infrastructure development in South Korea, while Taiwan packages many South Korean-made high bandwidth memory (HBM) chips. In 2025, Taiwan imported around USD 49.3 billion worth of integrated circuits from South Korea, representing 37.7 percent of Taiwan’s chip imports, far more than from any other country. South Korea accounted for a smaller but still significant share of Taiwan’s integrated circuit exports , around USD 18.4 billion, or 8.8 percent. Shared Challenges Yet despite this growing industrial interdependence, Taiwan and South Korea remain exposed to the same strategic vulnerability: both of them depend heavily on China as a major downstream market for their chips. China’s booming electronics industry consumes vast quantities of semiconductor chips for everything from iPhones to appliances to AI data centers. In 2025, 51.2 percent of Taiwan’s chip exports went to mainland China or Hong Kong, while 41.7 percent of South Korean chip exports headed to the PRC. Such overwhelming reliance on one market—especially one that is actively subsidizing its own domestic chip manufacturers to gradually reduce foreign dependence—carries substantial economic security risk. SK Hynix, Samsung, and TSMC may eventually lose much of China’s demand to state-backed Chinese firms. Moreover, Beijing’s increasingly aggressive security posture and willingness to coerce smaller economies make China a fundamentally unreliable customer. Taiwan and South Korea have long recognized this problem, and each has pursued its own trade reorientation over the past decade. Taipei launched the “New Southbound Policy” under former president Tsai Ing-wen (蔡英文) in 2016. Seoul followed in 2017 by initiating its “New Southern Policy” under then-president Moon Jae-in. These policies succeeded in deepening economic relations with other markets—especially those in Southeast Asia—but have failed to fundamentally reorient chip exports away from China. At the time, the political impetus and market opportunities were simply insufficient. Image: A semiconductor chip manufactured by SK Hynix, one of South Korea’s major chip manufacturers. Taiwan and South Korea manufacturers have faced intense competition qin the market for advanced chips. (Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) How to Team Up Through Chips Today, Seoul and Taipei cannot afford to go it alone. Reducing the relative weight of the Chinese market for their chip exports is not only a security imperative; it is an economic necessity as China’s indigenous chip ecosystem gains ground . Building on the complementary strengths of their semiconductor industries, South Korea and Taiwan could establish an industry-led bilateral working group led by their chip giants—TSMC, Samsung, and SK Hynix—to coordinate semiconductor trade and investment policy. Given the absence of formal diplomatic relations, a direct government-to-government framework with ministerial leadership would not be realistic. However, the sheer economic and monetary weight of these private firms and their close ties to their respective governments would give a cooperative framework substantial influence and credibility. For instance, Taiwan’s National Development Fund is a major shareholder in TSMC, while TSMC founder and former CEO Morris Chang led Taiwan’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) delegation seven times between 2006 and 2023. Similarly, given its strong relationships with Korean chip firms, the Lee Jae Myung administration has a record of leveraging its commercial involvement to pursue decisive political objectives . For instance, ahead of the August 2026 election in South Korea for Democratic Party leadership, Lee promoted a major semiconductor cluster in Jeolla Province backed by planned investment from Samsung and SK Hynix. The initiative benefited one of Lee’s cabinet officials, Kim Min-seok, helping him win the election for party leader to replace Lee’s prominent rival within the party, Jung Chung-rae. Critics accused the administration of using corporate investment to tilt politics in Lee’s favor. Yet, this example demonstrates that Seoul maintains substantial influence over its domestic semiconductor industry—and could work effectively with those firms to facilitate de facto economic collaboration with their Taiwanese counterparts that prioritizes national rather than private interests. Similarly, TSMC — which was established with Taipei’s financial and political backing in 1987 — retains close ties to Taiwan’s political leadership. Taiwanese and South Korean industry associations and companies would provide the institutional backbone of the working group and serve as the primary channel for bilateral engagement, with which the governments could easily and regularly engage. Trade and economic government officials could participate discreetly at the working level or through the two sides’ representative offices. More senior officials would have the opportunity to speak directly in private meetings alongside multilateral institutions in which both are represented, such as the APEC, to coordinate the working group. Some level of unofficial government contact is prudent to ensure that the nominally private sector working group advances the interests of South Korea and Taiwan as a whole, as well as those of their chip firms. This working group would have two primary aims: (1) to develop a common strategy to cultivate new markets; and (2) to coordinate negotiations on new trade and investment agreements with major economies from a position of greater strength. One Strategy, One Face Taiwanese and South Korean chips flow primarily to three sectors: cloud computing infrastructure; consumer goods such as electronics , appliances and automobiles ; and telecommunications equipment. Yet China’s massive output in all three categories has created a gravitational pull that has been hard for Taiwanese and Korean chip firms to escape. As a result, any joint Taiwan-South Korea strategy for cultivating overseas markets and negotiating trade agreements must go beyond setting up chip packaging facilities or even fabs. They must push for a broader set of economic reforms in those markets that will facilitate the rapid development of consumer electronics manufacturing and cloud computing infrastructure. India holds the most potential. Unlike in Southeast Asia , Chinese investment and 5G telecommunications penetration are fairly low , and the country has massive room for growth. Individual Taiwanese and South Korean firms such as Foxconn, Samsung, and Hyundai have had success with particular projects that received special Indian government attention and support. Indeed, the Indian government has repeatedly identified electronics, automobiles, and semiconductors as key sectors to bolster India’s manufacturing output. But India’s complex regulatory environment, bureaucratic proceduralism, infrastructure development bottlenecks, and sometimes counterproductive labor laws mean that India’s operating environment remains very difficult for foreign investors. [1] As a result, India has failed to generate an electronics manufacturing ecosystem—and chip demand—that can rival China’s. By speaking with one voice to New Delhi as the only two economies capable of helping fulfill India’s ambitions in electronics and semiconductor manufacturing, Seoul and Taipei might make greater progress in pressing for reforms in India than either could alone. They might also open greater access for Taiwanese and South Korean firms to a more populated market than China—one which has yet to expend its demographic dividend. The same logic applies to Taiwan’s and South Korea’s policies vis-à-vis the United States. In recent years, successive US administrations have pressed Taiwanese and South Korean chipmakers to expand manufacturing on American soil, from the Biden Administration’s CHIPS and Science Act to the Trump Administration’s greater demands for investments in the United States. Washington’s desire to reshore enough chip production to sustain its defense capabilities and economic system in a supply shock is a rational pursuit. However, as long as key inputs, downstream packaging, and testing still occur outside of the United States, domestic chip fabrication alone is inadequate to ensure US economic resilience. Moreover, a substantial share of the world’s chips still end up in electronics made in Asia. Even if the United States can ensure a bare minimum supply at home for military use and cloud services providers, it will have to look beyond its borders for sufficient demand to make US chip production economical in the long run. Image: Then-President Joseph Biden and then-President Yoon Suk-yeol visiting a Samsung semiconductor plant in South Korea (May 2022), (Image source: Wikimedia Commons ) More recent US administrations have focused on boosting foreign investment in the United States. A Washington willing to subordinate political and geostrategic partnerships in favor of a maximum reshoring effort might seek to play Taipei and Seoul against each other by inducing them to pledge ever greater semiconductor investments. This tactic could gradually hollow out the manufacturing capacity underpinning their respective “silicon shields,” leaving both more vulnerable to security threats from China in the long run — even if the most advanced logic chips are still produced in Taiwan. Instead of competing to offer ever-larger investments and concessions, Taipei and Seoul should coordinate the scale, terms, and technological scope of their US investments. Rather than sending an ultimatum to Washington, Taipei and Seoul could provide a roadmap for a sustained Taiwan-South Korea-US trilateral partnership on semiconductor innovation and fabrication to support US-led AI stack dominance (which covers the whole production chain from critical minerals and energy to semiconductors and telecommunications equipment, upon which the development and rollout of AI software relies). This triangle would be based on mutual trust and common economic and security interests. This would be far more beneficial to all involved—including the United States—than haphazard investment pledges. Targeted investments would complement ongoing economic security projects (such as the Hanwha Philly Shipyard in Philadelphia ) and help anchor chip fab suppliers in the United States. They would also allow Taiwanese and South Korean chip firms to better serve their US customers; indeed, this was part of the rationale that made the initial TSMC plant in Arizona feasible. More direct cooperation between Taipei, Seoul, and Washington may also allow all three parties to identify and capitalize on new production synergies of which US policymakers may not be aware. The main point : Ongoing commercial rivalry and nationalist sentiments show that the Taiwan-South Korea partnership will not be easy. But in continuing to work alone—and sometimes at odds—Taipei and Seoul are leaving leverage on the table that could secure their symbiotic prosperity for years to come. [1] Devesh Kapur and Arvind Subramanian, A Sixth of Humanity: Independent India’s Development Odyssey (Gurugram: HarperCollins Publishers India, 2025). title: Battle for the Capital: Inside the 2026 Taipei Mayoral Race, Part 2
