content:
周二，铜价回吐了周一人工智能推动的全部涨幅，因为在最近的人工智能暴跌期间抛售金属的投资者几乎没有回归的兴趣，而且交易员不断将美国库存转移到中国。纽约早盘交易中，Comex 12 月交割的铜价下跌 3.5%，至每磅 5.437 美元（每吨 11,985 美元）。该水平的结算价将是 3 月 24 日以来的最低水平。该合约周一结算价为 5.634 美元，上涨 2.7%，但远低于 Nvidia 恢复黄仁勋担任首席执行官后创下的盘中高点 5.787 美元。周二的下跌使铜价比 9 月 9 日创纪录的 6.889 美元下跌 21%，从技术上讲，这是一个熊市。该金属今年已下跌 3%，11 月份则下跌 16%。据路透社报道，伦敦金属交易所三个月期铜在官方交易中下跌 3.5%，至每吨 12,054 美元，此前曾一度跌破 12,000 美元。周一该股上涨了 5.3%。 11 月 12 日黄仁勋辞职后，在人工智能暴跌期间出售大宗商品的投资者并没有急着回来。 Panmure Liberum 分析师汤姆·普莱斯 (Tom Price) 对路透表示：“这些投资者并未完全重新投入事件发生前的头寸，其中包括大宗商品敞口。”他表示，许多人认为铜的波动性太大，正在削减大宗商品的投资，以专注于人工智能股票。杭州成联实业的基本金属交易员Aces Zhou告诉彭博社：“现在市场做空铜的原因有多种。”
他表示，除了人工智能的叙述之外，随着铜离开美国，贸易流开始逆转，支撑铜价两年上涨的因素正在瓦解。加息和强势美元加剧了阻力。据彭博社报道，市场完全预计美联储 12 月会议将上涨 25 个基点，这将是今年的第二次会议，而根据 BMO 资本市场的数据，美元指数处于 2025 年 3 月以来的最高水平。美国金属运往中国 现货市场依然紧张，但资金流已经压倒了市场，BMO分析师上周参加上海亚洲铜周后写道。可见的交易所库存仅能满足大约两天的消费量，而进口到中国的洋山溢价在一个月内从每吨不到 100 美元攀升至 500 美元左右。 BMO表示，这些溢价，加上纽约和伦敦价格之间的差距缩小，促使贸易商预订了估计3万吨至10万吨的美国阴极，以便直接运往中国。这些金属存放在美国西海岸的交易所仓库外，大约需要两周时间才能抵达。 BMO表示，发货量的重要性不在于吨位，而在于它们所发出的信号：贸易商正在对一项关税决定失去信心，该决定将使美国库存与世界其他地区隔绝。
中国业内人士预计唐纳德·特朗普总统将放弃对精炼铜征收关税的计划，而西方参与者仍倾向于征收关税。 BMO预计，抛售将持续下去，直到华盛顿方面发出关税意向或价格大幅下跌以影响供应，可能在每吨10,000美元至11,000美元的范围内。该银行表示，托克的成本曲线显示，通过溶剂萃取和电解提取生产的铜中约有 10% 已经亏损，亏损额约为 13,000 美元。 BMO 坚持其中期结构性看涨观点。冶炼厂就 2027 年处理费进行了挤压谈判，矿工向冶炼厂支付的精矿加工费用仍然相差甚远。安托法加斯塔报道

【原文 English Original】
Copper gave back all of Monday’s artificial intelligence-fuelled gains on Tuesday as investors who dumped metals during the recent AI rout showed little appetite to return, and traders kept moving US stockpiles to China. Comex copper for December delivery fell 3.5% to $5.437 a pound ($11,985 a tonne) in morning trade in New York. A settlement at that level would be the lowest since March 24. The contract settled at $5.634 on Monday, up 2.7% but well off the session high of $5.787 reached after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Tuesday’s drop leaves copper 21% below its record settlement of $6.889 on September 9, technically a bear market. The metal is now down 3% this year and 16% in November. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down 3.5% at $12,054 a tonne in official trading after briefly ducking below $12,000, Reuters reports. It had jumped as much as 5.3% on Monday. Investors who sold commodities during the AI rout that followed Huang’s resignation on November 12 are not rushing back. “These investors are not fully reengaging the positions they had pre-event, which includes commodity exposure,” Panmure Liberum analyst Tom Price told Reuters. Many have decided copper is too volatile and are cutting commodity exposure to concentrate on AI stocks, he said. “There are now multiple reasons for the market to short copper,” Aces Zhou, a base metals trader at Hangzhou Chenglian Industrial, told Bloomberg. Beyond the AI narrative, he said, trade flows are starting to reverse as copper leaves the United States, and the factors that supported the metal’s two-year rally are unravelling. Rate hikes and a strong dollar add to the headwinds. Markets are fully pricing a quarter-point increase at the Federal Reserve’s December meeting, which would be the second this year, Bloomberg reports, and the dollar index is at its highest since March 2025, according to BMO Capital Markets. US metal heads to China The physical market remains tight, but financial flows have overpowered it, BMO’s analysts wrote after attending Asia Copper Week in Shanghai last week. Visible exchange inventories cover only about two days of consumption, and the Yangshan premium for imports into China climbed from under $100 a tonne to around $500 in a month. Those premiums, together with a narrowing gap between New York and London prices, have prompted traders to book an estimated 30,000 to 100,000 tonnes of US cathode for direct shipment to China, BMO said. The metal, held outside exchange warehouses on the US west coast, takes about two weeks to arrive. The shipments matter less for the tonnage than for what they signal, BMO said: that traders are losing confidence in a tariff decision that would keep US stockpiles sealed off from the rest of the world. Chinese industry players expect President Donald Trump to drop plans for duties on refined copper, while Western participants still lean towards a tariff being imposed. BMO expects the selloff to extend until Washington signals its tariff intentions or prices fall far enough to hit supply, potentially in the $10,000 to $11,000 a tonne range. Trafigura’s cost curve shows about 10% of copper produced by solvent extraction and electrowinning is already losing money at around $13,000, the bank said. BMO stands by its structurally bullish medium-term view. Smelters squeezed Talks on 2027 treatment charges, the fees miners pay smelters to process concentrate, remain far apart. Antofagasta has reportedly offered around minus $200 a tonne, while China’s Tongling has signalled about minus $80 could be acceptable, according to BMO. This year’s benchmark was set at zero, already a record low, and BMO estimates some Chinese smelters break even on a cash basis at around minus $90. A deeply negative 2027 benchmark could speed up output cuts, especially as falling sulphuric acid prices erode by-product income. Mine supply remains tight. Global copper mine production fell 1% year on year in September and is down 1% over the first nine months of 2026, the International Copper Study Group said in its latest monthly bulletin. Output from Chile slumped 15% and Peru 9% in the month, more than offsetting gains in Indonesia, China and the Democratic Republic of Congo. Refined demand fell 2% from a year earlier, slightly more than supply, leaving the refined market in deficit for the month, though it remains in surplus for the year to date. Miners give back gains Copper stocks reversed much of Monday’s rally. Freeport-McMoRan fell 5% at the New York open, cutting its market value to $68 billion, and Southern Copper lost 4% to $117 billion. Teck Resources dropped 4% to $25 billion, while BHP slipped 2% to $174 billion and Rio Tinto 2% to $125 billion. The five New York-listed heavyweights shed about $15 billion in the first minutes of trading, after adding more than $25 billion on Monday. In London, Antofagasta dropped 7%, Anglo American almost 6% and Glencore 4%, while Poland’s KGHM fell 7%. In Toronto, First Quantum Minerals lost 6%, Lundin Mining and Hudbay Minerals 5% each and Ivanhoe Mines 4%. BHP this week outlined plans to spend up to $17.4 billion to roughly double copper output in South Australia to about 650,000 tonnes a year by 2040, with a final investment decision expected in the first half of 2027. First Quantum Minerals and Panama opened formal negotiations on Monday over the Cobre Panama mine, shut since 2023, after the company accepted the government’s five conditions for talks, including recognition that Panama owns the mineral resource. Trader Trafigura has taken full control of the $260 million La Farola copper-gold project in Chile, buying the remaining 50% of owner Minera Altair as it moves from trading concentrate into mine development. In Santiago, the price slump is threatening President José Antonio Kast’s budget plans , as copper accounts for about half of the country’s exports. (With files from Reuters and Bloomberg)

香港宏福苑大火一周年，BBC中文專訪多位遇難者家屬，紀錄他們災後如何走過一年。2025年11月26日，大埔宏福苑發生香港數十年以最致命火災，奪去168條性命，1984戶失去家園。
「11月26號之後，這條刺永遠都在我心內，可能直到我躺在棺材仍在，不會消散、不會磨滅。」
Christy全家居於最先起火的宏昌閣，她的丈夫逃生時在樓梯間遇難，當時一對子女年僅9歲和6歲。直至現在，她仍然經常拿起手機向丈夫昔日的電話號碼發短訊聊表思念。身為社工的她確診創傷後遺症與抑鬱症，努力適應成為家中唯一支柱的新生活。
火災後，蘇氏夫婦經常到墳場為年逾80歲的父母洗擦合葬墓地，相鄰一片都是新造的墓碑，全部刻著「終於二零二五年十一月廿六日」，屬於一同罹難的宏福苑街坊。媽媽的遺體最後只剩下一個飯盒大小的骸骨，蘇先生在燒成灰燼的舊居尋回雙親遺物，爸爸的手錶在烈焰下永遠定格。他和太太居於另一座的物業沒被大火波及，但政府決定一併收回拆卸，兩人仍未安頓長遠安置。
過去一年，遺屬在等一份調查報告，在排期申請法律援助，在學習如何向年幼的孩子解釋死亡。大火後11個月，香港政府公布獨立委員會調查報告點名四個部門有缺失，特首率官員鞠躬道歉，局長引咎辭職，數十人被捕或起訴。但對許多家庭來說，他們仍在傷痛中等待漫長的司法程序，部分人正申請法援計劃追討傷亡賠償。

这一出口政策的失败不仅仅是具体缺陷的总和。这源于特朗普政府对中国的更广泛立场。华盛顿在拥抱不受限制的人工智能加速的同时，也对北京采取了更加宽松的立场。这种结合为爆炸性的 Megaspeed 丑闻埋下了伏笔，或许还有其他尚未浮出水面的丑闻。结果，中国已经能够获得数量惊人的先进芯片，从而缩小与美国的人工智能差距，并为其人工智能驱动的军事现代化提供动力。据人工智能研究机构Epoch AI称，中国多达三分之一的人工智能算力可能来自走私芯片。中国顶尖的人工智能模型现在仅落后美国几个月。这一微小的差距反映出中国真正的创新和对丰富能源资源的获取，以及其为规避美国控制而做出的不懈努力。
黄仁勋在唐纳德·特朗普总统的要求下重返英伟达，这表明该公司和白宫似乎对阻止中国强大的人工智能芯片完全不感兴趣。相反，国会将负责确保美国利用其计算优势并保持其人工智能优势。中期选举和两党对 Megaspeed 灾难的担忧日益加剧，为国会提供了纠正方向的新动力。其近期议程应包括关闭

The reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia this week added another twist to a scandal that has transfixed Washington and Silicon Valley. The stakes go beyond the swings of the stock market or the salacious details about Huang’s affairs, including with Alice Huang, a former executive at the Singaporean firm Megaspeed and a potential Chinese asset. At its core, the scandal has exposed something that matters far more than any one man or company: American export-control policy remains riddled with loopholes, hobbled by incapacity and infighting, and divorced from clear strategy. Unless Washington fixes this, it risks imperiling the United States’ hard-won advantage in artificial intelligence.
This export policy failure is more than the sum of specific deficiencies. It stems from the Trump administration’s broader posture on China. Washington has embraced unfettered AI acceleration at the same time as it has struck a more accommodating stance toward Beijing. That combination set the stage for the explosive Megaspeed scandal—and perhaps others that have yet to emerge. As a result, China has been able to access an alarming number of advanced chips that have enabled it to narrow the AI gap with the United States and power its AI-driven military modernization. According to the AI research institute Epoch AI, up to a third of China’s AI computing power may come from smuggled chips. China’s top AI models are now just months behind the U.S. frontier. The narrow gap reflects China’s genuine innovation and access to abundant energy resources as well as its relentless efforts to circumvent U.S. controls.
Huang’s return to Nvidia at the behest of President Donald Trump suggests that both the company and the White House seem utterly uninterested in keeping powerful AI chips from China. It will instead fall to Congress to ensure that the United States leverages its compute advantage and maintains its AI edge. The midterm elections and mounting bipartisan concerns over the Megaspeed debacle give Congress new momentum to correct course. Its near-term agenda should include closing known loopholes that played a key role in allowing Megaspeed to supply advanced chips to China, stepping up enforcement of existing controls, and strengthening oversight of the administration’s export-control decisions.
Over the medium term, Congress must also tackle the broader question of how to balance the strategic benefits of exporting U.S. technology to build the world’s AI infrastructure with robust controls to prevent its leakage to China. The long-standing debate over which American AI chips and capabilities Washington should permit to diffuse globally and under what conditions has finally boiled over into the mainstream—and, in a perverse way, the national security community can thank Alice Huang for forcing the issue.
The issue before Congress, however, is much broader than addressing the specifics of the Nvidia scandal. Congress must also contend with the underlying impulses driving the administration’s China policy and install guardrails to avoid the erosion of U.S. export controls. This means that after Congress passes near-term bills to mop up the Megaspeed mess, it must then take the reins on setting long-term export-control strategy.
Congress cannot stand by idly as AI blazes forward. OpenAI’s top model can now perform professional tasks as well as or better than humans 85 percent of the time, up from just 14 percent in 2024. The time an AI model can independently work on a task is doubling every four months. Last week, a researcher at Anthropic announced that AI helped him untangle the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous problems in pure mathematics.
As capabilities have grown, so have risks. Frontier models can now complete simulated cyberattacks on networks on their own, and hackers are using AI models to partially automate their attacks. In the July incident involving the AI platform Hugging Face, rogue AI agents escaped their testing environment and plotted to evade human oversight, underscoring the difficulty of aligning model behavior with human intent. The growing power of AI and the risks from misuse or loss of control make U.S. leadership a national security imperative.
At its core, the U.S.-Chinese AI competition boils down to which country can deploy the best chips in the highest quantities to train and adopt advanced AI models. The Biden administration’s controls slowed Chinese AI developers by leaving them with fewer, worse chips. Nvidia’s top Blackwell chips are nearly seven times better than Huawei’s Ascend equivalents. By the end of 2026, Huawei will likely have produced less than four percent of the compute that Nvidia will have over the same time. As the founder and CEO of DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI companies, admitted in 2024, “Our problem has never been money—it’s the embargo on high-end chips.”
To circumvent Biden-era restrictions, elaborate networks for smuggling and transshipment emerged to divert chips to China from other countries that could legally acquire them, and Chinese companies leveraged export-control loopholes to remotely access U.S.-powered compute through data centers abroad. Chinese firms funded companies such as Megaspeed to facilitate these workarounds. Backed by the Chinese tech giant Alibaba, Megaspeed has purchased $4 billion worth of Nvidia chips since 2023, prompting an investigation from the U.S. government. Chinese companies also used a technique known as adversarial distillation—training their models on the outputs of top U.S. models at a fraction of the compute. All of this needlessly shrank the United States’ AI lead over China, even after the imposition of export controls.
Congress must take the reins on setting long-term export-control strategy.
These developments should have spurred the Trump administration to better resource, enforce, and update the export controls when it came into office. It did the opposite. In May 2025, the administration suspended the Biden administration’s AI Diffusion Rule, which had established rules for which countries could access advanced chips and in what quantities. Then, after initially prohibiting sales to China of Nvidia’s H20 chip, which was custom-built as a less powerful product for the Chinese market, the Trump administration reversed course in December 2025 and greenlighted the sale of Nvidia’s H200 chip. Although the H200 is two generations behind top U.S. chips, it remains superior to anything China can produce. An investigation from the House Foreign Affairs Committee in November revealed that between December 2025 and May 2026, the Trump administration approved the sale of more than 800,000 of Nvidia’s H200 chips and AMD’s MI325X equivalent, including to companies that the Pentagon has designated as linked to the Chinese military. This week, under pressure from Congress, the administration added Megaspeed to the entity list, which blocks those listed from buying U.S. products without a license—but before that, the administration had not added a single new individual or business to the list in 2026.
This regulatory vacuum and policy incoherence created the perfect conditions for Megaspeed. The Singaporean firm at the center of the Nvidia scandal seems tailor-made to operate in the seams of U.S. export controls. In 2024, the Commerce Department initiated a formal investigation of the company, which could have led to sanctions such as being placed on the entity list. But the Trump administration dragged its feet in pursuing the investigation. In the meantime, Megaspeed stocked Southeast Asian data centers with thousands of U.S. chips, enabling remote access for Chinese firms. This remote access loophole in U.S. export controls was a well-known and increasingly popular workaround for China-linked firms, but the Trump administration left it open for nearly two years and closed it only last week amid pressure from the Nvidia scandal. Regardless of the Megaspeed specifics, the net result of the Trump administration’s actions and inaction is that China has enjoyed access to far more computing power than it should have during a vital period of the AI competition.
The administration’s long-awaited closure of the remote access loophole is a welcome step. The rule requires foreign data centers to secure a license before offering significant computing power to China-based customers. It also requires a license to export advanced chips to places that could facilitate remote access and chip diversion, including Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore. This rule will make it harder for firms such as Megaspeed to import chips in the first place, or to use them to serve China-based customers. But the rule will be difficult to enforce because the U.S. Commerce Department does not have the legal authority under export controls to directly regulate services such as cloud computing. More important, the administration’s lax enforcement of past controls—and internal divisions over the new ones—raise serious questions about its willingness to follow through. Huang’s reinstatement as CEO, with Trump’s backing, will make it harder to vigorously enforce these new controls and move toward a tougher posture on China.
Since Congress cannot rely on the administration to fix export controls and protect the United States’ AI lead, lawmakers should urgently advance bipartisan measures to address the underlying conditions that gave rise to entities such as Megaspeed. As a starting point, Congress should pass the Remote Access Security Act, which would give the administration clear legal authority for controlling remote access to data centers powered by U.S. compute. While implementation will require close congressional oversight, getting the right legal structure in place is an important first step. Next, it should work with industry and technical experts to fund and fast-track “on-chip” technologies—basically, features that can verify a chip’s location and counter smuggling and diversion. Beyond sorting out the technical feasibilities, Congress will need to work with industry to understand the implications of on-chip security mechanisms for global competitiveness and the potential surveillance risks should China develop similar controls since it produces much of the world’s legacy chips.
Along with these technical fixes, Congress should seize on the Megaspeed scandal to strengthen oversight. The AI Overwatch Act, which may be included in the annual defense bill, would codify existing export controls on advanced chips into law, preventing the current or a future administration from reversing them. It would also empower Congress to review and block advanced chips sales to U.S. adversaries. Congress can go even further by establishing a new investigative committee or inspector general to strengthen oversight of sensitive chip export-control policies. Together, these actions would go a long way toward combating the circumvention that let firms such as Megaspeed thrive.
Trump has emphasized summitry optics over pushing China on any sensitive issues.
At the same time, closing loopholes and codifying rules is insufficient to fix the underlying issues that led to the Megaspeed scandal in the first place. This mess is directly downstream from Trump’s dovish shift on China that has seen the administration take a softer line on Beijing just as the AI race accelerated. The administration’s own overreach forced Washington into a conciliatory posture. Administration officials failed to realize that China had learned its lesson from the first Trump administration’s trade wars and was poised to retaliate hard in the second term. After China responded to Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs and export controls with its own punishing controls on rare earths, the Trump administration found its way into a vaguely defined and fragile truce. This has severely constrained U.S. policymaking, including related to compute controls.
Indeed, Trump became an easy sell for advocates of aggressive AI promotion such as Jensen Huang. This camp argues that U.S. leadership in the global AI race requires pushing American AI technologies to as many parts of the globe as possible—including China. They claim that keeping China “addicted” to the U.S. AI stack gives Washington leverage and outweighs the national security concerns that could come with helping China improve its AI capabilities. Huang even pushed demonstrably false narratives that China’s military was not interested in Nvidia’s chips and labeled his critics as “unpatriotic” for not wanting U.S. chips spread as far and wide as possible and therefore depriving American tech firms of global market share.
Trump, who was interested in stabilizing the relationship with China and prioritizing near-term, transactional victories on trade, bought it. He also broke with decades of U.S. foreign policy precedent to negotiate export controls with China. In a series of “do nothing” leader-level meetings since, the president has emphasized summitry optics over pushing China on any sensitive issues. And Huang’s restoration at Nvidia ensures that the president’s worst impulses on China will continue to be egged on by his favored tech CEO, to the detriment of U.S. national security.
A core part of Congress’s longer-term agenda should be outlining the basic principles to determine who can import or remotely access advanced AI chips and under what conditions. Administrations have gone back and forth over this line-drawing exercise. The Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule would have imposed a global licensing regime that controlled not just the export of chips but also the aggregate U.S.-powered compute that any country could receive. Under Trump, only a handful of countries face restrictions. A smarter approach would condition advanced chip sales on the buyer’s ability to protect them from diversion and guard against misuse by malign actors looking to skirt safety and security rules. Allied and partner governments could demonstrate this by developing robust economic security policies to prevent chip diversion or remote access. Foreign companies would have to show strong compliance and security commitments. In practice, this would mean having internal procedures to ensure that chips are not diverted and maintaining cooperation with Commerce Department officials to verify that such procedures were working.
Congress can also help rebuild allies’ confidence in U.S. export-control policy. There was hard-won, if imperfect, progress on allied alignment in key areas of export controls under the Biden administration, notably with the Dutch and the Japanese on controls of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The painstaking work needed to get allies on board can be agonizingly slow, but once achieved, it is far more likely to endure than if the United States imposes extraterritorial controls over their objections. The MATCH Act, one of the bills revived following the Megaspeed scandal, requires controls on allied-produced tools if Washington is unable to negotiate allied alignment. It is a rather rude approach at a moment when U.S. export controls seem to be on shaky footing, U.S. tariffs against allies have pushed relations to a near breaking point, and allies rightly question whether the United States still views China as a strategic threat. Instead, Congress should support efforts to create durable frameworks for allied alignment, such as economic security agreements in key strategic sectors.
A longer-term agenda must include fixing the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, the main agency responsible for administering and enforcing export controls. The bureau has been gutted by dismissals and low morale during the Trump administration, but it has been underresourced for far longer. Congress should increase funding and require modernization of the bureau’s antiquated IT system. Just as important, Congress needs to help insulate policymaking decisions from corporate influence, and it can help by insisting that future Commerce Department officials commit to independent and risk-based decision-making to earn confirmation.
None of these steps will be easy. The president’s support of Huang’s restoration shows that stock market fluctuations weigh more heavily in his decision-making than national security, and the administration is unlikely to welcome increased congressional oversight. The Constitution gives the executive wide deference on matters of foreign policy and national security. But Congress has a role in ensuring that the president faithfully executes the laws and is supported by the right resources, oversight, and strategic priorities. The United States’ AI lead may hinge on whether it meets the moment.

content:
Turnitin 披露影响面向客户的系统的网络攻击
Turnitin 披露影响面向客户的系统的网络攻击
Turnitin 披露影响面向客户的系统的网络攻击
教育技术公司 Turnitin 透露，它检测到涉及某些面向客户的系统的未经授权的活动，并部署了事件响应计划。
首席执行官 Chris Caren 在一份公开声明中表示，正在外部网络安全专家的帮助下调查该事件，并已通知执法部门和网络监管机构。
Turnitin 是一家全球性的大型教育技术公司，以其人工智能生成的写作检测、数字评分、学术研究完整性检查和考试监考而闻名。
据其网站称，其软件已在 185 个国家的 16,000 多个机构使用，为 7100 万学生提供服务。
“我们写这封信是为了让您知道，我们最近发现了涉及某些面向客户的 Turnitin 系统的未经授权的活动，”该平台网站上首席执行官的信中写道。
“发现问题后，我们实施了事件响应计划，与外部网络安全专家展开调查，并通知了执法部门和网络监管机构。”
Turnitin 表示，其系统完全正常运行且使用安全，并指出受影响的系统不会收集政府身份凭证或机构财务信息。
该公司表示，对该事件的调查仍在进行中，并未透露有关未经授权活动的性质和范围的任何细节。
如果您有关于此事件或其他未公开攻击的任何信息，您可以通过 Signal 646-961-3731 或 Tips@bleepingcomputer.com 与我们秘密联系。
Turnitin 继续监控其系统是否有进一步未经授权的活动，这表明现在要保证威胁已被完全消除还为时过早。
该公司尚未透露是否有任何用户数据被访问或被盗、事件发生的时间以及可能有多少人受到影响。
关于 Turnitin 服务可用性，该平台的状态页面显示 2026 年 11 月没有发生任何事件，并且正常运行时间历史记录没有中断。
截至撰写本文时，还没有勒索软件组织公开承认对 Turnitin 的攻击负责。
BleepingComputer 已联系该公司询问有关该事件的问题，但该公司代表表示，他们目前没有更多细节可透露。

Turnitin discloses cyberattack affecting customer-facing systems
Turnitin discloses cyberattack affecting customer-facing systems
Turnitin discloses cyberattack affecting customer-facing systems
Educational technology company Turnitin disclosed that it detected unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing systems and deployed its incident response plan.
In a public statement, CEO Chris Caren says that the incident is being investigated with help from external cybersecurity specialists, and law enforcement and cyber regulators have been notified.
Turnitin is a major education technology firm with a global presence, best known for its AI-generated writing detection, digital grading, academic research integrity checks, and examination proctoring.
According to its website, its software is used in over 16,000 institutions across 185 countries and serves 71 million students.
“We are writing to let you know that we recently identified unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing Turnitin systems,” reads the letter from the CEO on the platform's website.
“Upon identifying the matter, we implemented our incident response plan, initiated an investigation with external cybersecurity specialists, and notified law enforcement and cyber regulators.”
Turnitin says its systems are fully operational and safe to use, noting that the affected systems do not collect government identification credentials or institutional financial information.
The company said its investigation into the incident remains ongoing and has not disclosed any details about the nature and scope of the unauthorized activity.
If you have any information regarding this incident or other undisclosed attacks, you can contact us confidentially via Signal at 646-961-3731 or at tips@bleepingcomputer.com.
Turnitin continues to monitor its systems for further unauthorized activity, indicating that it is still early to guarantee that the threat has been eliminated completely.
The company has not disclosed whether any user data was accessed or stolen, when the incident occurred, and how many individuals might have been impacted.
Regarding Turnitin service availability, the platform’s status page shows no incidents for November 2026, and the uptime history logs no disruptions.
As of writing, no ransomware groups have publicly taken responsibility for the attack at Turnitin.
BleepingComputer has contacted the firm with questions about the incident, but a company representative said they have no additional details to share at this time.

title: China’s Cargo Drones Keep Getting Bigger With New W8000

content:
中国部署越来越大的无人货运飞机的野心正在不断增强，白鲸航空推出了 W8000 货运无人机，据报道，这款货运无人机设计可承载 8 吨（略低于 18,000 磅）。该飞机代表了该公司自主货运航空计划的重大扩展，恰逢其较小的 W5000 已开始飞行测试。参观者在珠海 W8000 前合影。来自中国互联网 W5000（左）停在珠海的 W8000 旁边。来自中国互联网 W8000 在中国国际航空航天博览会（俗称中国航展）之前亮相珠海。在 12 月 7 日该活动开幕之前，我们已经抢先了解了一个平台，该平台旨在将无人货运能力提升到目前仅限于传统载人运输机的水平。据报道，其有效载荷为 8 吨，远高于 W5000，后者的设计载荷可达 5 吨（11,000 磅）。与 W5000 一样，W8000 可以通过后坡道装卸。 W8000 尾部的翻盖式门和后装载坡道。然而目前，双涡轮螺旋桨飞机 W8000 仍然是一个开发概念。其有效载荷数字只是设计目标，其航程、最大起飞重量和操作要求等细节仍不清楚。
为了进行比较，八吨的有效载荷将使 W8000 与 DHC-5 Buffalo 双引擎涡轮螺旋桨短距起降运输机处于同一类别。无论如何，此次亮相凸显了白鲸航空开发一系列大型无人驾驶货运飞机的雄心，目标是区域货运、偏远地区物流和潜在的军事运输任务，在这些任务中，自主飞机可以比传统货运业务提供优势。珠海W8000的后视图。来自中国互联网 双涡轮螺旋桨飞机 W8000 动力装置所使用的发动机尚未确定。通过中国互联网 更大的无人运输 W8000 的有效负载能力将使其能够运输大型设备、托盘货物、工业用品和其他大件货物。在商业环境中，大型自主货运飞机在公路或铁路基础设施有限或传统航空运输过于昂贵而无法频繁运营的航线上特别有用。尽管消除了机上机组人员，但飞机仍然需要维护人员、地勤人员、货物装载基础设施和支持性运营网络。最终，该飞机也可能被批准在受控空域内运行，取代载人支线货运业务，但这种用例在未来仍有一段路要走。不可避免的是，该飞机的发展也表明了大型货运无人机的潜在军事意义。
珠海的 W5000 和 W8000。来自中国互联网 W8000 可以为中国人民解放军 (PLA) 提供大量额外的空运选择，以保障在偏远、孤立或基础设施匮乏的地点作战的部队。这在印度-太平洋地区尤其重要，中国不断扩大的军事设施和岛屿前哨网络已经对频繁的补给飞行产生了需求。例如，在南中国海，大型货运无人机可以将设备、医疗用品、备件和其他必需品运输到远程设施，而无需载人运输

【原文 English Original】
China’s ambitions to field increasingly large, uncrewed cargo aircraft are growing, with Air White Whale unveiling its W8000, a cargo UAV reportedly designed to carry up to eight metric tons — a little less than 18,000 pounds. The aircraft represents a significant expansion of the company’s plans for autonomous freight aviation, coming just as its smaller W5000 has begun flight testing. Visitors pose in front of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W5000 (left) parked next to the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W8000 appeared in Zhuhai, ahead of the China International Aviation & Aerospace Exhibition, commonly known as Airshow China . Before that event opens its doors on December 7, we have gotten an early look at a platform intended to push uncrewed cargo capacity into a class now limited to conventional, crewed transport aircraft. Its reported eight-ton payload would put it substantially above the W5000, which is designed to carry up to five metric tons (11,000 pounds). Like the W5000, the W8000 can be loaded and unloaded via a rear ramp. Clamshell doors and rear loading ramp in the tail of the W8000. via Chinese internet For now, however, the twin-turboprop W8000 remains a developmental concept. Its payload figure is a design target, and details about its range, maximum takeoff weight, and operational requirements are still unclear. For purposes of comparison, an eight-metric-ton payload would put the W8000 in much the same category as the DHC-5 Buffalo twin-engine turboprop STOL transport. Regardless, the unveiling highlights Air White Whale’s ambitions to develop a family of large uncrewed cargo aircraft, targeting regional freight, remote-area logistics, and potentially military transportation missions where autonomous aircraft could offer advantages over conventional cargo operations. Rear view of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The engines used in the powerplant for the twin-turboprop W8000 are yet to be identified. via Chinese internet An Even Bigger Uncrewed Transport The W8000’s payload capacity would allow it to transport large equipment, palletized freight, industrial supplies, and other bulky cargo. In a commercial context, large autonomous cargo aircraft could be particularly useful on routes where road or rail infrastructure is limited, or where conventional air transport is too expensive to operate frequently. Although eliminating onboard flight crews, the aircraft would still require maintenance personnel, ground handling, cargo-loading infrastructure, and a supporting operational network. Ultimately, the aircraft could also be cleared to operate inside controlled airspace, displacing crewed feeder cargo operations, but that use case is still some way off in the future. Inevitably, the aircraft’s development also points toward the potential military relevance of large cargo UAVs. The W5000 and W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet The W8000 could offer the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) a substantial additional airlift option for sustaining forces operating from remote, isolated, or infrastructure-poor locations. This is particularly relevant in the Indo-Pacific, where China’s expanding network of military facilities and island outposts is already creating demand for frequent resupply flights. In the South China Sea, for example, large cargo UAVs could potentially transport equipment, medical supplies, spare parts, and other necessities to remote installations without requiring a crewed transport aircraft for every mission. They could also support operations in western China , including remote and high-altitude regions where road infrastructure is limited and conventional air transport can face additional challenges. There are also potential applications in a conflict, where conventional logistics infrastructure could be damaged or otherwise unavailable. Uncrewed transports would remove the risk to aircrews during routine resupply missions through contested airspace, although the aircraft themselves would remain vulnerable. They would also remove the need for combat search and rescue (CSAR) capabilities, which might be impossible to provide in at least some scenarios. Their usefulness would also depend, at least in some cases, on reliable communications, autonomous navigation, and the ability to operate without continuous access to satellite navigation. Profile view of the W8000 at Zhuhai. via Chinese internet W5000 Has Already Begun Flight Testing The W8000’s unveiling comes as Air White Whale’s smaller W5000 has reached a significant development milestone, completing its maiden flight on November 14. The five-ton cargo UAV reportedly conducted a roughly 30-minute test flight after taking off within approximately 600 meters (1,969 feet). During the flight, it reportedly conducted maneuvers and tested autonomous flight functions, datalink communications, propulsion, and flight-control systems before landing. China’s W5000 large cargo UAV has completed its maiden flight in the Ordos region of Inner Mongolia on 14 November. The aircraft reportedly took off after a 600 m (1,969 ft) ground run, climbed to 2,000 m (6,562 ft) and completed a 30-minute test flight. The trial included… pic.twitter.com/NNLqPKbLLZ — Drone Wars (@Drone_Wars_) November 14, 2026 The W5000 is designed to carry up to five metric tons of cargo, with a reported maximum range of 2,600 kilometers (1,616 miles), maximum takeoff weight of 10.8 tons (21,600 pounds), and cargo compartment volume exceeding 65 cubic meters (2,295 cubic feet). The aircraft is powered by twin turboprop engines. Chinese sources claim that Air White Whale has received 835 orders or prospective commitments from domestic logistics companies for the W5000, although the nature of those commitments and how many represent firm purchase contracts remain unclear. Commercial operations are currently planned to begin by the end of 2027, subject to further testing and certification. The W5000’s flight provides an indication of the company’s progress toward developing large uncrewed cargo aircraft, but the W8000 is a considerably more ambitious undertaking. Several other companies are also pursuing increasingly ambitious uncrewed transport aircraft. These include Tengden’s four-engine TB-001D Scorpion D , which first flew in October 2022 and is designed to carry up to 1.5 metric tons (3,307 pounds) of cargo, as well as the Star UAV System-developed AT200, another 1.5-ton-class cargo drone. The TB0D Scorpion D built by China’s Tengden Technology company completed its maiden flight in Sichuan on October 25, 2022. Twitter video screenshot Other designs include the state-owned Aviation Industry Corporation of China’s HH-100 , with a reported payload capacity of around 700 kilograms (1,543 pounds), and the China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation’s CH-YH1000 , designed to carry approximately one metric ton (2,205 pounds). While these aircraft vary considerably in size, configuration, and intended missions, their development highlights China’s broader push to establish uncrewed cargo aviation as a viable logistics capability. A demonstrator of China’s HH-100 commercial cargo drone. Photo by Yue Shuhua/VCG via Getty Images VCG Outside of China, there is some other notable activity in this sector. The United States is also pursuing large uncrewed cargo aircraft for military logistics. As we reported , Textron Aviation and autonomy specialist Merlin recently unveiled the Cessna SkyCourier UX, a concept based on the twin-engine Cessna 408 SkyCourier. The proposed aircraft would use Merlin’s autonomous flight system and could carry approximately 6,000 pounds of cargo. Its designers are exploring a cockpit-less configuration with a hydraulically opening nose section for direct cargo loading, as well as kneeling landing gear and integrated loading systems to simplify operations at austere locations. With a reported range of around 900 nautical miles, the SkyCourier UX is intended to support distributed military forces, including across the Pacific, where it could move supplies between larger logistics hubs and smaller, remote operating locations. The U.S. Air Force has also experimented with autonomous Cessna Caravan aircraft through Joby Aviation and its former Xwing autonomy team, including logistics demonstrations across the Pacific. Better known for land vehicles, Oshkosh Defense also recently announced a partnership with Silicon Valley startup Grid Aero, with the aim of building large military cargo drones. These would draw upon Grid Aero’s experience developing the Lifter family, an autonomous aircraft series with modular payload capacity that the company describes as a “pickup truck of the skies.” The Lifter is planned to carry somewhere between 1,000 and 8,000 pounds over a distance of approximately 1,500 miles.  The Grid Aero Lifter. Oshkosh/Grid Aero While the United States is moving slower than China in this space, there is arguably an even stronger operational case for such capabilities in the U.S. military, given the expeditionary nature of a potential conflict across the vast distances of the Indo-Pacific . Sustaining forces spread across widely separated islands, remote airfields, and austere forward operating locations would place enormous demands on conventional airlift and sealift networks. China Targets A New Class Of Cargo Aviation Overall, the development of the W5000 and W8000 highlights China’s growing interest in cargo UAVs capable of moving freight measured in metric tons rather than kilograms. While smaller delivery drones are increasingly being explored for last-mile transportation, aircraft such as the W8000 are aimed at moving substantial loads between logistics hubs without requiring an onboard crew. If the W8000 progresses, it could eventually offer a heavier transport option alongside the W5000, allowing Air White Whale to target different cargo requirements and routes. The W5000 and W8000 at Zhuhai ahead of Airshow China. via Chinese internet For now, the W8000 points to where Air White Whale wants to take its cargo UAV program. The W5000’s flight-test program will be an important step in establishing whether the company can turn its designs into operational aircraft and start to offer a new class of uncrewed airlift. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post China’s Cargo Drones Keep Getting Bigger With New W8000 appeared first on TWZ .

title: China warns US against imposing new tariffs
zh_title: 中国警告美国不要征收新关税
summary: 在媒体报道称华盛顿计划宣布对中国和其他国家征收新关税后，北京周三敦促美国“维护贸易关系的稳定发展”。中国外交部发言人郭家坤。资料图：中国外交部。报道称，华盛顿的新征税措施将影响包括中国、欧盟、日本和韩国在内的美国主要贸易伙伴。当被问及华盛顿报道的计划时，中国外交部发言人郭家琨表示：“关税战和贸易战不符合任何人的利益。”
content:
在媒体报道称华盛顿计划宣布对中国和其他国家征收新关税后，北京周三敦促美国“维护贸易关系的稳定发展”。中国外交部发言人郭家坤。资料图：中国外交部。报道称，华盛顿的新征税措施将影响包括中国、欧盟、日本和韩国在内的美国主要贸易伙伴。当被问及华盛顿报道的计划时，中国外交部发言人郭家琨表示：“关税战和贸易战不符合任何人的利益。”他在例行新闻发布会上表示，世界两大经济体于 2025 年在贸易战中达成了脆弱的休战协议，“应该通过协商解决相关问题”。他补充说，对产能过剩的指控——亏损大规模生产以涌入海外市场并削弱当地竞争对手——是“虚假前提”和“政治操纵的借口”。中美双方应共同努力，切实落实两国元首达成的重要共识，维护中美经贸关系稳定发展。唐纳德·特朗普总统长期以来一直批评中国对美国不断扩大的贸易顺差，他将其归咎于当地制造业实力和就业机会的下降。
去年开始第二任期后，特朗普对中国商品征收新关税，引发了与北京针锋相对的升级，关税一度飙升至 145%。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平于 2026 年 11 月 19 日星期四在中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织 (APEC) 会议上。照片：白宫/Daniel Torok。特朗普和中国国家主席习近平于 2025 年 10 月达成的贸易停火协议将于 1 月到期，此前该协议于 9 月同意延长两个月。两人上周在中国南方深圳举行的 APEC 峰会上会面，并将于 12 月在美国举行的 G20 峰会上再次见面。在与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京举行历史性三边会谈之前，习近平在亚太经合组织会议上赞扬了中国与美国“稳定和改善”的关系。中国领导人还表示，中国应该在人工智能领域开展合作，让技术“处于人的控制之下”，防范安全风险。

【原文 English Original】
Beijing urged the United States on Wednesday to “uphold the stable development” of trade relations, after media reports said Washington was planning to announce new tariffs on China and other countries. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun. File Photo: China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs. The reports said that Washington’s new levies would affect major US trading partners including China, the European Union, Japan and South Korea. “Tariff wars and trade wars are not in anyone’s interest,” Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said, when asked about Washington’s reported plans. He told a regular briefing that the world’s two top economies, which in 2025 agreed a tenuous truce in their trade war, “should resolve relevant issues through consultation”. He added that accusations of overcapacity — mass production at a loss to flood overseas markets and undercut local rivals — was a “false premise” and a “pretext for political manipulation”. “China and the United States should work together to effectively implement the important consensus reached by the two heads of state and uphold the stable development of China-US economic and trade relations,” he said. President Donald Trump has long criticised China’s yawning trade surplus with the United States, which he has blamed for a decline in local manufacturing prowess and jobs. After starting a second term in office last year, Trump imposed new tariffs on Chinese goods, kicking off a tit-for-tat escalation with Beijing that at one point saw duties soar as high as 145 percent. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) in Shenzhen, China on Thursday, November 19, 2026. Photo: White House/Daniel Torok. The trade ceasefire struck by Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in October 2025 is due to expire in January, after a two-month extension was agreed in September. The two men met last week at an APEC summit in Shenzhen in southern China and are due to see each other again in December at a G20 summit in the United States. During their meeting at APEC, which came just before a historic trilateral with Russian President Vladimir Putin, Xi hailed China’s “stable and improved” ties with the United States. The Chinese leader also said that his country should cooperate in the field of artificial intelligence, keeping the technology “under human control” and guarding against safety risks.

title: Beijing slams US for ‘suppressing’ Chinese firms after Huawei conviction

content:
周三，在美国陪审团裁定科技巨头华为窃取商业机密并就其在伊朗的工作向监管机构撒谎后，北京猛烈抨击美国“打压”中国企业。华为总部位于深圳。照片：华为。全球领先的电信设备制造商华为已成为唐纳德·特朗普总统政府的攻击目标，经过三个月的审判后，华为于周二在纽约联邦法院被定罪。这项裁决是在美国和中国的政治敏感时期做出的，两国领导人上周在深圳会晤时试图展现特朗普所说的“奇妙”关系。陪审团裁定华为面临 12 项刑事罪名中的 10 项罪名成立，包括银行欺诈、合谋窃取商业机密以及合谋诈骗美国。中国周三予以回击，称“坚决反对美国打压和围堵中国企业，坚定支持中国企业维护合法权益”。特朗普政府长期以来一直声称华为存在代表中国政府从事间谍活动的风险，并此前敦促各国不要在新的 5G 移动网络中使用该公司的基础设施。 “没有任何人或公司可以凌驾于法律之上，”美国司法部长托德·布兰奇在定罪后的一份声明中表示。
“几十年来，华为及其三个子公司在谎言和盗窃的基础上在美国开展业务。”美国和中国国旗。资料图片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。华为周三驳回了这一判决，并在一份声明中表示，该判决“没有法律或事实依据”。 “我们将彻底审查相关判决，并采取一切必要的法律行动来捍卫我们的权益，”它补充道。 “必要的法律行动” 然而，陪审团确实宣判华为无罪，该公司表示，此举“欢迎”，并补充说，它“证实了这些指控缺乏事实依据，并证明了我们在过去八年中的一贯立场。” “我们认为政府的其余指控同样没有法律或事实依据……我们将彻底审查相关判决，并采取一切必要的法律行动来捍卫我们的权益，”声明继续说道。这些指控部分涉及华为与伊朗政府的业务往来。美国司法部表示：“华为多次对其在伊朗业务的性质撒谎，错误地告诉银行、记者和美国政府，它没有协助伊朗政府、军队或情报部门。”
“华为向银行谎报其在伊朗的活动，以获得数十亿美元并获得美元清算服务，这使华为成为全球电信服务市场的成熟参与者——部分原因是它的谎言。”这家设备制造商还被指控试图招募美国电信公司的员工，并在此过程中从他们那里获取技术信息。根据最初的起诉书，这些数据据称使华为能够开发与其竞争对手类似的产品，然后以较低的价格出售。资料图片：维基百科。美国司法部在一份新闻稿中表示：“被盗用的知识产权包括商业秘密信息和受版权保护的作品，例如互联网路由器的源代码和用户手册、天线技术和机器人测试技术。”华为甚至还推出了一款inter

【原文 English Original】
Beijing lashed out at the United States on Wednesday for “suppressing” Chinese companies, after a US jury found tech giant Huawei guilty of stealing trade secrets and lying to regulators over its work in Iran. Huawei headquarters in Shenzhen. Photo: Huawei. Huawei, the world’s leading telecom equipment manufacturer, has been targeted by President Donald Trump’s administration, and was convicted on Tuesday in a New York federal court after a three-month trial. The ruling comes at a politically sensitive time for the United States and China, whose leaders sought to project what Trump called a “fantastic” relationship when they met in Shenzhen last week. Jurors found Huawei guilty of 10 of the 12 criminal counts facing it — including bank fraud, conspiracy to steal trade secrets and conspiracy to defraud the United States. China hit back on Wednesday, saying it “firmly opposes the US suppressing and containing Chinese enterprises and firmly supports Chinese enterprises in safeguarding their legitimate rights and interests.” Trump’s administration has long alleged a risk of Huawei spying on behalf of the Chinese government, and previously urged countries not to use the company’s infrastructure in new 5G mobile networks. “No person or company is above the law,” US Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement after the conviction. “For decades, Huawei and three of its subsidiaries conducted their business in the United States on the basis of lies and theft.” The US and Chinese flag. File photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Huawei rejected the conviction on Wednesday, saying in a statement it was “without legal or factual merit.” “We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests,” it added. ‘Necessary legal actions’ The jury did, however, acquit Huawei of racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice, a move the company said it “welcomed,” adding that it “confirms that these allegations lack factual basis and vindicates our consistent position over the past eight years.” “We believe the government’s remaining charges are equally without legal or factual merit… We will thoroughly review the relevant verdicts and take all necessary legal actions to defend our rights and interests,” the statement continued. The charges in part involved Huawei’s business dealings with the government of Iran. “Huawei repeatedly lied about the nature of its business in Iran, falsely telling banks, journalists, and the US government that it did not assist Iran’s government, military, or intelligence community,” the DOJ said. “Huawei lied about its activities in Iran to banks to obtain billions of US dollars and access to US-dollar clearing services, which enabled Huawei to be a sophisticated participant in a global marketplace for telecommunications services — in part because of its lies.” The equipment manufacturer was also accused of attempting to recruit employees of US telecoms firms and obtaining technological information from them in the process. That data allegedly enabled Huawei to develop products similar to those of its competitors, which it then sold at lower prices, according to the original indictment. File photo: Wikipedia. “The misappropriated intellectual property included trade secret information and copyrighted works, such as source code and user manuals for internet routers, antenna technology, and robot testing technology,” the DOJ said in a release. Huawei even launched an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors, prosecutors claimed. “Today’s verdict sends an unmistakable message: America will defend its businesses, protect its workers, and safeguard its national security against corrupt foreign corporations that lie, cheat, and steal to get ahead,” Assistant Attorney General A. Tysen Duva said in a statement.

title: Hong Kong rules out government-run matchmaking services amid low birth rate, delayed marriages
zh_title: 由于出生率低、晚婚，香港排除政府经营的婚介服务
summary: 一名政府官员表示，香港当局不会效仿新加坡等国家推出婚介服务来解决晚婚和低出生率问题。一对情侣在西九龙的港口接吻。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。民政及青年事务局局长麦家丽周三在书面答复立法会议员朱汉基有关家庭政策的问题时表示，政府知道其他司法管辖区已推出“官方或准官方的婚介活动”。 “鉴于社会背景、人口结构、制度等方面的差异，
content:
一名政府官员表示，香港当局不会效仿新加坡等国家推出婚介服务来解决晚婚和低出生率问题。一对情侣在西九龙的港口接吻。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。民政及青年事务局局长麦家丽周三在书面答复立法会议员朱汉基有关家庭政策的问题时表示，政府知道其他司法管辖区已推出“官方或准官方的婚介活动”。 “鉴于各地社会背景、人口结构、制度体系等差异，相关经验不一定适用于香港。”麦说。她补充说，从约会到结婚的转变涉及“许多不同的因素和个人考虑”。香港中环斑马线上的人们。照片：香港政府一站通。 “是否组建家庭的最终决定并不一定取决于是否组织相亲活动，”她说。与许多发达城市一样，香港近几十年来也出现了推迟结婚的趋势。 2006年，25岁至29岁之间的未婚男性比例为81%。到2021年，这一比例已增至87%。对于同一年龄段的女性，这一数字从 68% 上升至 76%。从未结婚的人数也有所增加，而登记结婚的人数却有所下降。情人节相亲？
9月，新加坡政府为政府工作人员试行了一项婚介服务。该平台名为FirstDate，承诺结束“刷卡疲劳”并提供“不同的约会方式”。它向年龄在 21 岁至 45 岁之间为政府工作的人开放。根据 FirstDate 的网站，用户必须使用政府颁发的身份证明进行注册，并填写一份调查问卷，询问他们的“兴趣、习惯、价值观和偏好”。朱询问香港是否也会举办“相亲节活动，并允许参加者向政府报销部分相亲费用”。新加坡。照片：Virginia Chien，来自 Pexels。他还建议政府可以将此类举措与情人节结合起来，并补贴非营利组织和地区团体提供约会活动。楚说，社区中“私人约会服务”的质量参差不齐，并补充说，这削弱了“单身人士使用这些服务的信心”。香港生育率下降一直是政府近年来的政策重点。 2023年，推出“婴儿奖金”计划，为每个新生儿的家庭发放2万港元。 9月，政府将奖励金额提高至3万港元，并增加了家长的税收优惠。香港民意研究所2024年的一项调查发现，香港的教育制度和政治是香港人不想要孩子的主要原因。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong authorities will not follow countries like Singapore in launching matchmaking services to address delayed marriages and low birth rates, a government official has said. A couple kiss by the harbour in West Kowloon. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Secretary for Home and Youth Affairs Alice Mak said in a written reply on Wednesday to lawmaker Roy Chu’s questions about family policies that the government was aware that other jurisdictions had launched “official or quasi-official matchmaking activities.” “Given the differences in social backgrounds, demographic structures, and institutional systems across different places, the relevant experience may not be necessarily applicable to Hong Kong,” Mak said. She added that the move from dating to marriage involves “many different factors and personal considerations.” People at a zebra crossing in Central, Hong Kong. Photo: GovHK. “The ultimate decision on whether to start a family does not necessarily hinge on whether matchmaking activities are organised,” she said. Like many developed cities, Hong Kong has seen a trend of marriage postponement in recent decades. The percentage of unmarried men aged between 25 and 29 was 81 per cent in 2006. By 2021, it had increased to 87 per cent. For women of the same age group, the figure rose from 68 per cent to 76 per cent. The number of people who have never been married has also increased, while the number of registered marriages has fallen. Valentine’s Day matchmaking? In September, the Singapore government piloted a matchmaking service for government workers. Named FirstDate, the platform promised an end to “swipe fatigue” and a “different approach” to dating. It was open to people aged between 21 and 45 who work for the government. According to FirstDate’s website, users must sign up with their government-issued identification and fill in a questionnaire that asks about their “interests, habits, values and preferences.” Chu asked if Hong Kong would also organise “matchmaking festival activities and allow participants to claim reimbursement from the Government for part of their dating expenses.” Singapore. Photo: Virginia Chien, via Pexels. He also suggested the government could combine such initiatives with Valentine’s Day, as well as subsidise non-profit-making and district groups to offer dating activities. The quality of “private dating services” in the community varies, Chu said, adding that this undermines the “confidence of single persons in using them.” Hong Kong’s falling fertility rates have been a policy focus for the government in recent years. In 2023, it introduced a “baby bonus” scheme, giving HK$20,000 to families for every newborn. In September, the government raised the incentive to HK$30,000, and also increased tax concessions for parents. A 2024 survey by the Hong Kong Public Opinion Research Institute found that the city’s education system and politics were the main reasons why Hongkongers did not want children.

title: Hong Kong gov’t response to Tai Po fire reflects responsibility and ‘strong resolve,’ Beijing says
zh_title: 北京表示，香港政府对大埔火灾的反应体现了责任感和“坚定决心”
summary: 北京赞扬香港政府在致命的大埔火灾后承担全部责任并表现出“坚强决心”，并列举了灾后救援工作和系统性改革计划。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔宏福苑发生火灾的第二天，人们看到浓烟滚滚。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港澳门事务办公室（港澳办）周二在评论中表示，香港政府已对悲剧的“痛苦”进行反思。政府加快了改革步伐，以解决“长期存在”的缺陷，包括
content:
北京赞扬香港政府在致命的大埔火灾后承担全部责任并表现出“坚强决心”，并列举了灾后救援工作和系统性改革计划。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔宏福苑发生火灾的第二天，人们看到浓烟滚滚。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。香港澳门事务办公室（港澳办）周二在评论中表示，香港政府已对悲剧的“痛苦”进行反思。政府加快了改革步伐，以解决“长期存在”的缺陷，包括建筑维护制度方面的漏洞以及政府部门之间责任不明确的问题。 “政府正在‘刮骨解毒’，”港澳办写道。该评论的发表是在宏福苑火灾周年纪念日前两天发表的，去年 11 月，宏福苑在政府资助的住宅小区发生火灾，造成 168 人死亡。当时该庄园正在进行大规模的改造工程。不符合消防安全标准的不合格建筑材料被发现导致了火灾的迅速蔓延。独立调查委员会的一份报告还强调了承包商和顾问串通赢得项目的串通投标行为。有关宏福苑维修工程的招标文件。照片：James Lee/HKFP。
港澳办表示，自10月份政府委派委员会发布报告后，当局宣布了新措施，向公众道歉，并追究政治责任。评论称，“这一切充分体现了特区政府迅速、务实、正面推进改革的坚强决心和果断行动”。警惕“别有用心”敦促北京驻香港联络办公室周二发表类似评论，称香港当局为受害者安排了长期住房计划，并“大胆推出系统性改革”。该办公室写道：“（政府）正在突破瓶颈，开辟新前景，同时展现善治新时代。”北京驻香港联络处。照片：维基共享资源。报告补充说，过去一年，政府“赢得了香港社会，特别是受害者本身的广泛认可”。周四没有官方纪​​念活动纪念致命火灾一周年。周二，政务司司长陈家祥表示，当局不会举办任何官方哀悼活动，并补充说社区活动已经在进行中。他还表示，政府不会阻碍“合法”的纪念活动。本月早些时候，计划举行纪念弥撒的天主教堂领导人表示，他们收到了警方的询问。
港澳办在评论中表示，香港必须警惕“别有用心”的人图谋“兴风作浪，破坏社会稳定”。它还补充说，煽动针对政府的袭击是不会容忍的。周三，保安局局长邓克里斯表示，警方有必要对纪念活动进行调查，以评估风险并防止“煽动”行为。

【原文 English Original】
Beijing has praised the Hong Kong government for taking full responsibility and exhibiting “strong resolve” in the aftermath of the deadly Tai Po fire , citing post-disaster relief efforts and plans for systemic reforms. People watch smoke coming from Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on November 27, 2025, a day after the fire broke out at the housing estate. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office (HKMAO) said in a commentary on Tuesday that the city’s government had reflected on the “pain” of the tragedy. The government had accelerated overhauls to fix “long-standing” flaws, including loopholes in building maintenance regimes and unclear accountability across government departments. “The government is ‘scraping the bone to cure the poison,'” the HKMAO wrote. The commentary’s publication comes two days before the anniversary of the Wang Fuk Court fire, which killed 168 people when it broke out in the government-subsidised housing estate last November. The estate was undergoing a large-scale renovation project at the time. Substandard construction materials that did not meet fire safety standards were found to have contributed to the blaze’s rapid spread. The practice of bid-rigging, where contractors and consultants collude to win projects, was also highlighted in a report by an independent probe committee. Tender documents relating to the Wang Fuk Court maintenance works. Photo: James Lee/HKFP. The HKMAO said that, after the release of the government-appointed committee’s report in October, authorities had announced new measures, apologised to the public, and taken political accountability. “All of this fully demonstrates the SAR government’s strong resolve and decisive action in driving forward reforms swiftly, pragmatically, and head-on,” the commentary read. Vigilance against ‘ulterior motives’ urged Beijing’s liaison office in Hong Kong issued a similar commentary on Tuesday, writing that the city’s authorities arranged long-term housing plans for the victims and “boldly introduced systemic reforms.” “[The government is] breaking through bottlenecks and opening up new prospects, while demonstrating a new era of good governance,” the office wrote. Beijing’s liaison office in Hong Kong. Photo: Wikicommons. It added that, over the past year, the government had “won broad recognition across Hong Kong society, especially among the victims themselves.” No official commemorations Thursday marks one year since the deadly blaze. On Tuesday, Chief Secretary for Administration Eric Chan said that authorities would not host any official mourning events, adding that activities in the community were already underway. He also said the government would not obstruct “lawful” memorials. Earlier this month, leaders of Catholic churches that planned memorial masses said they received enquiries from police . The HKMAO said in its commentary that the city must be vigilant against people with “ulterior motives” planning to “stir up trouble and disrupt social stability.” It added that incitement of attacks against the government would not be tolerated. On Wednesday, Secretary for Security Chris Tang said police enquiries about memorial events were necessary for risk assessment and to prevent “seditious” acts.

title: Tai Po fire: Hong Kong security chief defends police enquiries surrounding memorial events citing ‘sedition’ risks
zh_title: 大埔火灾：香港保安局局长为警方围绕纪念活动的调查辩护，称存在“煽动叛乱”风险
summary: 香港保安局局长邓克里斯在周四大埔致命火灾周年纪念活动之前为警方的调查进行了辩护，称这些调查对于进行风险评估和防止“煽动”行为是必要的。保安局局长邓克里斯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025年11月26日，大埔宏福苑七栋住宅楼发生大火，造成168人死亡、数千人流离失所。由法官戴维·洛克（David Lok）担任主席的独立委员会成立了，以调查起火原因。唐周三在广播节目中表示，当局采取“
content:
香港保安局局长邓克里斯在周四大埔致命火灾周年纪念活动之前为警方的调查进行了辩护，称这些调查对于进行风险评估和防止“煽动”行为是必要的。保安局局长邓克里斯。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025年11月26日，大埔宏福苑七栋住宅楼发生大火，造成168人死亡、数千人流离失所。由法官戴维·洛克（David Lok）担任主席的独立委员会成立了，以调查起火原因。唐周三在广播节目中表示，当局采取“基于风险的方法”，并负责评估任何纪念活动的范围，包括其形式、预期参与人数和潜在风险。唐发表此番言论之前，警方于本月早些时候对两座天主教堂进行了调查，这两座教堂正计划为这场致命火灾举行追悼会。大埔圣母无原罪圣心堂后来将周年纪念弥撒改为为“过去一年去世的兄弟姐妹”举行的一般仪式，教区居民和参加者表示此举是迫于当局压力的结果。唐周三表示，当局必须防止恶意行为者“利用特殊日期进行煽动行为”。致命火灾后的宏福苑，2026 年 4 月 23 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
“仍然有人说政府收购宏福苑是为了高价出售土地。这显然是错误的，政府已经明确表示该土地将用于社会设施，”邓用粤语说。 “是否有人继续以这种方式煽动社会不稳定？我们有责任（知道），”他补充道。唐说，只要合法，纪念活动都是允许的，但他警告说，可能有人别有用心地试图“劫持”此类活动。他没有具体说明是谁。当被问及警方是否会敦促高风险活动的组织者取消活动时，唐表示，当局只会提醒他们潜在的风险，例如网上出现任何暗示可能造成干扰的评论。他说，当局没有统计有多少活动被取消，并补充说，这取决于组织者的决定。上周，一场旨在分享火灾中移民幸存者故事的新书发布会在原定举行前一天被取消。

【原文 English Original】
Hong Kong’s security chief Chris Tang has defended police enquiries ahead of memorial events marking Thursday’s anniversary of the deadly Tai Po fire , calling them necessary to conduct risk assessments and prevent “seditious” acts. Secretary for Security Chris Tang. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On November 26, 2025, a blaze engulfed seven residential towers at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, killing 168 people and displacing thousands. An independent committee chaired by Justice David Lok was set up to examine what caused the fire. Speaking on a radio programme on Wednesday, Tang said authorities take a “risk-based approach” and are responsible for assessing the scope of any memorial event, including its format, expected turnout and potential risks. Tang’s remarks followed police enquiries earlier this month into two Catholic churches planning memorial services for the deadly blaze. One church, the Immaculate Heart of Mary Church in Tai Po , has since replaced the anniversary mass with a general service for “the brothers and sisters who died in the past year,” with parishioners and attendees suggesting that the move was the result of pressure from the authorities. Risk of ‘seditious acts’ Tang said on Wednesday that authorities had to prevent malicious actors from “using the special date to conduct seditious acts.” Wang Fuk Court after deadly fire, April 23, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. “Some people are still saying that the government acquired Wang Fuk Court to sell the land at a high price. This is clearly false and the government has made it very clear that the land will be used for social facilities,” Tang said in Cantonese. “Is anyone continuing to incite social instability in this way? It is our responsibility [to know],” he added. Tang said memorial events are permitted as long as they are lawful, but warned that there might be people who seek to “hijack” such events with ulterior motives. He did not specify who. Asked whether police would urge organisers of high-risk events to call them off, Tang said authorities would only remind them of potential risks, such as the emergence of any online comments suggesting possible disruption. He said authorities do not keep a tally of how many events have been called off, adding that it is up to organisers to decide. Last week, a book launch set to share stories from migrant survivors of the fire was called off, a day before it was scheduled to take place.

title: After Putin’s photo op, Europe must rejoin great-power diplomacy

content:
封面图片：图片联盟/SIPA|弗拉基米尔·普京、习近平和唐纳德·特朗普在深圳的会晤以领导人发表简短的“和平宣言”结束，然后回家。普京与习近平和特朗普并肩作战，旨在恢复俄罗斯作为不可或缺大国的地位，这一形象自 2022 年以来就已丧失。俄罗斯在继续对乌克兰发动战争的过程中，在外交上仍处于部分孤立状态。然而在深圳，中国将自己定位为世界事务的三个仲裁者之一。和平宣言并没有建立新的世界秩序。但它确实开始使这样的想法正常化：美国、中国和俄罗斯可以在没有欧洲、乌克兰或其他直接受影响国家参与的情况下讨论和平、能源、国际正义和核风险。其措辞也故意含糊其辞，提及联合国改革、稳定能源流动、抵制国际法院“滥用管辖权”以及减少核风险对话。这些都不需要时间表、核查机制、谈判授权或具体承诺。这使得俄罗斯、中国和美国可以随心所欲地使用“和平”、“改革”和“稳定”。毫无疑问，他们的定义与欧洲的定义截然不同。解决方案 欧洲各国政府应将深圳宣言视为警告，而不是突破。他们应该拒绝莫斯科获得主要奖品：欧洲和乌克兰是其中的对象而不是参与者的大国格局。
首先，欧洲各国政府应坚持认为，任何影响欧洲安全的讨论都应以欧洲国家和乌克兰为主体。任何关于结束俄罗斯在乌克兰战争的安排都不应越过基辅进行谈判。其次，欧洲各国政府应提出详细的反议程：加强集体安全和问责制的联合国改革；能源安全不使俄罗斯供应链合法化；对国际正义的明确立场；包括中国在内的减少核风险，但不奖励其核武库扩张。第三，欧洲各国政府应通过欧盟和北约进行协调。莫斯科将尝试利用欧盟成员国之间的分歧，分别与各国政府打交道。共同立场是对抗分而治之的最佳防御。背景普京、习近平和特朗普在深圳亚太经合组织会议期间举行的首次正式峰会没有产生什么实质性成果。在乌克兰、伊朗、军备控制、贸易或台湾问题上没有达成和解。然而，对于普京来说，这是一次公共关系的成功。与习近平和特朗普平等地亮相，强化了克里姆林宫对国内和全球南方受众的主张，即俄罗斯是世界政治的核心。乌克兰缺乏公众压力对莫斯科同样有价值，它可以提出大国讨价还价，而不是乌克兰主权，作为结束战争的框架。这反过来又使乌克兰成为欧洲安全秩序更大谈判中的一个项目。
此次峰会的重要性取决于以下因素：核对话能否达成议程、时间表和核查； “联合国改革”是加强还是削弱问责制；能源合作是否成为俄罗斯供应链依赖的掩护；深圳没有成为“新雅尔塔”，但这表明普京仍然渴望得到一个。来源

【原文 English Original】
Cover image: picture alliance / SIPA | Apaimages Problem Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump’s meeting in Shenzhen ended with the leaders issuing a short “declaration toward peace”—and going home. Putin, sitting alongside Xi and Trump, aimed to restore Russia as an indispensable great power, an appearance that has been lost since 2022. Russia remains partially isolated diplomatically as it continues its war against Ukraine. Yet in Shenzhen, the country projected itself as one of three arbiters of world affairs. The peace declaration did not create a new world order. But it did begin to normalise the idea that the US, China and Russia can discuss peace, energy, international justice and nuclear risk without Europe, Ukraine or other directly affected states at the table. Its language was also deliberately vague, with references to UN reform, stable energy flows, resistance to “jurisdiction abuse” by international courts and dialogue on nuclear-risk reduction. None of these require a timetable, verification mechanism, negotiating mandate or concrete commitment. This leaves Russia, China and the US free to use “peace,” “reform” and “stability” as they wish. No doubt their definitions would differ sharply from Europe’s. Solution European governments should treat the Shenzhen declaration as a warning, not a breakthrough. They should deny Moscow the main prize: a great-power format in which Europe and Ukraine are objects rather than participants. First, European governments should insist that any discussion affecting European security includes European states and Ukraine as principals. No arrangement on ending Russia’s war in Ukraine should be negotiated over Kyiv’s head. Second, European governments should offer a detailed counter-agenda: UN reform that strengthens collective security and accountability; energy security that does not legitimise Russian supply chains; a clear position on international justice; and nuclear-risk reduction that includes China without rewarding its arsenal expansion. Third, European governments should coordinate through the EU and NATO. Moscow will try to deal with capitals separately, exploiting differences among EU member states. A common position is the best defence against divide-and-rule. Context The first formal summit between Putin, Xi and Trump, on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen, produced little of substance. There were no settlements on Ukraine, Iran, arms control, trade or Taiwan. For Putin, however, it was a public relations success. Appearing as an equal alongside Xi and Trump reinforced the Kremlin’s claim, for domestic and global south audiences, that Russia is central to world politics. The absence of public pressure over Ukraine was equally valuable to Moscow, which could present great-power bargaining, rather than Ukrainian sovereignty, as the framework for ending the war. This, in turn, makes Ukraine one item in a larger bargain about Europe’s security order. The summit’s importance will depend on what follows: whether the nuclear dialogue gains an agenda, timetable and verification; whether “UN reform” strengthens or weakens accountability; whether energy cooperation becomes cover for Russian supply-chain dependence; and whether Ukraine is included as a sovereign participant. Shenzhen did not become a “new Yalta”, but it shows that Putin is still eager to get one. Source

title: Local Elections to set Stage for Taiwan’s Next President

content:
摘要：台湾 11 月 28 日的地方选举重点关注民生问题，包括交通、住房负担能力、基础设施和社会福利。他们还将塑造 2028 年总统选举之前的政治格局。结果将反映选民对赖清德总统领导下的现任民进党政府的满意度。强劲的表现将表明该党能够在台湾南部的传统据点之外维持支持。国民党目前占据 22 个最高行政职位中的 16 个。台北、新北和台中的关键选举结果将影响2028年的候选人名单，其中包括现任台中市长卢秀妍和台北市长蒋万安。台湾人民党 (TPP) 正在合作推翻民进党候选人，不过结果将决定这种合作是否持续到 2028 年。北京的干预并不是这次选举的主要话题，但它提供了竞选资金，创建了机器人账户来影响媒体叙事，并对与民进党结盟的个人进行跨国镇压。台湾将于11月28日举行四年来首次地方选举。
近2000万符合资格的成年人（20岁或以上）将投票选出从市长、县长到当地村长的九个职位的代表，因此俗称“九合一选举”。地方选举通常关注基础设施发展和电价等民生问题。今年也不例外，候选人强调解决生活成本和生活质量问题的政策。台湾的党派政治不太关注意识形态，而是关注实际问题和政治人物，因此候选人的日常媒体露面和政策辩论在选民心目中的影响力更大。房间里的大象是迫在眉睫的总统选举，定于 2028 年初举行，九合一选举将有助于奠定基础。这是因为，无论哪个政党在 11 月份脱颖而出，都将为在地方一级获得多数席位的政党提供动力，而且地方政治也为通往国家办公室提供了共同的垫脚石。该国的集权化，加上其规模较小，为市长——特别是直辖市的市长——提供了一条相当直接的通往国家级权力的道路。其强大的媒体环境，对地方政客的频繁报道，也支持了他们的崛起。

【原文 English Original】
Executive Summary: Taiwan’s local elections on November 28 are focused on bread-and-butter issues, including transportation, housing affordability, infrastructure, and social welfare. They will also shape the political landscape leading up to the 2028 presidential elections. Results will reflect voter satisfaction with the incumbent Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) administration under President Lai Ching-te. A strong showing will be a sign that the party is able to maintain support beyond its traditional stronghold in Southern Taiwan. The Kuomintang (KMT) currently holds 16 of the 22 top executive posts. Outcomes of key races in Taipei, New Taipei, and Taichung will affect its pool of candidates for 2028, including current Taichung mayor Lu Shiow-yen and Taipei mayor Chiang Wan-an. The Taiwan People’s Party (TPP) is cooperating to unseat DPP candidates, though results will determine whether that cooperation continues through to 2028. Beijing’s interference is not a major talking point in this election, but it has provided campaign funds, created bot accounts to influence media narratives, and engaged in transnational repression against individuals aligned with the DPP. Taiwan is set to hold local elections for the first time in four years on November 28. Nearly 20 million eligible adults (those aged 20 or older) will vote for representatives in nine positions ranging from city mayors and county magistrates down to local village chiefs—hence the colloquial name the “nine-in-one elections” (九合一選舉). Local elections typically focus on bread-and-butter issues such as infrastructure development and electricity prices. This year is no different, with candidates emphasizing policies to tackle cost-of-living and quality-of-life concerns. Partisan politics in Taiwan is less focused on ideology than on practical issues and political personalities, and so candidates’ day-to-day media appearances and policy debates carry more weight in the minds of voters. The elephant in the room is the looming presidential election, scheduled for early 2028, for which the nine-in-one elections will help set the stage. This is because candidates who come out on top in November will provide momentum for whichever party manages to secure a majority at the local level, and because local politics also provides a common stepping stone to national office. The country’s centralization, coupled with its small size, provides mayors—specifically those of special municipalities (直轄市)—a fairly direct path to national-level prominence. Its robust media environment, which provides frequent coverage of local-level politicians, also supports their ascendance. Candidates Campaign on Bread-and-Butter Issues Going into this cycle, the Kuomintang (KMT) holds 16 of 22 top local executive posts. This makes it somewhat vulnerable, as it has more seats to lose, including swing cities and counties such as New Taipei, Taichung, and Changhua. The Democratic Progressive Party (DPP), meanwhile, holds five jurisdictions, all of which are located in the South, a traditional stronghold. Although the DPP might have more to gain, its recent record in local elections is a cautionary one. The party suffered a heavy defeat in 2018 and another poor showing in 2022 led to former Taiwan president Tsai Ing-wen (蔡英文) resigning as party chair ( Taiwan Television [TTV] , November 26, 2022). Kinmen, the only other county, is held by an independent that briefly joined the Taiwan People’s Party (TPP). For these elections, the TPP has decided to cooperate with the KMT in a “blue-white coalition” (藍白合), and is contesting only the Chiayi County magistrate election. Local campaigns tend to focus on the day-to-day issues that fall within the purview of local governments, such as urban renewal and transportation development. Housing affordability is a major issue in Taiwan, especially in the north, and some candidates have unveiled plans to construct more public housing, with priority given to young people who do not own property ( United Daily News [UDN] , November 20). Others are promising new transportation infrastructure. In New Taipei, for instance, KMT candidate Lee Shu-chuan (李四川) has proposed a metro line crossing the Dahan River and light-rail connections linking Linkou, Bali, and Tamsui with the nearby Taoyuan Metro network ( Mirror Media , July 31). In Taichung, KMT candidate Johnny Chiang (江啟臣), who is currently deputy speaker of the Legislative Yuan, is proposing a “20-minute city” (20分鐘生活圈) in which residents can access essential services close to home. His opponent, DPP legislator Ho Hsin-chun (何欣純), is running on a platform to reduce traffic congestion and make improvements to the city’s transportation system ( UDN , September 15; Ho Hsin-chun Campaign Office , accessed November 12). Demographic challenges are also prominent. Taiwan has had declining birth rates and an aging population since the 2010s, but people are only now starting to feel the economic impact of these changes. As municipal governments are responsible for much of the service delivery for social welfare, candidates are responding to a growing demand for childcare, maternal health services, hospice care, and migrant caregiver policies. These issues are particularly relevant to younger voters, who face rising housing costs and the financial burden of supporting older family members ( Now News , November 23). Alongside the nine-in-one elections, voters are asked to decide on specific national issues at the polls. Unusually, the franchise is expanded for these referenda to those aged 18 and 19. This year, the issue on the ballot is whether to use nuclear power to revitalize the economy, overturning the Tsai Ing-wen government’s “nuclear-free homeland” (非核家園) policy. Nuclear energy has been a topic of perennial political contestation in Taiwan. The latest referendum—the fourth on the issue since 2018—comes on the heels of Taiwan becoming “nuclear-free” in 2025, when its last reactor reached the end of its 40-year lifespan ( China Brief , August 23, 2024; Taiwan Central News Agency [CNA] , November 12). President Lai Ching-te (賴清德) has previously indicated openness to restarting nuclear energy production, saying that he “does not wish to exclude any particular energy source due to ideology” (不要因為意識形態，而排除任何一種能源) ( UDN , October 16). Elections to set Stage for 2028 The upcoming election will likely have a significant impact on how parties approach 2028. This is particularly true for the KMT, who will use the vote to assess candidates’ viability for the country’s highest office. Lai will likely attempt to seek a second term for the DPP, while the TPP will have choices to make depending on both its own performance and that of the KMT. The six special municipalities (直轄市)—Taipei, New Taipei, Taoyuan, Taichung, Tainan, and Kaohsiung—are politically the most consequential. These cities account for the majority of the population and of economic activity on the island, and their mayors have greater national visibility than other local officials. Among these, the Taipei mayor is the most prominent. Three of five previous presidents had previously served in this role, while others have gone on to chair their respective political parties ( GTI , October 30). Some see the KMT incumbent, Chiang Wan-an (蔣萬安), as a torchbearer for a younger KMT, and pundits—including former 2024 vice presidential candidate Jaw Shaw-kong (趙少康)—have speculated about a 2028 presidential run ( TTV News , October 20). But even though Taipei is traditionally a stronghold for the KMT, Chiang has seen his polling numbers slip to an innovative campaign by DPP challenger Shen Pao-yang (沈伯洋; a.k.a. Puma Shen). Shen, whose campaign is colloquially called “ocean current” (洋流), punning on a homophone of his name, has overcome a more than 20-point deficit over the last six months, making the race too close to call ( SET News , May 7; TVBS , May 27; Initium Media , November 17).  [1] His popularity has even led other DPP candidates to vie for joint appearances, in the hope of boosting their own chances ( Liberty Times [LTN] , November 23). Taichung will be a key bellwether for the KMT, where incumbent mayor Lu Shiow-yen (盧秀燕) has reached the end of her second term. The party hopes to retain the mayoralty and preserve Lu’s political legacy, as she is widely considered a presidential contender ( Storm Media , September 15). If Johnny Chiang successfully defends the seat, his win would preserve the KMT’s political patronage network in central Taiwan and allow Lu to claim credit for managing the succession and for good governance. Conversely, a DPP victory would weaken her position and damage her chances for a 2028 bid, while potentially strengthening the standing of other figures, such as KMT chairperson Cheng Li-wun (鄭麗文). New Taipei City, the country’s most populous administrative division, is home to four million people, making it a key battleground. The DPP last governed the city in 2005, under Su Tseng-chang (蘇貞昌), who later served as premier in both the Chen Shui-bian (陳水扁) and Tsai Ing-wen administrations. His daughter, Su Chiao-hui (蘇巧慧), is running as the DPP candidate against KMT candidate Lee Shu-chuan. Su Chiao-hui has touted her experience as a sitting legislator and announced family-oriented neonatal and hospice care policies, while Lee, drawing on his technocratic background as a civil engineer and his long stints as deputy mayor of Taipei, New Taipei, and Kaohsiung, has focused on urban renewal projects ( CNA , August 19; Su Chiao-hui New Taipei City Mayoral Campaign Office , accessed November 10). Polling numbers indicate both candidates are within a few percentage points of each other and the race has been described as a toss-up ( Legislator Lin Chu-yin , November 13; TTV , November 16). A DPP win would likely shock the KMT, and improve the party’s assessments of its chances for 2028. In Kaohsiung, a southern port metropolis of 2.5 million people, both candidates are sitting legislators. In the campaign, the DPP’s Lai Jui-lung (賴瑞隆) has attacked the KMT’s Ko Chi-en (柯志恩) and her party’s legislative caucus for passing amendments to the revenue allocation law, which controls how much funding municipalities receive from the central government. Kaohsiung was one of the losers after the reallocation, leading to accusations from the pan-Green camp that the amendments are the latest manifestation of the sentiment that resources and capital often “prioritize the North at the expense of the South” (重北輕南) in Taiwan ( FTV News , August 29).  [2] The Kaohsiung City Government has argued that the city needs more funds because it is in the midst of industrial upgrading and that it has borne the brunt of environmental pollution arising from its massive industrial economy ( Kaohsiung City Government , December 21, 2024). Current polling indicates a DPP win is likely in Kaohsiung ( Radio Taiwan International , November 16). Outside of the special municipalities, Changhua stands out as the most crucial race. The largest county by population, it is home to 1.25 million people. The primary process for selecting candidates was marred by controversy, mainly arising from factional politics. The KMT candidate, Wei Cheng-ping (魏政平), does not come from the factions system and is seen as a compromise, which has led to local resentment against Cheng Li-wun’s electoral strategy (Cheng is personally acting as the head of Wei’s campaign) ( UDN , October 13). The DPP candidate, Chen Su-yueh (陳素月), has the backing of some local factions, but faces a split pan-Green ticket. DPP Changhua County Party Chapter chair Chiu Chien-fu (邱建富) is also running, but as an independent. Polls have Chen in the lead, but 40 percent of Changhua voters are still undecided ( CNA ; UDN , October 19).
