（中央社台北25日電）外媒分析，黃仁勳被重新任命輝達（NVIDIA）執行長，美國最具影響力的對中出售先進晶片倡導者重新掌舵輝達，對北京似乎是好消息。但北京也認識到，黃仁勳如今可能處處受到掣肘，華盛頓的議員們正準備質詢他，並收緊對中晶片銷售規定。
紐約時報（The New York Times）報導，這一反覆將進一步提供北京動力，推動中國企業擺脫對美國技術的依賴、發展自己的技術。因為從長遠來看，他們不希望能否獲得這種重要資源，取決於白宮某個人的一時興起。
報導指出，從中美兩國更廣泛的競爭格局來看，中國擁有出色的工程技術人才、世界一流的人工智慧（AI）模型，以及建設資料中心所需的廉價電力和廣闊土地。中國也一再展現出以更少資源創造更多價值的能力。
但中國在晶片領域明顯處於劣勢，仍難以生產足夠的晶片來滿足國內需求。非營利研究機構Epoch AI估計，走私晶片約占中國人工智慧算力的1/3。在先進人工智慧晶片設計方面，沒有任何企業能與輝達匹敵，而華盛頓正力求在這項具有變革意義的技術上保持對北京的領先優勢。
亞洲協會（Asia Society）政策研究所中國經濟研究員李其（Lizzi C. Lee）透過電子郵件回覆說，對中國人工智慧產業和人工智慧模型而言，「鑒於對輝達的依賴和美國技術的重要性，黃仁勳的回歸是好消息」。她說，北京或許也會因此感到安心，因為這表明「務實考量和商業利益在華盛頓依然能夠占據上風」。
但李其表示，鑒於美國期中選舉的結果以及美國總統川普已成為「跛腳鴨」總統，中國的政策制定者不太可能把所有希望寄託在川普的態度上。她說：「如果說有什麼影響的話，這場風波已經暴露出中國人工智慧發展雄心所面臨的軟肋，預計此後國產替代的努力將進一步加快。」
北京的兩個關鍵問題是，它是否會繼續獲得輝達晶片，以及阻止中國公司遠程訪問晶片的新規則是否會持續。
川普政府2025年撤銷對中銷售輝達H20晶片的禁令，隨後批准對中銷售性能更強大的H200晶片。多名議員上週披露，美國商務部已批准向中國企業出售80多萬枚先進人工智慧晶片，其中一些企業與中國軍方存在關聯。
直到不久前，中國企業還一直在利用一個監管漏洞。由於無法進口輝達最先進的晶片，它們通過東南亞及其他地區的資料中心租用這些晶片的算力。直到上週，美國商務部發布新規，嚴格限制中國企業通過第三國的資料中心使用輝達先進晶片。
上海復旦大學國際問題研究院院長、中國外交部顧問吳心伯說，更嚴格的管制只會加深北京對華盛頓的不信任，在北京看來，這場風波進一步證明，美國「不是一個可靠的合作夥伴」。
他說，華盛頓隨時都可以找個藉口切斷中國的供應鏈。在輝達事件中，中國與其說是主角，不如說是美國政治大戲中的一個道具。「黃仁勳事件反映了美國內部激烈的政治內鬥，中國只是背景音樂」。（編輯：朱建陵/馮昭）1151125

content:
资料照片：时尚品牌Shein的购物袋叠放在英国利物浦的一辆圣诞促销汽车上(2024年12月14日)
美国联邦贸易委员会(FTC)指控称，中国跨境时尚巨头Shein(希音)在获取数十亿美元营收的同时，采取了不公平的客户服务做法，并在其产品、供应商及消费者评价等问题上欺骗了数百万美国消费者。
联邦贸易委员会星期二(11月25日)发布新闻稿，指Shein将支付1亿美元用于消费者赔偿，与联邦贸易委员会对其提出的指控达成和解。
联邦贸易委员会指控称，这家快时尚零售商存在多项违法行为，包括人为设置障碍，使消费者难以解决购物问题；未能兑现配送承诺；压制负面评价，以及就供应链和棉花来源做出欺骗性陈述等。
根据联邦贸易委员会的起诉书，Shein曾宣传其配送服务“快速、透明且可靠”，但数以万计的消费者反映，他们的订单出现了数天、数周甚至数月的延迟，部分消费者甚至从未收到过商品。
起诉书指出，Shein未能向消费者提供充分的配送进度更新，且消费者也无法联系到客服人员来查询订单延迟或丢失的情况。
起诉书还指出，Shein称公司每天向美国运送近100万个包裹，然而截至2025年9月，该公司仅雇佣了五名客服人员处理美国消费者的电话咨询，且未在其网站上提供这些客服人员的联系电话。消费者的诉求往往得不到回应。
联邦贸易委员会还指控称，Shein存在系统性地阻止在其网站上显示用户评价的行为，该公司选择发布正面评价，同时压制或删除那些批评产品或退货的客户所留下的评价，这违反了相关法律。
另外，起诉书还称Shein对其产品所用棉花的产地说明也存在欺骗行为。例如，一些被Shein标称为“美国产”的棉花，实际上产自中国；此外，其部分产品所用棉花的产地根本无法追溯。
联邦贸易委员会指控Shein的上述行为违反了《联邦贸易委员会法》第五条、《邮购、互联网或电话订购商品规则》，以及《消费者评价与推荐使用规则》。
联邦贸易委员会消费者保护局(Bureau of Consumer Protection)局长克里斯托弗·穆法里奇(Christopher Mufarrige)指出：“Shein通过一系列承诺吸引消费者，例如提供平价服装、快速配送，并声称其供应商在童工和强迫劳动等相关标准方面获得了高于平均水平的评价。然而，该公司在产品、供应商以及客户评价的真实性等方面误导了数百万消费者。”
根据拟议的裁决令，Shein将向联邦贸易委员会支付1亿美元，这笔资金将用于向因该公司违法行为而受损的消费者提供赔偿。
目前，联邦贸易委员会已向美国加利福尼亚中区联邦地区法院提交了起诉书及拟议的最终裁决令。
一旦经联邦地区法院法官批准并签署，拟议的最终裁决令即具有法律效力。
联邦贸易委员会主席安德鲁·弗格森(Andrew Ferguson)11月24日在社媒平台X上发帖说：“SHEIN存在缺陷的客户服务机制，导致消费者在遇到问题时无法获得有效的解决途径。为解决这些指控，SHEIN将维持客户服务渠道，确保消费者能够获得及时、有效的帮助，并向消费者支付1亿美元作为赔偿。”
对此，阿肯色州共和党联邦参议员汤姆·科顿(Tom Cotton)11月25日在X上转了该帖，并称赞联邦贸易委员会采取了“明智之举”。科顿写道：“Shein欺骗美国消费者，并用来自共产中国的假冒伪劣商品充斥了我们的市场。”
Shein曾是国际服装零售业界最火的公司之一。公司于2012年在中国成立，2021年将总部迁至新加坡。新冠疫情期间，该公司曾以其服装款式变化之快、价格之低廉，以及“Shein开箱”的热潮，吸引全世界大批Z世代年轻消费者追捧其平价服饰。
Shein自9月1日在香港交易所上市以来，股价整体承压并低于发行价，截至11月25日收盘，Shein报1股36.3港元，显著低于48.56港元的IPO发行价。
劳工组织将发新报告，披露Shein非正规制衣作坊“恶劣”工作状况；Shein否认相关表述

资料照片中国天津某港口堆放着的集装箱。(2023年1月16日)
特朗普政府星期三(11月25日)提出对大多数中国输美商品加征最高20%的关税，理由是中国的产业政策造成制造业“结构性产能过剩”，损害美国商业利益。美国贸易代表办公室(USTR)同时提出，如果美方认定与北京的磋商未能充分解决调查提出的问题，可能考虑对所有中国输美商品加征最高40%的关税。
美国贸易代表贾米森·格里尔(Jamieson Greer)当天公布了依据《1974年贸易法》第301条对中国、欧盟、日本和台湾等14个经济体作出的调查结论。美国今年3月启动了涉及16个经济体的调查，目前尚未就墨西哥和挪威作出认定。
在针对中国的调查中，美国贸易代表办公室(USTR)认定，北京长期扶持特定产业，向制造商提供广泛的融资和其他支持，并以非商业条件扶持国有企业。美方还列举了强制技术转让、知识产权盗窃和劳动保护不足等问题，称这些做法压缩了美国企业在中国及第三国市场的销售机会，并影响美国制造业的就业和投资。USTR的报告点名钢铁、电池、太阳能和半导体等行业。
中国外交部发言人郭嘉昆星期三在美方公布方案前被问及拟议关税时称，所谓“产能过剩”是一个“伪命题”，中方反对以此为由进行“政治操弄”。他说，关税战和贸易战不符合任何一方利益，双方应通过协商解决分歧。
根据美国贸易代表办公室公布的方案，未列入两份附件的中国商品拟加征最高20%的关税，附件A所列商品拟加征最高10%，包括部分牛肉和柑橘汁、含胰岛素的药品，以及部分民用飞机发动机和零部件。附件B所列商品拟免于本轮加征，包括部分烟花、床上用品、家用微波炉和玩具。附件B所列商品来自美中贸易委员会“30换30”安排下的美国进口清单。这指的是双方在这一框架下各选出贸易额约300亿美元的商品，拟相互给予较低关税待遇。
20%是本轮拟加征税率的上限。路透社报道，这项新关税将叠加在特朗普第一任期内对部分中国商品加征的既有关税之上。美方公告同时规定，如果同一商品在另一项涉及强迫劳动产品的301调查下被加征关税，方案中的20%和40%上限均需扣除那项调查下适用的税率。
此次公告发布之际，距离美中现行贸易休战安排到期还有约一个半月。该安排将于2027年1月10日到期。美国贸易代表办公室将于1月5日截止接收书面意见，并于1月25日举行公开听证。
美国贸易代表办公室星期三公布关税提案的同一天，也通报了美中贸易委员会农业工作组的首次会议。中国商务部说，会议于星期一和星期二(11月23日至24日)在北京举行。美国贸易代表办公室与中国商务部共同主持会议，两国相关监管机构的代表也出席了会议。
美方的通报说，双方讨论了影响农产品贸易的非关税壁垒、市场准入，以及如何扩大贸易、让农业生产者受益。中方通报也提到农产品监管和市场准入。双方同意继续通过工作组沟通，推动解决各自在农业领域的关切。双方通报均未宣布新的农产品采购承诺或具体的市场准入措施。

title: 法国世界报 - 英伟达"闹剧"：习近平的"稳定"与特朗普的"混乱"之最新一章
summary: 本期世界报头版关注点如下：欧盟准备重新与普京开启对话、政党“不屈法国”领导人梅朗雄在左翼阵营的主导地位得到了强化、针对法国极右翼政党国民联盟的司法调查的跟进、法国前总统萨科齐相关司法案件进展、中国是如何获取英伟达芯片的、法国职业病情况汇总与跟踪等。我们在本期节目中，为您选取和中国相关的内容做综述。 首先是英伟达。世界报表示，中国获取英伟达战略性芯片的手段，正受到全球媒体的追踪。事实上，黄仁勋曾排除可能，称没有任何证据表明其人工智能芯片遭到了转移。他尤其指出，处理器机架体积庞大
content:
本期世界报头版关注点如下：欧盟准备重新与普京开启对话、政党“不屈法国”领导人梅朗雄在左翼阵营的主导地位得到了强化、针对法国极右翼政党国民联盟的司法调查的跟进、法国前总统萨科齐相关司法案件进展、中国是如何获取英伟达芯片的、法国职业病情况汇总与跟踪等。我们在本期节目中，为您选取和中国相关的内容做综述。

首先是英伟达。世界报表示，中国获取英伟达战略性芯片的手段，正受到全球媒体的追踪。事实上，黄仁勋曾排除可能，称没有任何证据表明其人工智能芯片遭到了转移。他尤其指出，处理器机架体积庞大，他的一套尖端系统重量就要接近两吨，“不可能把它藏在口袋里或背包里”。根据黄仁勋当时的说法，要想追踪这些设备的去向，其实也并不困难。另外，各国政府和企业都明白，如果他们违规转移订单内容，日后将很难再从英伟达处进行采购。

但世界报指出，就在黄仁勋发表上述些令人安心的言论的前三个月，抓捕行动就已经开始了：2025年2月，新加坡警方在两起彼此独立、但存在诸多共同点的案件中，逮捕了一名中国商人和数名新加坡人。他们涉嫌协助从戴尔和超微电脑等美国大型集团购买装有英伟达处理器的服务器，还被怀疑虚假申报。这些处理器机架在购买后，被转运到了马来西亚，部分随后又被运往第三国，这第三国，很有可能就是中国。

世界报评论认为，华盛顿为了让中国技术追赶减速，实际上创造了一个巨大的需求空间。从2022年起，美国政府禁止英伟达向中国交付其最先进芯片。因此对于中国科技行业而言，除了使用已经入库的芯片、仍在市场上流通的英伟达旧一代芯片，以及性能较弱的中国华为芯片之外，只剩下两条途径：第一，利用安装在例如马来西亚的服务器，开发其新一代人工智能。第二，将芯片转移并走私到中国。

接下来就由黄乐出场了。纽约时报援引美国情报部门的说法，黄乐自从2025年春以来一直与中国情报部门保持联系。这意味着，她与黄仁勋关系持续期间，与中国有联系。北京则对此予以否认。黄乐、李明广泛参与管理的超速国际公司总部在新加坡，通过将位于中国境外的服务器租给阿里巴巴等，发展迅猛。超速国际因此前经营过网络电子游戏许可证业务，具备了作为英伟达合法客户进行注册所需的背景，直至成为英伟达在东南亚最大的客户。2024年至2025年间，超速国际购买了价值46亿美元的英伟达设备。2025年，英伟达担心其库存记录被美国盯上，曾在几个月内把超速国际列入“不再向其销售产品”的客户名单。

然而，就在同一年，超速国际以新名称出现了，这次名为Novagate。2026年前五个月，Novagate通过其在马来西亚的子公司，购买了价值3亿美元的、包含英伟达芯片的设备。彭博社更是调查指出，由李明、黄乐夫妇的商业合作伙伴所经营的企业购买的英伟达芯片，最终直接进入了上海郊区一座大型数据中心。柬埔寨犯罪网络，也在多方调查下，被发现与英伟达进入中国，有着影影绰绰的关联。

英伟达也是本期法国世界报社论所关注的。这篇社论认为，美国总统促成了黄仁勋的回归，对英伟达做出了危险的纵容。除了技术主导地位，英伟达对人工智能生态系统的金融控制力日益增强。世界报这篇社论称，如果英伟达是一家银行，其贷款能力等将在美国银行业中排名第十。也就是说，向黄仁勋追责的代价，极其高昂。社论称，把华尔街繁荣置于法律之上，特朗普鼓励了行业的越轨，而美国经济对这一行业的依赖，已经十分危险。

本期世界报与中国相关的刊文还有一则，地缘政治版面的一篇论坛文章聚焦了“习近平的稳定与特朗普的混乱”。当中指出，随着一次又一次的会面，特朗普的步伐，越来越按照习近平的步伐来调整了。本次深圳峰会的种种，让蒙田研究所指出，“后美国世界到来”了。而英伟达这场数万亿美元股票市值的闹剧，暴露了美国政府内部在对华战略上的深刻分歧。

title: 要闻分析 - 欧盟500亿欧元基金缩小美欧在AI与量子领域差距
summary: 英国金融时报（Financial Times）引述2名参与相关讨论的官员报导，该基金名为“主权科技股权基金”（Sovereign Tech Equity Fund，简称Stef），将聚焦投资AI与量子领域。与现有的欧盟融资机制相比，这一新基金将进行规模更大、风险更高且时间更长的投资。 其中1名官员说：以上计划针对高风险领域的长期稳定投资，这与欧盟惯常的做法恰好相反，不过这正是我们需要它的原因。由该基金投资一家企业，有助鼓励其他投资人跟进。 欧盟执行委员会预计11月25日提出一
content:
英国金融时报（Financial Times）引述2名参与相关讨论的官员报导，该基金名为“主权科技股权基金”（Sovereign Tech Equity Fund，简称Stef），将聚焦投资AI与量子领域。与现有的欧盟融资机制相比，这一新基金将进行规模更大、风险更高且时间更长的投资。

其中1名官员说：以上计划针对高风险领域的长期稳定投资，这与欧盟惯常的做法恰好相反，不过这正是我们需要它的原因。由该基金投资一家企业，有助鼓励其他投资人跟进。

欧盟执行委员会预计11月25日提出一项量子战略，以巩固欧盟在这个新兴产业的地位。

由于美国政策不确定性升高和地缘政治局势日益动荡，这个新基金计划将是进一步强化欧洲科技自主的一环。欧盟期盼刺激对新兴技术的投资，以往欧洲企业难以在这些领域与美国和中国竞争。

基金具体融资方式仍在商议中。官员表示，执委会打算将欧盟基金当作种子资金，吸引民间部门投入额外资金，目标是每投入1欧元，可吸引最多6欧元资金的投注。

欧盟科技事务主管维尔库南（Henna Virkkunen）已与欧洲投资银行（European Investment Bank，EIB）讨论这个基金构想。EIB可在不需承担投资风险的情况下，提供金融专业经验。

今年8月间，英国金融时报（Financial Times）曾经报导，预测显示，在疫情后的6年里，美国企业投资增幅是欧洲的3倍以上，特别是人工智能（AI）热潮扩大了美国与欧洲两大经济体间的差距。

据牛津经济公司（Oxford Economics）预测，自2021年至2027年底，美国企业在新设备及厂房设施的支出扣除通膨后将增加40%，AI设备投资激增是背后的主要推动力。相比之下，欧元区同期实质投资仅增加12%，其中德国企业投资几乎停滞。

牛津经济公司的预测显示，自从欧洲中央银行（ECB）前总裁德拉吉（Mario Draghi）2024年9月发布具里程碑意义的竞争力报告以来，欧洲缩小投资差距的进展可说微乎其微。

牛津经济公司的经济学家哈伦伯格（Daniel Harenberg）表示：美国经济更具活力，也更具企业家精神，因此发展速度更快，在AI竞赛中也有更多回报。欧洲则要慢得多。

欧洲也面临与美国之间日益扩大的生产力差距。英国曼彻斯特大学（University of Manchester）教授范阿克（Bart van Ark）今年夏天在欧洲央行辛特拉论坛（ECB Forum in Sintra）告诉ECB决策官员：美国最近又进一步拉大了与欧洲的差距。

根据范阿克的分析，2018年至2025年间，美国每工作1小时创造的国内生产毛额（GDP）增加14美元，欧洲仅增加2美元。他指出，这不只是数位产业的问题，美国的优势也延伸到其他产业，包括批发零售与专业服务。

不过，范阿克认为，单纯增加投资不太可能解决欧洲的生产力困境。欧洲的更深层问题在于创新无法有效转化为各产业采用的新技术和工具。

欧洲的优势在于法律框架，它是全球率先制定严格AI使用规范的地区之一。2024年通过的“人工智能法”（AI Act）是全球首个针对这项技术的法律框架。

但批评人士警告，严格的法规可能扼杀创新，并降低企业投资AI的意愿。法国总统马克龙2年前在演说中提醒说：我们已与变化中的世界脱节，欧洲管制过度但投资不足。

就在欧洲正努力追赶美国的时候，2026年的美国中期选举前后，美国人自己开始关注美国大举押注AI所面临的风险。

国际清算银行（BIS）等机构已警告：“投资热潮急遽消退”（Investment Bust）的风险正在升高。除了英伟达公司和黄仁勋事件带来的震动以外，谷歌（Google）、Meta、微软（Microsoft）及亚马逊（Amazon）2026年全年投资总额预计超过7250亿美元，竞相建设更多AI基础设施。

美国带动的这一波全球AI发展狂潮正在放慢脚步：投资人担心，企业投注数十亿美元投资AI基础设施，取得报酬的速度可能过慢，难以支撑由举债推动的扩张步伐。过去几周以来，这个疑虑已拖累AI相关企业和供应商的股价下挫。

路透社报导，AI芯片巨头英伟达董事会11月23日决议通过前执行长黄仁勋复职，使近来走疲的股市反弹，不过，防范科技公司债务违约的投保成本近日急升，显示市场仍担忧AI支出热潮过于庞大。

英国资讯服务商马基特（IHS Markit）资料显示，日本软银集团（SoftBank Group）11月24日的5年期信用违约交换（CDS）利差跳升至501个基点，为2022年10月以来最宽。

在东京上市交易的软银立即在25日收盘时重挫14.83%，从11月迄今累计跌幅达36.75%，可能写下2000年网路泡沫（dot-com bubble）以来最大单月跌幅。

据标普全球市场情报（S&P Global Market Intelligence）资料，甲骨文（Oracle）、Google母公司Alphabet、太空探索科技公司（SpaceX）以及资料中心营运商CoreWeave，在隔夜交易中的5年期信用违约交换CDS利差同创历史新高，其中CoreWeave未来5年违约机率攀升至68%。

专家提醒。如果出现放款机构转趋谨慎或企业更难取得资金的迹象，投资支出展望将蒙上阴影。

Executive Order 14439 of November 20, 2026
Protecting the Executive's Privileges and Enhancing Efficiencies in Federal Contracting
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act (40 U.S.C. 101 et seq.) and the common law, it is hereby ordered:
Section 1 . Purpose and Policy. In order to protect and serve the American people, the executive branch must be able to work closely with its employees and contractors on sensitive matters without fear that confidential information will be released to unauthorized third parties. The doctrine of executive privilege, which the Supreme Court has recognized is inextricably rooted in the separation of powers under the Constitution, protects confidential executive branch information from disclosure. Protecting this information from unauthorized disclosure, including to members of the Congress, is vital to the functioning of the executive branch.
The ability of the Congress to seek executive branch information is limited; it cannot seek information from executive branch departments and agencies (agencies), employees, or Federal contractors without a valid legislative purpose that does not intrude on core Executive functions. Nor can the Congress obtain privileged information, including information shared between Federal employees and Federal contractors, before the executive branch has an opportunity to assert relevant privileges. Despite these bedrock protections, certain congressional leaders have threatened to intrude on these Executive prerogatives by seeking confidential executive branch information from agencies and harassing private companies that contract with the Federal Government. The executive branch has a compelling interest in its confidential information, and the right to protect that information from disclosure even by Federal contractors pursuant to a congressional request.
A lack of coordination between Federal contractors and the executive branch undermines the ability of contractors to provide economical and efficient goods and services. If Federal contractors fail to provide timely notice and coordinate with the White House and agencies prior to responding to congressional requests for information, the executive branch may be required to intervene or engage in separate litigation to defend its rights. Federal contractors also may be unaware of the executive branch's interests and positions, resulting in duplicative and wasteful efforts. Federal contractors and the executive branch engaging in separate strategies and litigation regarding the same requests and information is inefficient and wastes taxpayer resources. Moreover, the executive branch engages in sensitive and vital work with contractors, including on matters of national and homeland security. Such work often involves confidential information. If the executive branch cannot be assured that those communications will remain confidential, agencies and the White House will be chilled from sharing sensitive information with contractors, which will stymie the operation of critical Government programs. An inability to safely and freely share such information with Federal contractors will also substantially reduce the efficiency of those contractors and the work being provided to the public. The executive branch will thus have to find alternative means of carrying out similar functions, reducing and even eliminating reliance on Federal contractors for certain ( printed page 76628) purposes. Such an outcome is neither efficient nor desirable for the Federal Government or its contractors.
It is therefore the policy of the United States to protect confidential information and enhance economy and efficiency in Federal contracting by preventing and prohibiting uncoordinated disclosures of information pursuant to congressional requests.
Sec. 2 . Requirements for Federal Contractors. In order to protect the executive branch's interests and rights, and to ensure economical and efficient work with Federal contractors, all Federal contractors must immediately:
(a) notify the White House and the contracting agencies of any pending or future congressional request respecting the contractors' communications or work with the executive branch; and abide by any instructions received from the White House and contracting agency related to the withholding of communications that the White House or the agency has determined are protected by executive privilege.
(b) Agencies shall coordinate with the White House and contractors on appropriate responses to such congressional requests, including the application or assertion of any relevant privileges.
(c) This section also applies to subcontractors working for a Federal contractor on a Federal contract. Agencies shall take steps to require Federal contractors to be responsible for ensuring that subcontractors working on Federal contracts comply with this section.
Sec. 3 . Implementation. (a) Each agency shall promptly inform all contractors and subcontractors of the obligations in this order and shall require such contractors and subcontractors to comply with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order.
(b) The Office of Management and Budget shall develop guidance on how agencies can ensure that contractors are complying with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order and steps that agencies should take to ensure adequate coordination between the contracting agencies, contractors, and White House to enhance efficiency and the protection of Executive information.
Sec. 4 . Enforcement. If a Federal contractor or subcontractor fails to comply with the requirements set forth in section 2 of this order, contracting agencies shall consider whether to take all appropriate actions, consistent with applicable law, to enforce the terms of this order, including the potential termination or cancellation of contracts and the potential debarment or suspension of contractors.
Sec. 5 . Severability. If any provision of this order, or the application of any provision to any person or circumstance, is held to be invalid, the remainder of this order and the application of its provisions to any other persons or circumstances shall not be affected thereby.
Sec. 6 . General Provisions. (a) Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect:
(i) the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; or
(ii) the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.
(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations.
(c) This order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit, substantive or procedural, enforceable at law or in equity by any party against the United States, its departments, agencies, or entities, its officers, employees, or agents, or any other person.
(d) The costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of Labor.

Notice of information collection; request for comment.
The Department of the Treasury, as part of its continuing effort to reduce paperwork and respondent burden, invites the general public and other federal agencies to comment on the proposed information collections listed below, in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.
Written comments must be received on or before January 25, 2027.
Send comments regarding the burden estimate, or any other aspect of the information collection, including suggestions for reducing the burden, to U.S. Department of the Treasury, Attention: Treasury PRA Clearance Officer, 1500 Suite #7500, JBAB, 250 Murray Lane SW, Bldg. 410/Door 123, Washington, DC 20222, or email at PRA@treasury.gov.
Copies of the submissions may be obtained from Spencer W. Clark by emailing PRA@treasury.gov, calling (202) 927-5331, or viewing the entire information collection request at www.reginfo.gov.
Title: Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund Reporting & Recordkeeping.
OMB Control Number: 1505-0277.
Type of Review: Extension without change of a currently approved collection.
Description: Section 604 of the Social Security Act (the “Act”), as added by section 9901 of the American Rescue Plan Act of 2021, Public Law 117-2 (Mar. 11, 2021) authorized the Coronavirus Capital Projects Fund (“CPF”). The CPF provides $10 billion in funding for the Department of the Treasury (“Treasury”) to provide grant payments to States (defined to include the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico), seven territories and freely associated states (including the United States Virgin Islands, Guam, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Federated States of Micronesia, and the Republic of Palau), and Tribal governments to carry out critical capital projects directly enabling work, education, and health monitoring, including remote options, in response to the public health emergency with respect to the Coronavirus Disease (“COVID-19”). Section 604(b) of the Act prescribes that the $10 billion be allocated to eligible grant recipients according to a formula provided in the statute.
The current information collection will be used to solicit information related to quarterly project and expenditure reports and annual performance reports. Both information collections are described generally in the Compliance and Reporting Guidance. The Compliance and Reporting Guidance provides recipients with information needed to fulfill their reporting requirements and compliance obligations. The period of performance for all recipients and projects types will end by December 31, 2027, and final closeout reports will be due by April 20, 2028. Recipients must retain program-related records for five years following submission of the final expenditure report.
Form: Quarterly Project & Expenditure Report, Annual Performance Report.
Affected Public: State, Local, Tribal, Territorial and Freely Associated State Governments.
Estimated Number of Respondents: 609.
Frequency of Response: Quarterly, Annually.
Estimated Total Number of Annual Responses: 845.
Estimated Time per Response: Varies from 20 to 80 hours per year depending on type of respondent and report.
Estimated Total Annual Burden Hours: 30,352.
Request for Comments: Comments submitted in response to this notice will be summarized and included in the request for Office of Management and Budget approval. All comments will become a matter of public record. Comments are invited on: (a) whether the collection of information is necessary for the proper performance of the functions of the agency, including whether the information shall have practical utility; (b) the accuracy of the agency's estimate of the burden of the collection of information; (c) ways to enhance the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; (d) ways to minimize the burden of the collection of information on respondents, including through the use of technology; and (e) estimates of capital or start-up costs and costs of operation, maintenance, and purchase of services required to provide information.
Authority:44 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.

title: 黄仁勋重返英伟达，北京喜忧参半
source: 纽约时报中文网 国际纵览

content:
DAVID PIERSON, 黄瑞黎, CECILIA KANG2026年11月25日
周一，英伟达的官方X账号发布了黄仁勋重新出任公司首席执行官的照片。 Nvidia, via Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
黄仁勋被重新任命为英伟达首席执行官，对北京来说似乎是好消息：在特朗普总统非同寻常的干预下，美国最具影响力的对华出售先进芯片的倡导者重新掌舵英伟达。
但北京对此事的看法可能更为复杂。尽管一些中国科技高管对黄仁勋的回归表示欢迎，他们也认识到，黄仁勋如今可能处处受到掣肘。华盛顿的议员们正纷纷准备对他展开质询，并收紧对华芯片销售规定。
无论如何，这一反复将给北京提供进一步动力，推动中国企业摆脱对美国技术的依赖、发展自己的技术。围绕全球最具影响力的芯片企业及其一手缔造者的这场风波，如今又出现了新的转折，这意味着英伟达将继续处于美中关系的焦点。
在先进人工智能芯片的设计方面，没有任何企业能与英伟达匹敌，而华盛顿正力求在这项具有变革意义的技术上保持对北京的领先优势。
从中美两国更广泛的竞争格局来看，中国拥有出色的工程技术人才、世界一流的人工智能模型，以及建设数据中心所需的廉价电力和广阔土地。中国也一再展现出以更少资源创造更多价值的能力。
9月，中国领导人习近平在白宫。对华鹰派人士和国家安全官员认为，美国应限制对华出口人工智能技术。 Doug Mills/The New York Times
但中国在芯片领域明显处于劣势，仍难以生产足够的芯片来满足国内需求。非营利研究机构Epoch AI估计，走私芯片约占中国人工智能算力的三分之一，但该机构也表示，实际比例可能远低于或远高于这一估算值。
亚洲协会政策研究所中国经济研究员李其在电子邮件中说，对中国人工智能产业和人工智能模型而言，“鉴于对英伟达的依赖和美国技术的重要性，黄仁勋的回归是好消息。”她还说，北京或许也会因此感到安心，因为这表明“务实考量和商业利益在华盛顿依然能够占据上风”。
但李其表示，鉴于中期选举的结果以及特朗普已成为“跛脚鸭”总统，中国的政策制定者不太可能把所有希望都寄托在特朗普的态度上。她说：“如果说有什么影响的话，这场风波已经暴露出中国人工智能发展雄心所面临的软肋，预计此后国产替代的努力将进一步加快。”
很大程度上，事态的发展将取决于华盛顿。围绕如何处理中国获取先进人工智能芯片的问题，华盛顿一直存在激烈争论。最近几周，在《纽约时报》报道美国情报官员认为，据称与黄仁勋有婚外情的中国女商人黄乐(Alice Huang)是为中国情报机构工作的线人后，这场争论进一步升级。
对华鹰派和国家安全官员认为，在人工智能上保持领先的最佳方式是限制美国技术出口。黄仁勋及其支持者则认为，更好的做法是取消限制，让中国依赖美国芯片。
北京的两个关键问题是，它是否会继续获得英伟达芯片，以及阻止中国公司远程访问芯片的新规则是否会持续。
2025年，特朗普政府撤销了对华销售英伟达H20芯片的禁令，随后又批准了性能更强大的H200芯片的对华销售。多名议员上周披露，商务部已批准向中国企业出售80多万枚先进人工智能芯片，其中一些企业与中国军方存在关联。
直到不久前，中国企业还一直在利用一个监管漏洞。由于无法进口英伟达最先进的芯片，它们通过东南亚及其他地区的数据中心租用这些芯片的算力。这种做法此前一直是合法的，直到上周，美国商务部发布新规，严格限制中国企业通过第三国的数据中心使用英伟达先进芯片，并要求向马来西亚、新加坡、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西的企业出口芯片必须获得许可证。
美国商务部上周出台了一项规定，严格限制中国企业通过马来西亚等第三国的数据中心使用英伟达先进芯片。 Ulet Ifansasti for The New York Times
然而，就在特朗普政府公布这些规定一周后，特朗普却帮助这些规定最具影响力的反对者重新掌权。
特朗普在解释黄仁勋回归的原因时表示，此举部分是为了防止他倒向北京。“黄仁勋可以马上搭乘下一班飞机去中国，我向你保证，他想要什么，他们就会给他什么，”特朗普周一对CNBC说。
在中国，黄仁勋的遭遇引发了广泛同情，一些舆论认为，他的回归证明了他是清白的。中国官员此前驳斥有关间谍活动的指控，称其为“污蔑抹黑”。
黄乐此前执掌总部位于新加坡的数据中心公司Megaspeed，该公司购买了大量英伟达芯片，目前正因将这些芯片走私到中国的指控而接受联邦调查。她未回应《纽约时报》的置评请求。
周二，受黄仁勋回归消息的提振，亚洲股市在科技股的带动下大幅上涨。
中国外交部拒绝就黄仁勋发表评论。不过，中共小报《环球时报》暗示，黄仁勋复职证明，这起间谍风波是美国媒体一手挑起的一场“闹剧”。
周一，即黄仁勋回归同一天，商务部将Megaspeed列入贸易黑名单。黄仁勋还定于下周在众议院接受质询，并在参议院作证。
美国情报官员称，新加坡数据中心企业Megaspeed的高管黄乐是为中国情报机构效力的线人，她被认为曾与黄仁勋有婚外情。 Taryn Ng/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
“黄仁勋回归之际，美国出口管制面临新的政治现实，即对全球芯片销售采取放任自流做法受到了更多质疑，”新美国安全中心技术与国家安全项目主任维韦克·奇卢库里说。
专家普遍认为，中国的人工智能发展落后美国六至九个月。奇卢库里表示，如果华盛顿“真正堵住出口管制政策中的漏洞，并严格执行现行规定，这一领先优势可能翻倍”。
上海复旦大学美国问题学者、中国外交部顾问吴心伯说，更严格的管制只会加深北京对华盛顿的不信任，在北京看来，这场风波进一步证明，美国“不是一个可靠的合作伙伴”。他说，华盛顿随时都可以找个借口切断中国的供应链。
在吴心伯看来，在英伟达事件中，中国与其说是主角，不如说是美国政治大戏中的一个道具。
“黄仁勋事件反映了美国内部激烈的政治内斗，中国只是背景音乐，”他说。
其他中国分析人士警告华盛顿不应低估北京的影响力。中国主导着美国工厂和武器制造商依赖的稀土和磁铁供应。根据去年达成的贸易休战，北京暂停了对稀土出口的全面管制。但该休战将于1月10日到期，是否延长协议可能会与美国芯片出口的争论纠缠在一起。
中国分析人士还说，中国市场太大，美国芯片制造商不可能放弃。他们补充说，新的限制措施只会加快中国利用国产芯片和软件推动人工智能产业蓬勃发展的步伐。中国领先的人工智能企业之一DeepSeek正在为华为生产的芯片开发软件，部分目的是为了绕过英伟达自己的软件。
但悉尼大学美国研究中心战略技术项目主任奥利维娅·沈表示，中国政府与本国人工智能企业的利益诉求并不总是一致。她说，北京希望本国人工智能产业使用国产芯片，稀宇科技和智谱等上市企业则希望开发具有全球竞争力的模型，而至少目前，这样的模型只能依靠英伟达芯片进行训练。
中国上市人工智能企业稀宇科技曾使用英伟达的芯片训练人工智能模型。 Go Nakamura/Reuters
“从长远来看，他们不希望能否获得这种重要资源取决于白宫某个人的一时兴起，”奥利维娅·沈说。

title: Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy: Why Hong Kong’s works regulation must break from civil service culture
zh_title: 宏福苑火灾惨案：为何香港的工程规管必须脱离公务员文化
summary: 宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们考虑一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第二）
content:
宏福阁大火夺去了168人的生命，一年后，让我们考虑一下政府的应对措施是否足够。当局道歉，住房局局长何温妮辞职。这些都是值得欢迎的举措，现在的重点是改革。但有一个问题很突出：香港的监管质量明显参差不齐。香港民众悼念在大埔宏福苑火灾中丧生的遇难者。照片：Tom Grundy/HKFP。世界银行对香港的监管制度给予高度评价。该城市在全球约 200 个地区中排名第八，在亚洲排名第二，仅次于新加坡（全球排名第一）。然而，我们在宏福苑火灾悲剧和其他与工程相关的丑闻中却表现出了监管的无能。调查火灾的独立审查委员会将监管失误描述为“系统性和普遍性”。香港在金融服务、公共卫生、诚信（反腐败）和其他领域的监管无疑相对较好。因此评价很高。因此，我们不能说工程监管的缺位和/或不力（不仅是宏福苑火灾，还有玛丽医院电梯事件、太宗电梯防火板事件等）代表了整个香港的公共监管。问题是，为什么建筑监管如此草率和参差不齐，明显优先考虑行政便利，或许还保护建筑业？
政府的工务部门历史悠久，是殖民地香港最早的政府职能之一，人员全部由公务员组成。当局于 1843 年设立测量总署。1870 年演变为测量部，并于 1883 年更名为工务署 (PWD)。工务署管理所有工务职能。 1982 年，官员们将这个庞然大物拆分为七个工程部门。它们大多由现任发展局局长监管。该报告向我们表明，几十年来，监管制度未能充分优先考虑服务和保护公众的情况一直被容忍。那些领导建筑和建设的人大多是从公务员队伍内部提拔的，公务员队伍分为专业队伍。新入职的公务员在进入时就已经融入了本部门实践中的价值观。团队领导者和团队成员执行非正式规范，指导新进入者应如何行事以及对他们的期望。接受这些非正式规范对于在部门中相处和取得进步是必要的。 “不要破坏现状”的文化占主导地位。官僚问责制度在这些规范内运作。官僚文化具有“粘性”，难以改变。现在想想我们表现良好的监管机构：香港金融管理局、证券及期货事务监察委员会、廉政公署。
在最近的各个时期，这些当局都是在公务员系统之外设立的。在这些当局中，当局优先考虑的是与过去的做法的彻底决裂。独立委员会关于宏福苑火灾的报告副本，2026 年 10 月 29 日。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。委员会对火灾的审查报告特别指出了住房部门独立检查组（ICU）的行为。独立审查组本应监督宏福苑的外墙翻新和维护工作，批准计划、进行检查并确保符合建筑安全标准。作者

【原文 English Original】
A year on from the Wang Fuk Court blaze, which claimed 168 lives, let’s consider whether the government’s response is sufficient. Authorities apologised and housing chief Winnie Ho resigned. These are welcome moves, and the focus now is on reform. But one area stands out: Hong Kong’s apparently uneven regulatory quality. Hongkongers pay tribute to victims who died in the fatal fire in Tai Po Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. The World Bank rates Hong Kong’s regulatory regime highly. The city ranks eighth out of some 200 territories globally and second in Asia after Singapore (globally ranked as No. 1). And yet we have demonstrated regulatory incapacity in the Wang Fuk Court fire tragedy and other works-related scandals. The independent review committee looking into the blaze described the regulatory failings as “ systematic and pervasive .” Hong Kong regulates financial services, public health, integrity (anti-corruption) and undoubtedly other areas relatively well. Hence the high rating. So, we cannot say that absent and/or poor works regulation (not only the Wang Fuk Court fire disaster, but the Queen Mary Hospital elevator case , the Taizoom elevator fire panel case , etc.) is representative of Hong Kong public regulation as a whole. The question is why building and construction regulation is so sloppy and uneven, apparently prioritising administrative convenience and perhaps protecting the construction industry? The works side of the government is ancient, created among the earliest government functions in colonial Hong Kong and staffed entirely by civil servants. Authorities set up the Surveyor General’s Office in 1843. It morphed into the Survey Department in 1870, and was renamed the Public Works Department (PWD) in 1883. PWD managed all works functions. In 1982, officials broke up this behemoth into seven works departments. They are mostly supervised by the Secretary for Development who is still in her post. The report shows us that a regulatory regime hat failed to sufficiently prioritise serving and protecting the public was tolerated for decades. Those leading building and construction are mostly promoted from within the civil service, which is organised into professional streams. Newly hired civil servants are socialised into the values in practice of their department when they enter. Team leaders and team members enforce informal norms that guide new entrants into how they should behave and what is expected of them. Accepting these informal norms is necessary to get along and ahead in the department. A “don’t rock the boat” culture dominates. Bureaucratic accountability systems operate within these norms. Bureaucratic culture is “sticky” and difficult to change. Now consider our well-performing regulators: the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, the Securities and Futures Commission, the Independent Commission Against Corruption. Each of relatively recent vintage, these authorities were set up outside the civil service. In them, authorities prioritised a sharp break from past practice. Copies of the independent committee’s report on the Wang Fuk Court fire, on October 29, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The committee review report into the fire singles out the behaviour of the housing department’s Independent Checking Unit (ICU). The ICU was supposed to supervise external wall renovation and maintenance work at Wang Fuk Court, approving plans, conducting inspections and ensuring compliance with building safety standards. Authorities classified Wang Fuk Court’s renovation as lower-risk “minor works” although it was an eye-popping HK$330 million project. This reduced the statutory level of ICU oversight required. The unit was also responsible for investigating and addressing residents’ reports and safety complaints. The report noted in particular the ICU’s “lack of sense of crisis, regulatory lapses, systemic blind spots, and enforcement failures.” This is a damning judgement. The ICU is composed of senior professionals including many structural engineers, maintenance surveyors, architects, and technical staff. Not only did the ICU fail in its duty to serve and protect citizens, but the professionals among them failed in their duty to uphold the values of professionalism, integrity, and excellence. The government set up a new public housing building control section which is welcome. But transferring the existing ICU staff who bring with them values in practice that led to the tragedy is a mistake. I urge the government to set up a new body outside the existing works bureaucracy. Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po on December 2, 2025, days after a fatal fire engulfed seven of the eight blocks of the residential estate. Photo: Tom Grundy/HKFP. Beyond government, action is needed too. Professional bodies should enforce discipline among their members. Many professionals were involved in the various works scandals. Professional bodies such as the Engineers Registration Board should investigate those involved, and if found culpable, take action with consequences, such as suspending or cancelling their licences to practise in Hong Kong. title: HKFP Lens: A year of grief and inquiry, after Tai Po blaze
zh_title: HKFP 镜头：大埔大火后悲痛与质询的一年
summary: 宏福苑是一个建于 20 世纪 80 年代靠近吐露港的八座住宅屋村，拥有近 2,000 户家庭。消防处于 2026 年 11 月 26 日对宏福苑致命火灾作出反应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大埔综合楼的家庭辛辛苦苦买了一套舒适的公寓并抚养孩子。其中一些人后来成为了公寓业主，并在同一片土地上养育了第三代。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔致命火灾发生一天后，一名男子站在被毁坏的宏福苑屋苑前。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。我
content:
宏福苑是一个建于 20 世纪 80 年代靠近吐露港的八座住宅屋村，拥有近 2,000 户家庭。消防处于 2026 年 11 月 26 日对宏福苑致命火灾作出反应。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。大埔综合楼的家庭辛辛苦苦买了一套舒适的公寓并抚养孩子。其中一些人后来成为了公寓业主，并在同一片土地上养育了第三代。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，大埔致命火灾发生一天后，一名男子站在被毁坏的宏福苑屋苑前。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。它曾是香港梦的缩影，直到去年11月26日下午，社区发生致命火灾。由于当时正在进行大规模翻修工程，火势迅速蔓延到八栋用泡沫板和脚手架网覆盖的建筑物中的七栋。 2025 年 11 月 27 日，家人在辨认大埔大火受害者亲人的尸体后哭泣。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。在平常的工作日下午，老年人、儿童、全职妈妈、夜班后休息的爸爸以及家政工人都被困在火灾中。 2025年11月28日，在致命的大埔火灾中失去家园的人们暂时住在广福村的大厅，这是一个公共屋村，靠近遭受火灾的宏福苑。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
这场大火最终夺去了 168 人的生命，导致数千人无家可归，标志着充满无尽悲伤、愤怒和疑问的一年的开始。香港摄影记者回顾了过去一年的照片，我们的摄影记者跟踪了香港数十年来最严重火灾后的重大事件和事态发展。火灾发生后，数以千计的香港人动员线上线下支持受害者。照片显示，2025 年 11 月 27 日，志愿者在宏福法院附近集会，设立摊位，提供免费食物、衣服和生活用品。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，人们在大埔地铁里阅读对火灾受害者的支持信息。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025年12月5日，数千人献花和玩偶，哀悼宏福苑火灾中的遇难者。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，一名学生在哀悼死者时流下了眼泪。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2025 年 12 月 1 日，道士为死者举行仪式。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。火灾发生后，宏福苑部分建筑物发现非阻燃脚手架网。后来被证实是导致火势迅速蔓延的原因之一。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。火灾发生后不久，立法会于 2025 年 12 月 7 日举行选举。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 11月底，香港警务处命令义工拆除广福村平台的临时补给站。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。
2025 年 12 月 19 日，消防员聚集在一起哀悼在大埔火灾中因公殉职的消防员何伟豪。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。悲剧发生后，2026年1月16日，宏福苑居民江志强（左一）、李家强（中）和叶家驹（右一）回忆起居民如何徒劳地试图报告火灾风险。他们敦促政府调查火灾原因。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。 2026年2月5日，独立委员会召开启动前第一次公开会议

【原文 English Original】
Wang Fuk Court, an eight-block residential estate built in the 1980s near Tolo Harbour, was home to nearly 2,000 households. The Fire Services Department responds to the fatal blaze at Wang Fuk Court on November 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The families at the Tai Po complex had worked hard to purchase a comfortable flat and raise their children. Some of whom later became flat owners, bringing up a third generation on the same estate. On November 27, 2025, one day after the fatal Tai Po fire started, a man stands in front of the ravaged Wang Fuk Court housing estate. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. It was the epitome of the Hong Kong dream, until a fatal fire struck the community on the afternoon of November 26 last year. The blaze quickly spread through seven of the eight buildings which were covered with foam board and scaffolding nets, as a large-scale renovation project was underway at the time. On November 27, 2025, family members cry after identifying the bodies of loved ones who fell victim to the fatal Tai Po fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Seniors, children, full-time moms, dads who were taking a break after night shifts, and domestic workers were among those trapped in the fire during the otherwise ordinary weekday afternoon. On November 28, 2025, people who lost their homes in the deadly Tai Po fire stay temporarily in the hall of Kwong Fuk Estate, a public housing estate near the fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The fire eventually claimed 168 lives, left thousands homeless, and marked the start of a year of relentless grief, anger and questions. HKFP looks back at images from the past year, as our photojournalist followed the major events and developments surrounding the aftermath of Hong Kong’s worst fire in decades. Following the fire, thousands of Hongkongers mobilised online and offline to support victims. The photo shows volunteers rallying to set up booths to provide free food, clothes and daily necessities near Wang Fuk court on November 27, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. People read supportive messages for the fire victims in a subway in Tai Po on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On December 5, 2025, thousands of people presented flowers and dolls to mourn those killed in the Wang Fuk Court fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A student sheds tears while mourning the deceased on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Taoist priests hold rituals for the deceased on December 1, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Following the fire, non-flame retardant scaffolding nets were identified on some buildings of Wang Fuk Court. They were later confirmed as one of the causes leading to the rapid spread of the blaze. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Soon after the fire, the Legislative Council held elections on December 7, 2025. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In late November, the Hong Kong Police Force orders volunteers to remove the makeshift supply stations at a podium of Kwong Fuk Estate. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On December 19, 2025, firefighters gathered and mourned Ho Wai Ho, firefighter who died in the line of duty during the Tai Po fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Following the tragedy, on January 16, 2026, Wang Fuk Court residents Jason Kong (first from left), Garrick Lee (middle) and Yip Ka-kui (first from right) recalled how residents made futile attempts to flag fire risks. They urged the government to investigate the causes of the fire. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On February 5, 2026, an independent committee held the first public meeting before starting hearings to probe the Tai Po fire. Judge David Lok (3rd left), chair of the committee, is seen walking out of the hearing. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Tony Tsui (centre right), the former chair of Wang Fuk Court owners’ corporation management committee, leaves after attending a public hearing to probe the Tai Po deadly fire on March 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Wang Fuk Court resident talks with the press after attending a public hearing on March 26, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On April 20, 2026, nearly half a year after the fire, Wang Fuk Court residents are allowed to return to their fire-ravaged homes to retrieve belongings. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wang Fuk Court residents return home to retrieve belongings on May 4, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A resident of Wang Fuk Court is seen in his fire-ravaged flat as he looks to retrieve personal belongings on April 23, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A Wang Fuk Court resident finds his wedding rings in his flat at Wang Fuk Court on April 20, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. On July 19, 2026, the administrator of the Wang Fuk Court housing estate hosted a special owners’ meeting at four different venues, after a months-long wait. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Jason Kong, a flat owner of Wang Fuk Court and a former member of the owners’ board, was arrested over alleged fraud in May 2026 and charged in August after he organised a petition for a homeowners’ meeting. The photo shows Kong leaving the Shatin Law Courts Buildings on September 1, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Nearly one year after the tragedy, Hong Kong leader John Lee leads top officials to bow in apology as he introduced reforms related to the Tai Po fire. The press conference was held on October 29, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Roman Catholic bishop Joseph Ha offers blessings to Wang Fuk Court residents during a mass at the Immaculate Heart of Mary Church on November 15, 2026. The church revised the theme of the mass from one dedicated to the fire victims to one for “remembering all who had passed away over the past year.” The change came after they reportedly faced police enquiries. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A fire-ravaged Wang Fuk Court flat is seen with banners stating “I love Wang Fuk” and “I want to move back” on the window. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. A community art exhibition by NGO Forget Thee Not in Central called “Life Goes On” on November 25, 2026. Several Wang Fuk Court residents participated in the show, expressing their feelings and experiences through text and photos. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. Wang Fuk Court on November 19, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP.

title: How China got access to Nvidia’s AI chips despite rules to stop them
zh_title: 尽管有规则阻止，中国如何获得英伟达的人工智能芯片
summary: 人工智能芯片是中美科技竞赛的核心战场。为了保持领先地位，华盛顿近年来制定并修改了规则，限制中国获得先进的半导体和芯片制造技术，同时平衡国家安全担忧与贸易考虑。围绕美国最大的人工智能芯片出口商英伟达（Nvidia）的戏剧性事件，使这些规则成为人们关注的焦点。深入研究由此产生的法规是一个泥潭。出口管制规则因其复杂性和不断修订而常被比作美国税法。以下是一些理解的基础知识
content:
人工智能芯片是中美科技竞赛的核心战场。为了保持领先地位，华盛顿近年来制定并修改了规则，限制中国获得先进的半导体和芯片制造技术，同时平衡国家安全担忧与贸易考虑。围绕美国最大的人工智能芯片出口商英伟达（Nvidia）的戏剧性事件，使这些规则成为人们关注的焦点。深入研究由此产生的法规是一个泥潭。出口管制规则因其复杂性和不断修订而常被比作美国税法。以下是一些了解中国获取美国人工智能芯片合法和不合法的一些基础知识： 美国什么时候开始限制向中国提供芯片？ 2022年10月，美国对中国推出先进芯片的全面限制，标志着美国对华技术出口政策出现数十年来最大转变。一年后，它收紧了规则，以获取更多芯片，并阻止英伟达等芯片设计商销售设计性能略低于早期限制的产品。它还将限制范围扩大到中东国家，并将芯片限制到总部位于中国的海外公司。 2025 年 1 月，拜登政府在全球范围内扩大了限制，在全球范围内实施了许可要求。但今年五月，即该规则生效前几天，特朗普政府宣布不会执行该规则。
特朗普政府上周才正式废除并取代了这一规定，留下了一个缺口，使得新加坡等国家的数据中心容量得以激增，中国企业可以在这些国家远程租用计算能力来训练和部署人工智能模型。新加坡云公司Megaspeed的前高管据称与英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋有染，其运营合法吗？必读 Nvidia 的黄仁勋被判无罪 两年多来，当局一直在调查 Megaspeed 是否将芯片转移到中国，这将是非法的。但包括新加坡在内的国家的公司可以无需许可为其数据中心购买先进的人工智能芯片，直到美国上周发布新规定禁止这种做法。 Megaspeed 可能不会再获得更多芯片了。该公司本周与其泰国和马来西亚子公司一起被列入美国贸易黑名单，基本上阻止了发货。英伟达还表示，将于2025年6月停止对Megaspeed的销售。英伟达向中国运送AI芯片是否合法？大约一年前，唐纳德·特朗普总统允许英伟达向中国出口其 H200 芯片，此举引起了专家的批评，他们表示这些芯片将有助于推动中国的军事现代化，并削弱美国在人工智能领域的领先地位。 H200 芯片是 Nvidia 更先进的芯片之一，但不是顶级的。英伟达不能简单地将芯片运送给支付费用的中国公司。
英伟达必须向美国商务部申请许可证，美国商务部自去年春天以来一直根据具体情况发放许可证。上周，众议院外交事务委员会公布的许可数据显示，特朗普政府批准从 2025 年 12 月到 2026 年 5 月向中国企业运送近 90 万颗英伟达和 AMD 生产的先进 AI 芯片。特朗普政府的新规定有何作用？上周，特朗普政府颁布了一项新规定，增加了对马来西亚、新加坡和泰国等五个国家的许可要求。

【原文 English Original】
AI chips are a central battleground in the US-China technology race. To preserve its lead, in recent years Washington has imposed and revised rules to restrict China’s access to advanced semiconductors and chipmaking technology, while balancing national security concerns with trade considerations. The drama around Nvidia, the top US exporter of AI chips to China, has thrust those rules into the spotlight. Delving into the resulting regulations is a quagmire. Export control rules are often likened to the US tax code in their complexity and constant revision. Here are some basics for understanding what’s legal, and what’s not, when it comes to China’s access to US AI chips: When did the US start to restrict chips to China? In October 2022, the US unveiled sweeping restrictions on advanced chips to China, marking the biggest shift in US policy toward exporting technology to China in decades. A year later, it tightened the rules to capture more chips and stop chip designers such as Nvidia from selling products engineered to fall just below the performance thresholds of the earlier restrictions. It also expanded the restrictions to countries in the Middle East and restricted chips to overseas companies headquartered in China. In January 2025, the Biden administration extended the restrictions globally, imposing a worldwide license requirement. But in May, days before it was set to take effect, the Trump administration announced it would not enforce that rule. The Trump administration only formally rescinded and replaced the rule last week, leaving a gap that allowed data center capacity to proliferate in countries such as Singapore, where Chinese companies could rent computing power remotely to train and deploy AI models. Did Megaspeed, the Singapore cloud company whose former executive allegedly had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , operate legally? Must Read At AI speed, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang finds exoneration For over two years, authorities have been investigating whether Megaspeed diverted chips to China, which would be illegal. But companies in countries including Singapore were allowed to buy advanced AI chips for their data centers license-free until the US issued a new rule last week cutting off that practice. Megaspeed likely won’t be getting any more chips. It was added to a US trade blacklist this week, along with its Thai and Malaysian subsidiaries, essentially blocking shipments. Nvidia also said it cut off sales to Megaspeed in June 2025. Are Nvidia’s shipments of AI chips to China legal? About a year ago, President Donald Trump allowed Nvidia to ship its H200 chip to China, drawing criticism from experts who said the chips would help jumpstart China’s military modernization and erode the US lead in AI. The H200 chip is one of Nvidia’s more advanced chips, but not top-of-the-line. Nvidia cannot simply ship the chips to Chinese companies that pay for them. Nvidia must apply for licenses from the US Department of Commerce, which has issued them since last spring on a case-by-case basis. Last week, the House foreign affairs committee released licensing data showing the Trump administration approved shipments of nearly 900,000 advanced AI chips made by Nvidia and AMD for Chinese companies from December 2025 through May 2026. What does the new Trump administration rule do? Last week, the Trump administration issued a new regulation, adding license requirements for five countries including Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, in an effort to crack down on chips being smuggled into China. Prior to that, the chip-based license requirement generally applied to countries like Russia that raise national security concerns, along with companies headquartered in arms-embargoed countries. Now they also apply to Southeast Asian countries viewed as transshipment points with a high risk for illegal diversion to China. The rule also clamped down on AI chip sales to non-US data centers that supply a high volume of computing power to Chinese-headquartered firms. How big a problem is chip smuggling? For years, Nvidia’s Huang has said there is no evidence of chip smuggling to China. But that assertion, which experts already viewed skeptically, was further questioned in March when US prosecutors charged three people associated with California-based AI server maker Super Micro Computer SMCI.O, including its co-founder, in a scheme to divert about $2.5 billion of US technology into China, including AI servers packed with Nvidia AI chips. Critics say Nvidia has tried to minimize a well-known risk. Huang once said Nvidia’s sophisticated Grace Blackwell AI chip platform weighed nearly 1.8 metric tons and could not fit into a pocket or backpack. But servers are not smuggled in backpacks. They are routed through third countries and intermediary companies. Supporters say Nvidia may not have had verified evidence of diversion and that the company cannot keep tabs on all its products after they’re sold. Can Nvidia track its chips to see where they end up? Nvidia has built location verification technology that could indicate which country its chips are operating in, the company confirmed in December 2025. It has offered the feature as a software option for customers. But the company has opposed proposed legislation that would require location verification and diversion reporting for advanced AI processors. A measure known as the Chip Security Act is among several export control bills that gained new momentum in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, and may be included in the National Defense Authorization Act that Congress is expected to pass next month. – Rappler.com

Fundraiser by Tarra Subhar Massallo : Immediate aid for families affected by the Nepal-Tibet Flood
This fund provides direct aid for shelter, food, and essentials to Nepal-Tibet families
Tarra Subhar Massallo is organizing this fundraiser.
After fleeing from the Chinese annexation of Tibet, many Kyirong Tibetan families crossed into Nepal believing their exile would be temporary. It was not. Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley had become their home instead- a place where hundreds of families had to rebuild from nothing, including my grandparents. Like many Tibetan refugees, they eventually moved on to build new lives in India. However, not everyone left. Some of their family stayed behind in Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley, carrying on the roots left behind by previous generations.
On August 26, 2026, a glacier collapse high in the Langtang Himal sent a wall of water and debris surging down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Bazaar: the towns where that branch of our family stayed and built their lives after losing everything once before. Four households in our family were directly affected:
Our cousin Dawa Dakpa (confirmed deceased) leaves behind a wife and two young children.
Aku Jangchup, his wife, and child (confirmed deceased)
Nama Nangsa Ghongma's family and relatives (missing)
Nama Karmo Subhar's family and relatives (missing)
Now, our families face rebuilding once again, with roads and homes submerged in mud. 100% of every contribution will go directly to these impacted families and the wider flood-affected communities as they recover together. The funds will be spent on various essentials based on each family's needs (including, but not limited to: temporary shelter, food, emergency medical care, and transportation costs). We invite you to help write the next chapter of this story. Please help support this fundraiser in any way that you can.
My name is Tarra Subhar Massallo. I am the granddaughter of Tibetan refugees who fled from Kyirong during the 1959 Chinese annexation of Tibet, and the daughter of a Tibetan immigrant mother who moved from India to the United States with her family in search of a better life. Growing up in a mixed household, I am surrounded by the importance of my many cultures and giving back to my respective communities.

content:
Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family
“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

content:
Fundraiser by Dominic Urso : Help Bhujung Rebuild After the Tibet-Nepal Flood
Bhujung’s fund covers urgent food, shelter, and essentials lost in the recent Syabru Besi flood
Dominic Urso is organizing this fundraiser.
Dominic and Kayla are raising funds for Bhujung Tamang, a friend they met while traveling in Nepal before/after the Langtang trek. During that trip, Dominic and Kayla stayed with Bhujung for a few days in his village of Syabru Besi. Bhujung welcomed them with kindness and gave them a truly special local experience they have never forgotten. Now, after a devastating flood destroyed Syabru Besi, Bhujung is facing an unimaginable loss. His home and hotel were destroyed, many of his friends were killed or are missing, and he lost all of his possessions in the disaster. It is estimated that Syabru Besi still has 1300 people missing.
Dominic and Kayla met Bhujung by chance while starting their 7 day hike up the Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's premier hiking destinations. They were looking for a place to stay and found the only hotel in the Old Village of Syabru Besi. Upon getting to know Bhujung, Dominic and Kayla discovered that they were the first guests Bhujung had had in almost 3 years because he was taking care of his late mother's declining health. As a token of gratitude and friendship, Bhujung gifted Dominic and Kayla a hand stitched bag his mother made pictured above.
This fundraiser is meant to provide direct relief to Bhujung as he begins the long process of recovering and rebuilding after this tragedy. The money raised will go directly to him to help support his immediate needs (food, housing, etc.) and give him a foundation to move forward after losing so much. Dominic and Kayla are asking for donations of any amount to help Bhujung through this heartbreaking time. If you are able to give, thank you for showing compassion and support to someone who once showed such generosity to travelers far from home. Please consider donating and sharing this fundraiser to help Bhujung rebuild his life.

Fundraiser by Kurshat Uyghur : Support Uyghur film & tell the story together
Kurshat Uyghur is organizing this fundraiser.
We've been making preparation for this film for nearly a year. It is a story of a young Uyghur man’s life in exile after losing contact with his family members. We have received funding from a few organizations, but not quite enough for the entire production process. So we decided to ask for help from those of you who care about the Uyghurs and the work that we’re doing. Our goal is to reach $10,000.
If you have any interest in Uyghur culture or the Uyghur film industry, then please consider a contribution. Your small act of kindness will greatly enhance this film, you will not be disappointed. This film will open your eyes to stories from a beautiful and marginalized people group
The film will be released on March 21st, 2023. All donors will be listed in the end credits and receive a steamable/ download link to the film, and donors who give $100 or more contributions will receive special thanks and additional gifts as shown below:
$100 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film and a handwritten thank you letter.
$200 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter.
$500 donation - you will receive a physical copy of the film, a poster with the director’s signature and a handwritten thank you letter also your name will be present on the director's special thanks section ending of the film.
$5000 donation - you will receive all of the above and will be credited as a co-producer.
Shirzat, an Uyghur international student who has just graduated from college in the United States, had big dreams for his future prior to undertaking his education. He had planned to return to his homeland to take over his father's business, marry his long-term girlfriend, build a happy family, and become a successful entrepreneur. But with the sudden implementation of China's arbitrary mass abduction policy, millions of Uyghurs, like his father, were taken and have disappeared. For Shirzat, who wasn’t able to pursue his studies due to the crisis back home, this was tragic. He felt he had been thrown from the sky to the ground. With finances in ruins, his father missing, his family in danger, his relationship hanging by a thread, he soon spiraled into a cloud of depression and compulsive attention to politics. He withdrew from his relationships with his friends and put his life on hold while struggling to overcome his painful reality and searching for hope in the midst of it.
We will work with some of the most talented people around the world. The Director and screenwriter of this film have decades of experience in the industry. He has also made a number of short films while in university, many of which won the best picture of the year at regional and international film festivals. Our core team members are creative-minded people who have participated in numerous film projects. We have absolute confidence that we will work together as one and give the audiences astonishing results.

summary: Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser. The Contemporary Uyghur An
content:
Fundraiser by Uyghur Anthology : Support the Contemporary Uyghur Anthology
This anthology funds Uyghur writers and artists, translation, events, and community growth
Uyghur Anthology is organizing this fundraiser.
The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a publication that platforms Uyghur (and anyone drawing their roots from East Turkistan) artists and writers in the diaspora by providing a space that is often inaccessible to those in our community. There are no other projects of its kind in the English language, and with two volumes already published, we hope to take this project to the next level. It's a rare look at Uyghur expression in an environment where all our stories are told by people pushing their own narratives without the intimate knowledge of our lived experiences.
<"Manifesto" by Sumayah Jurad from Vol. II>
We asked ourselves these questions - why wait for others to invite us to the table when we can pull up a chair and introduce ourselves? Why let others speak for us without trying first to speak? Our broken English can only be improved with audacity, and world literature is only enriched by the presence of new voices.
All-in-all, our efforts have been met with support from our community and pleasant surprise from those who did not know what they did not know.
Somewhat unprecedented is that we publish the authors' original language alongside the translation. Our book is filled with Uyghur, Latin, Cyrillic, and Chinese script to encapsulate as much of our community's experience as we can.
There are many publications in diaspora communities that platform East and South Asians, SEA, MENA, and more. Central Asia is often underrepresented in world literature or Asia-specific publications, and occupied territories even less so. Uyghurs themselves have been a relatively new diaspora community in English-speaking countries, and haven't had the opportunities to grow their literary or artistic communities. Many don't have the tools to nurture their talents, or knowledge of creative networks or opportunities, even when many journals seek work from underrepresented groups. In instances where they are aware, it's difficult to be published in this competitive field without the education and styles that publications look for. There are only a handful of literary translators translating from Uyghur to English, and not many Uyghurs who have had the chances to develop their creative language when learning English.
To sum up, the issues were:
No spaces for Uyghur writers and artists to develop their skills
A disconnect from artist communities, be it local or online
No bridge between our native tongue and English, and in turn, world literature
So, we put together a small group at the Tarim Network to take on this challenge. Completely volunteer-run; the very essence of a passion project. We did a call-out for anything and all. New writers, established writers, any language, any genre, whatever we could print in a book. And here we were, the first book of its kind, created to speak for ourselves without outsider voices, without a publishing house, raw and straight from the source.
<From the launch of Vol. I at Harvard University>
"The Contemporary Uyghur Anthology is a collection of Uyghur reflections in diaspora. Weaving together memories of the homeland, experiences of displacement, and transitions of identities, this anthology is a creative reflection of the beauty and complexities of the Uyghur experience.
By centering Uyghur voices at the forefront, this anthology serves as a form of living memory in a pivotal moment of Uyghur history. The title Under the Mulberry Tree refers to a story from the Uyghur literary classic Ana Yurt, where youthful Nuri faces terrible injustices, separation, and turmoil; but for one moment in the Charbagh, his love for Sebihe and his own family is full, ripe, and sweet, like the mulberries from the ancient tree. In a similar way that the mulberry tree offered comforts in Nuri’s time of need, we hope this volume offers a place of reflection and celebration of Uyghur culture."
We'd partnered with a member from a Jewish organisation to run writing workshops and explain editorial processes, as we had never worked on something like this before. After that collaboration, we decided to publish a revised edition on our own. This time, we added editors' notes to the pages to explain certain terms and historical and cultural contexts - mainly for our own youth, who don't always have access to cultural education. We translated more pieces from Uyghur and Chinese. Our contributors spanned 13 countries, at all levels of experience.
Was this work sustainable? Equipped with the tools, experience, and outpouring of support from our first volume, we spent the next two years saying yes. Our first book was now in libraries, there were articles and academic papers that mentioned it, and most of all, we reaffirmed the need for this sort of work. Not only were we accepting submissions, we worked one-on-one with emerging writers and artists to edit their pieces. We also helped first-time translators have their first publications with help from more experienced translators, as well as connecting them with the original authors.
Our second volume was even better than the last. From the blurb:
"How do we respond to the unexpected, and how does it influence perceptions of ourselves or the environments in which we exist? As a diaspora population, unexpected encounters can shape and transform what it means to be Uyghur as we build a new life outside of the homeland. Encounters Under the Mulberry Tree takes on the literal, abstract, and expanded renditions of these moments. We feature contemporary and historical works, including art, poetry, and prose in five languages with contributors based in a dozen countries, from established writers like award-winning author and filmmaker Tahir Hamut Izgil, to emerging artists, writers and translators of all ages. This book is a library of vignettes that grapple with intersections and how we make sense of it all."
Five languages (Uyghur, English, Chinese, Russian, Turkish)
<Vol. II showcased at a college hosted by Rawan Mentorship>
Now we embark on our third volume. The three of us do this while maintaining full time jobs, academic careers, and other side projects. We all live in different countries and have only met in person once. But it's something that we need to do, for our community and for ourselves. Our contributors have gained so much from this experience and we want to extend this opportunity to more people. This needs to survive in order for similar initiatives to be born.
Supporting the editors - all expenses so far have been paid out-of-pocket or through book sales. We do not have any donors or sponsors (yet!).
Supporting our contributors - we cannot afford to pay any of our contributors. Despite this, we have given free copies of the book to contributors, but this is definitely leaving a dent in our pockets.
Recruiting more people - paid internships or remuneration for one-off work would help volunteers spend more time on this project in this economy.
Enhance our level of expertise - we want to improve. Workshops or courses for our editors and contributors, professional feedback, the works. Unfortunately there is no one who speaks Uyghur and who is involved in Western publishing or English literature on a professional or academic level. We would appreciate connections with professionals from any language background, or the funding to level up.
Expand our network - we'd love to promote our work at literary festivals, go to conferences, do book events, establish ourselves in the public eye, provide reader copies to reviewers, and so on. However, there is a funding barrier to overcome to be able to attend these events, organise, or pre-order books.
<Vol. I on display at the Mosquers Film Festival, 2025>
Munawwar Abdulla is an Uyghur advocate, poet, and scientist born on unceded Kaurna land (Australia) and based in Massachusetts. She co-founded The Tarim Network, runs Uyghur Collective, and collaborates on projects with Uyghur rights organisations around the world. Her writings and literary translations have been published in places such as Modern Poetry in Translation, Asymptote, the Margins, the Georgia Review, and others.
Sonya Imin is a mixed Uyghur American scholar and multi-disciplinary creative who has worked on art and film projects across the US, Europe, and Central Asia. Growing up between the borderlands of the Uyghur homeland, broader Central Asia, and the midwestern United States, interrogations of belonging, home, and displacement influence the nature of her work. Currently based in Brussels, she is working on her doctoral research on Uyghur artistic production in the diaspora.
Maidina Kadeer is a mixed Uyghur-Hui writer and editor, born in Ghulja and currently based in Montreal (Tiohtià:ke), Canada. She holds a BA in English Literature and Law and Society from Concordia University, with a focus on post- and neo-colonial literature. Her work explores Uyghur identity, history, and culture through cuisine, agriculture, and neo-colonialism. She has contributed to projects such as a poem, NinetySix, in Slavs and Tatars’ Contest of the Fruits (2021) and participates in panels and interviews on Agriculture and Food History to raise awareness about Uyghur culture.

Nurnisa Kurban for Uyghur Academic Foundation
Uyghur Cultural Preservation and Survival Through Education
The Uyghur people have been persecuted and subjected to repressive Chinese government policies in their Indigenous homeland of East Turkestan for many years. It is estimated that up to three million Uyghurs have been interned, imprisoned, and enslaved in detention centers, prisons, and forced labor facilities throughout China since 2017.
In 2021, the Uyghur Tribunal found that China was committing genocide and other crimes against humanity against Uyghurs. In 2022, the United Nations also concluded that China was committing human rights violations against Uyghurs amounting to crimes against humanity. Countries including the United States, Canada, the Netherlands, Czech Republic, United Kingdom, Lithuania, Belgium, and France have all declared a genocide in East Turkestan. Despite these declarations of genocide and related reports by various human rights organizations, atrocities against Uyghurs continue today with very limited international recognition and accountability.
During this time of ongoing genocide and cultural erasure in their Indigenous homeland, Uyghurs of the diaspora are working to preserve their culture and identity as a matter of survival. Uyghur education has been eradicated by the Chinese State, Uyghur texts are forbidden and in danger of being eliminated, and the Uyghur language itself is prohibited.
Uyghur scholars, linguists, and other specialists in the diaspora worldwide serve on the Uyghur Language and Education Committee of the Uyghur Academy to preserve the work of Uyghur intellectuals who have been persecuted and forcibly disappeared. This work has been ongoing since 2009 and is continuing to expand.
The Committee has created standards-aligned K-5 textbooks, which include classic and contemperory Uyghur literature, poetry, historical texts, and biographies for Uyghur children to learn about their own culture and identity in their native language. The Committee is seeking funding to expand and revise the existing K-5 textbooks, create teacher’s edition textbooks for educators, and design supplemental resources. They also hope to develop Middle and High School textbooks and related supplemental resources. To effectively implement these educational materials, they would also like to provide training for teachers.
Please consider supporting this urgent work of the Uyghur Academic Foundation as a matter of cultural survival for future generations of the Uyghur people.

content:
Fundraiser for Silkroad Uyghur by Sarah Elder : Help our local Uyghur restaurant!
Sarah Elder is organizing this fundraiser on behalf of Silkroad Uyghur.
In 2018, Gairatjan Rozi, a talented Uyghur chef, trained in Europe and now settled in America, opened 'Marco & Polo' in Hyattsville. The restaurant's menu features the cuisine of his homeland, in the Uyghur Autonomous Region of China, with classic Uyghur dishes including hand-pulled laghman noodles, dumplings, and lamb kebabs, complemented by more familiar Turkish and Mediterranean fare.
Within just a few years, Mr. Rozi and his restaurant has earned the love of our community. His food & restaurant has been featured in the local press and has earned a dedicated following in the Washington DC region.
Unfortunately the COVID-19 pandemic is forcing Mr. Rozi to close his family-run kitchen, shutter his beloved restaurant, and put in storage his colorful collection of Uyghur artifacts which decorate 'Marco & Polo.'
But Mr. Rozi is hopeful. Having dedicated his new life in America to 'Marco & Polo,' he dreams of reopening his restaurant soon - in a new location that will attract even more customers who want to enjoy & explore both the cuisine and the Uyghur culture of Central Asia.
Your generous donation to this GoFundMe effort will help Mr. Rozi begin to recover finically from the COVID-19 disaster and allow him to pursue his dream of creating another unique Uyghur dining experience for our community! Rehmet! (Uyghur for 'thank you')

content:
Fundraiser by Aydin Anwar : Uyghur Students in Egypt
Aydin Anwar is organizing this fundraiser.
Help save Muslim Uyghur students in Egypt from deportation to China, where they will face detention, persecution, torture, lengthy prison sentences, and perhaps even death.
Hundreds of Muslim Uyghur students in Egypt with resident permits are currently being rounded up to be deported to China, where they will be subject to persecution, imprisonment, torture, and death sentences. Their crime? Being Uyghur and studying Islam. #SaveUyghurStudents
In its attempt to "crackdown on Islamic extremism", China has significantly tightened its security measures and prohibition of religious practice in East Turkestan (aka Xinjiang, occupied by China). Chinese authorities are now seeking the return of thousands of innocent Uyghur students abroad in "wide sweeps" to extend this crackdown.
It has been reported that all airports in Egypts are preventing Uyghurs from leaving the country. Some Uyghur students have already been deported, and the remaining are either in detention awaiting deportation or in hiding within Egypt’s borders. Several that we know managed to escape to Turkey, but are currently homeless or in extreme financial hardship.
Therefore the funds we collect will go to providing shelter, food and other support to the Uyghurs who have already managed to flee Egypt. It will also go to provide those in hiding with necessities (e.g. food, room, board) while we work with nonprofit human rights organizations to pressure Egypt and China to stop the deportations and detentions.
The funds will be collected through Uyghur Youth Campaign, a 501(c) nonprofit based in the US, and will (for now) be directly delivered to the Uyghur students who fled to Turkey by one of its members, Aydin Anwar, who has been in Istanbul. She is connected with these refugees through Munevver Ozuygur, an Uyghur activist based in Zeytinburnu, Istanbul.
Please donate and help spread awareness. Do not remain silent as these young men and women are sent off to be detained, tortured, imprisoned and perhaps even killed in China. They need our help.
